====Specific communities====
[[Romesh Ranganathan]], [[Meera Syal]], [[Adil Ray]], [[Sadiq Khan]] and others produced a video specifically encouraging ethnic minority communities in the UK to be vaccinated including addressing conspiracy theories stating "there is no scientific evidence to suggest it will work differently on people from ethnic minorities and that it does not include pork or any material of fetal or animal origin."<ref>{{cite web |title=COVID-19 vaccine: Stars bust myths in video urging people from ethnic minority communities to get the jab |url=https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-vaccine-stars-bust-myths-in-video-urging-people-from-ethnic-minority-communities-to-get-the-jab-12199469 |access-date=31 March 2021 |website=Sky News |archive-date=25 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425174547/https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-vaccine-stars-bust-myths-in-video-urging-people-from-ethnic-minority-communities-to-get-the-jab-12199469 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Oprah Winfrey]] and [[Whoopi Goldberg]] have spoken about being vaccinated and encouraged other [[black American]]s to be so.<ref name="People" /> [[Stephanie Elam]] volunteered to be a trial volunteer stating "a large part of the reason why I wanted to volunteer for this COVID-19 vaccine research{{snd}}more Black people and more people of color need to be part of these trials so more diverse populations can reap the benefits of this medical research."<ref name="People" />

=== Experiences of prior hesitant individuals and others ===
Many news articles, TV interviews and posts on social media appeared in 2021 to highlight either the anger of individuals whose children or immune compromised family members either caught COVID-19 or were vaccine hesitant and later tested positive. The Chief Medical Officer for England, [[Chris Whitty|Prof. Chris Whitty]], tweeted in September 2021 that "The majority of our hospitalised Covid patients are unvaccinated and regret delaying their vaccines" with about 60% of all hospitalisations due to COVID-19 in the UK being of unvaccinated individuals.<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Kale S  |date=14 September 2021 |title='The virus is painfully real': vaccine hesitant people are dying – and their loved ones want the world to listen |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/14/the-virus-is-painfully-real-vaccine-hesitant-people-are-dying-and-their-loved-ones-want-the-world-to-listen |url-status=live |access-date=30 September 2021 |website=The Guardian |archive-date=30 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210930142806/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/14/the-virus-is-painfully-real-vaccine-hesitant-people-are-dying-and-their-loved-ones-want-the-world-to-listen}}</ref> While some cases have allowed for more discussions to open up about the vaccine and the effects of the disease, some still have remaining hesitancy about the vaccination process,<ref>{{Cite news | vauthors = Varney S |date=2021-09-03 |title=This Teen's Community Rallied as She Fought COVID. But Many Still Shun the Vaccine |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/09/03/1032665979/child-near-death-covid-vaccine-hesitancy-mis-c |access-date=2021-09-30 |archive-date=30 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210930155722/https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/09/03/1032665979/child-near-death-covid-vaccine-hesitancy-mis-c |url-status=live |language=en |department=Shots |publisher=[[NPR]] }}</ref> others have expressed their regret for not pushing the vaccine or determination to get vaccinated.<ref>{{Cite magazine | vauthors = Dellenger R |date=12 September 2021 |title=I Didn't Want to Push My Aunt to Get the Vaccine. Now I Live With Regrets |url=https://time.com/6096505/covid-19-vaccine-hesitancy-family/ |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-30 |magazine=Time |language=en |archive-date=30 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210930142806/https://time.com/6096505/covid-19-vaccine-hesitancy-family/}}</ref>

=== Targeted lockdowns and fines ===
Austria and Germany both announced in late 2021 that they would introduce lockdowns for only unvaccinated citizens.<ref name="Mackintosh_2021" /> These targeted lockdowns faced criticism from various quarters, including from the far-right [[Freedom Party of Austria|Freedom Party]] which labeled the measures as creating a group of second-class citizens. Additionally, thousands protested in [[Vienna]] against the vaccine mandate, expressing concerns over personal freedoms and governmental overreach.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-11-14 |title=Covid: Austria introduces lockdown for unvaccinated |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59283128 |access-date=2025-04-06 |language=en-GB}}</ref> In Greece, those who refused to get vaccinated and were above the age of 60 were fined 100 euros a month, with the payments put towards a hospital service fund. In Singapore, all citizens who chose not to get vaccinated were required to pay their medical bills in full if they tested positive and receive hospital care, while in Ukraine all teachers and government officials who remain unvaccinated were placed on unpaid leave, and restaurants, shopping malls and fitness centers must have 100% of their employees vaccinated to operate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 December 2021 |title=These Countries Are Slapping the Unvaccinated With Fines and Bans |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-01/these-countries-are-slapping-the-unvaccinated-with-fines-bans|access-date=2021-12-28 |website=www.bloomberg.com}}</ref>

=== Vaccine lotteries and benefits ===
[[Moscow Kremlin|The Kremlin]] announced in 2021 that it was supporting a lottery that would give 1,000 chosen vaccinated individuals the equivalent of $1,350. The [[Mayor of Moscow]] also announced that the city would give away five cars every week to vaccinated residents.<ref name="Burakovsky-2021" /> In the United States, many states such as Alaska,<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Early W |date=2021-09-17 |title=Here are the first 2 winners of the state's $49K COVID vaccine sweepstakes |url=https://www.alaskapublic.org/2021/09/16/first-two-winners-of-the-states-covid-19-vaccine-sweepstakes-announced/ |access-date=2021-09-20 |website=Alaska Public Media |language=en-US |archive-date=20 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920212434/https://www.alaskapublic.org/2021/09/16/first-two-winners-of-the-states-covid-19-vaccine-sweepstakes-announced/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Pennsylvania,<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Yu A |date=25 August 2021 |title=The results of Philadelphia's COVID-19 vaccine lottery? 'Discouraging' |url=https://whyy.org/articles/the-results-of-philadelphias-covid-19-vaccine-lottery-discouraging/ |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-20 |website=WHYY |language=en-US |archive-date=20 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920212057/https://whyy.org/articles/the-results-of-philadelphias-covid-19-vaccine-lottery-discouraging/}}</ref> and Ohio,<ref>{{Cite news | vauthors = Vigdor N, Paybarah A |date=2021-05-12 |title=Ohio Lottery to Give 5 People $1 Million Each to Encourage Vaccination |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/12/us/ohio-lottery-coronavirus-vaccine.html |access-date=2021-09-20 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> along with cities and universities, offered scholarships, money, and physical items in lotteries. These benefits had varying success in raising vaccination numbers. In July 2021, the Polish government launched the National Vaccination Programme Lottery to encourage vaccinations against COVID-19. It was open to people aged 18 years and over who had completed the COVID-19 vaccination programme and had registered for the lottery by 30 September 2020. The final prize draw took place on 6 October 2021, and there were two cash prizes of PLN 1 million (US$264,000) and two Toyota C-HR cars to be won.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Poland launches lottery to promote Covid-19 vaccinations |url=https://www.pap.pl/en/news/news%2C902316%2Cpoland-launches-lottery-promote-covid-19-vaccinations.html |access-date=2021-12-02 |website=Polska Agencja Prasowa SA |language=en}}</ref>

First Capital Bank, based out of Malawi, issued a statement that they would only give the annual performance bonuses to vaccinated employees.<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Karombo T |title=Africa's largest telecom operator mandates vaccines for employees |url=https://qz.com/africa/2100119/mtn-employees-who-refuse-vaccination-will-be-fired/ |access-date=2021-12-28 |website=Quartz |date=8 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Vaccine mandates ===
{{See also|COVID-19 vaccination mandates in the United States}}

In France, since September 2021, all health care workers must have received at least one dose of the vaccine to continue working with any resisters suspended without pay. Additional worker groups that have been mandated to do so earlier in the year are military members and firefighters.<ref name="WLFI News" /> In November 2021, Austria announced that it would introduce a nationwide vaccine mandate.<ref name="Mackintosh_2021" />

In the United States, many businesses,<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Schaffler R |date=3 August 2021 |title=Mandating COVID-19 vaccines for workers? Employers weigh their options {{!}} Video |url=https://www.njspotlight.com/video/mandating-covid-19-vaccines-for-workers-employers-weigh-their-options/ |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=NJ Spotlight News |language=en-US |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163124/https://www.njspotlight.com/video/mandating-covid-19-vaccines-for-workers-employers-weigh-their-options/}}</ref> schools<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Dukes D |date=2021-09-14 |title=Decatur schools mandate COVID-19 vaccines for staff, no decision yet for students |url=https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/decatur-schools-to-weigh-covid-19-vaccine-mandate-for-staff-students |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=FOX 5 Atlanta |language=en-US |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163123/https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/decatur-schools-to-weigh-covid-19-vaccine-mandate-for-staff-students |url-status=live}}</ref> and universities,<ref name="Snyder-2021">{{Cite web | vauthors = Snyder S |date=28 June 2021 |title=The vaccination debate on college campuses: A mandate or not? And for whom? |url=https://www.inquirer.com/news/vaccination-debate-college-campuses-mandate-or-not-who-20210628.html |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=The Philadelphia Inquirer |language=en |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163122/https://www.inquirer.com/news/vaccination-debate-college-campuses-mandate-or-not-who-20210628.html}}</ref> healthcare providers,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-14 |title=AlohaCare Implements COVID-19 Vaccine Mandate for Employees |url=https://www.khon2.com/local-news/alohacare-implements-covid-19-vaccine-mandate-for-employees/ |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=KHON2 |language=en-US |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163124/https://www.khon2.com/local-news/alohacare-implements-covid-19-vaccine-mandate-for-employees/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and governmental and state departments have enacted vaccine mandates.<ref name="Liptak-2021">{{Cite web | vauthors = Liptak K, Collins K |date=9 September 2021 |title=Biden announces new vaccine mandates that could cover 100 million Americans |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/09/09/politics/joe-biden-covid-speech/index.html |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=CNN |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163440/https://www.cnn.com/2021/09/09/politics/joe-biden-covid-speech/index.html}}</ref> While many of the mandates allowed for a person to opt out due to medical or religious reasons and be regularly tested, the federal mandate signed in September 2021 did not include these options.<ref name="Liptak-2021" /> The federal mandate was eventually [[National Federation of Independent Business v. Occupational Safety and Health Administration|struck down]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Kendall |first1=Brent |last2=Bravin |first2=Jess |date=2022-01-13 |title=Supreme Court Blocks Biden Vaccine Rules for Large Employers |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/supreme-court-blocks-biden-vaccine-rules-for-private-employers-allows-them-for-healthcare-workers-11642103130 |access-date=2025-04-06 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Some of the mandates were focused only on specific groups, such as [[Rutgers University]], which only mandated the vaccine for students and health-care and public-safety employees.<ref name="Snyder-2021" /> The mandates have seen push back with a New York Judge temporarily blocking one for healthcare workers who claimed they could not opt out due to religious reasons,<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Wiessner D |date=2021-09-14 |title=U.S. judge blocks N.Y. vaccine mandate for healthcare workers |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-judge-blocks-ny-vaccine-mandate-healthcare-workers-2021-09-14/ |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=Reuters |language=en |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163122/https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-judge-blocks-ny-vaccine-mandate-healthcare-workers-2021-09-14/}}</ref> and [[Arizona]] Attorney General [[Mark Brnovich]] suing the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] for its vaccine mandate for federal employees and private businesses with over 100 employees.<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Shaw A |date=2021-09-14 |title=Arizona sues Biden administration over COVID-19 vaccine mandate |url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/arizona-sues-biden-administration-covid-19-vaccine-mandate |access-date=2021-09-15 |publisher=Fox News |language=en-US |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163123/https://www.foxnews.com/politics/arizona-sues-biden-administration-covid-19-vaccine-mandate |url-status=live}}</ref> Additional push back on vaccine mandates were seen at local levels with at least one sheriff's department in California announcing they would not enforce any vaccine mandates as "the last line of defense from tyrannical government overreach",<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Smith H |date=2021-09-14 |title=Riverside County sheriff says he will not enforce COVID-19 vaccine mandates |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-09-14/riverside-county-sheriff-wont-enforce-covid-vaccine-mandates |url-status=live |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US |archive-date=15 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915163123/https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-09-14/riverside-county-sheriff-wont-enforce-covid-vaccine-mandates}}</ref> while others have seen mass resignation.<ref>{{Cite web | vauthors = Joseph E |title=NY hospital pausing delivering babies after Covid-19 resignations |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/09/12/health/ny-hospital-pausing-baby-deliveries-covid-19-resignations/index.html |access-date=2021-09-15 |publisher=CNN |date=12 September 2021 |archive-date=15 WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Children in the Gaza war

{{Short description|none}}
{{protection padlock|small=yes}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2025}}
[[File:Boys salvaging a destroyed building in the Gaza Strip.jpg|thumb|Boys salvaging a destroyed building in the Gaza Strip]]
The [[Gaza war]] has disproportionately affected children, who make up about 40% of the population of the [[Gaza Strip]].<ref>{{bulleted list|{{#invoke:cite|web |title=Israel-Hamas war has disproportionate impact on women and children in Gaza |url=https://www.wbur.org/hereandnow/2024/01/26/women-children-gaza |website=WBUR |date=26 January 2024 |access-date=4 February 2024 |archive-date=4 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240204162105/https://www.wbur.org/hereandnow/2024/01/26/women-children-gaza |url-status=live}}|{{#invoke:cite|news |last1=Kekatos |first1=Mary |date=7 November 2023 |title=Why women, children are disproportionately impacted by the conflict in Gaza: Experts |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/women-children-disproportionately-impacted-conflict-gaza-experts/story?id=104655493 |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |access-date=19 November 2023 |archive-date=18 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231118152736/https://abcnews.go.com/International/women-children-disproportionately-impacted-conflict-gaza-experts/story?id=104655493 |url-status=live |ref=none}}|{{#invoke:cite|web |title=Women and newborns bearing the brunt of the conflict in Gaza, UN agencies warn |url=https://www.who.int/news/item/03-11-2023-women-and-newborns-bearing-the-brunt-of-the-conflict-in-gaza-un-agencies-warn |website=[[World Health Organization]] |access-date=4 February 2024 |archive-date=7 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240207165942/https://www.who.int/news/item/03-11-2023-women-and-newborns-bearing-the-brunt-of-the-conflict-in-gaza-un-agencies-warn |url-status=live}}}}</ref> In November 2023, [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|UN Secretary General]] [[António Guterres]] warned that "Gaza is becoming a graveyard for children. Hundreds of girls and boys are reportedly being killed or injured every day."<ref>{{#invoke:Cite|news |last=Wintour |first=Patrick |author-link=Patrick Wintour |date=6 November 2023 |title=Gaza becoming 'a graveyard for children', says UN secretary general |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/06/gaza-becoming-a-graveyard-for-children-says-un-secretary-general |archive-url=https://archive.today/20231106224638/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/06/gaza-becoming-a-graveyard-for-children-says-un-secretary-general |archive-date=6 November 2023 |access-date=25 February 2024 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> As the war continued, the toll increased steadily, reaching at least 19,424 children by 3 September 2025.<ref name="hums42">{{#invoke:cite|web | title=Humanitarian Situation Report No. 42 | url=https://www.unicef.org/media/174306/file/SOP-Humanitarian-SitRep-31-August-2025.pdf.pdf | access-date=2025-10-12}}</ref>

Within the first month of the war, about 700,000 children in Gaza had been [[Forced displacement|displaced]].<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web |title=In Gaza, more than 700,000 children have been displaced - forced to leave everything behind. |url=https://twitter.com/UNICEF/status/1724155268148191524?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1724155268148191524%7Ctwgr%5E78a7cd78ba86ee0532e86d8148dc1907f48297a9%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.aljazeera.com%2Fnews%2Fliveblog%2F2023%2F11%2F13%2Fisrael-hamas-war-live-gazas-two-largest-hospitals-shut-amid-nonstop-raids |access-date=13 November 2023 |website=X post by UNICEF |publisher=[[UNICEF]]}}</ref><ref>{{#invoke:cite|news |title=PRCS tries to 'alleviate suffering of displaced children' |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/12/israel-gaza-war-live-israeli-army-surrounding-al-quds-hospital?update=2480667 |work=[[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]] |access-date=12 November 2023 |archive-date=16 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231216015928/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/12/israel-gaza-war-live-israeli-army-surrounding-al-quds-hospital?update=2480667 |url-status=live}}</ref> A May 2025 estimate reports that 1.9 million people, roughly 90% of Gaza's population, had been displaced by the war. Many had been uprooted repeatedly, in some cases more than ten times.<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web | title=UNRWA Situation Report #172 on the Humanitarian Crisis in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem | website=UNRWA | date=2025-05-23 | url=https://www.unrwa.org/resources/reports/unrwa-situation-report-172-situation-gaza-strip-and-west-bank-including-east-jerusalem| access-date=2025-10-13}}</ref> The collapse of essential services created a [[Gaza humanitarian crisis|humanitarian crisis]], as families struggled to access food, clean water, and medical care. The ongoing crisis also impacted routine vaccinations, leaving thousands of children at risk of preventable disease. Additional hardships included inadequate shelter, a lack of adequate winter clothing, and the continuing psychological toll on children's mental health.<ref name="france24live20231213" /><ref>{{bulletedlist|{{#invoke:cite|news |title=Gaza families live in tents with no winter clothing |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-middle-east-67548831 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=10 February 2024 |archive-date=26 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231226034438/https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-middle-east-67548831 |url-status=live}}|{{#invoke:cite|news |title=UN: Gaza is World's Most Dangerous Place for Children |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/un-gaza-is-world-s-most-dangerous-place-for-children-/7404592.html |work=[[Voice of America]] |date=19 December 2023 |access-date=10 February 2024 |archive-date=14 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240114080158/https://www.voanews.com/a/un-gaza-is-world-s-most-dangerous-place-for-children-/7404592.html |url-status=live}}|{{#invoke:cite|news |title=Disease could kill more in Gaza than bombs, WHO says amid Israeli siege |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/28/disease-could-kill-more-in-gaza-than-bombs-who-says-amid-israeli-siege |work=[[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]] |access-date=4 February 2024 |archive-date=4 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240204162105/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/28/disease-could-kill-more-in-gaza-than-bombs-who-says-amid-israeli-siege |url-status=live}}}}</ref>

As a result of the war, many children had sustained amputations and other permanent disabilities, as well as psychological trauma. Thousands more suffered from dehydration, malnutrition, diseases linked to the lack of clean water such as [[gastroenteritis]], and respiratory diseases.

In January 2024, two months into the war, the UNICEF deputy director described the situation of children in Gaza as the "most horrific" he had ever seen.<ref name="unicef.org">{{#invoke:cite|web |title=Statement by UNICEF Deputy Executive Director Ted Chaiban upon conclusion of his visit to the Gaza Strip |url=https://www.unicef.org/eap/press-releases/statement-unicef-deputy-executive-director-ted-chaiban-upon-conclusion-his-visit |website=[[UNICEF]] |access-date=20 January 2024 |archive-date=24 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124181112/https://www.unicef.org/eap/press-releases/statement-unicef-deputy-executive-director-ted-chaiban-upon-conclusion-his-visit |url-status=live}}</ref>{{efn|He also called for immediate and "unconditional" release of [[Gaza war hostage crisis|Israeli children who were being held hostage by Hamas]].}} By August 2025, humanitarian conditions for children were reported to have reached an unprecedented level of severity, affecting every aspect of their rights and well-being. Nutritional conditions had become catastrophic, with an officially confirmed famine in three of Gaza's five governorates.<ref name="hums42" /> A June 2026 UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry report found that Israel had killed approximately 20,000 children and injured 44,000 more since 7 October 2023. The report documented cases of children being killed by single, precise gunshots from snipers and drones, which it said indicated deliberate targeting rather than incidental harm.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-23 |title=Israel continues to commit genocide, atrocity crimes by deliberately targeting Palestinian children, UN independent commission finds |url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/06/1167790 |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=UN News |language=en}}</ref>

== Health ==
{{See also|Timeline of the Gaza Strip healthcare collapse|Healthcare in Palestine}}
[[File:Dead infant in Kamal Adwan Hospital 28 june 2024.jpg|thumb|A dead infant in Kamal Adwan Hospital on 28 June 2024 as a result of the humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip]]
Since 2007, [[Blockade of the Gaza Strip|Israel had implemented a strict land and sea blockade]] that had prevented items such as food and medicine from moving into the Gaza Strip, with the health system struggling before the war.<ref name="npr20231019">{{Cite news |last=Mohammad |first=Linah |date=19 October 2023 |title=Children make up nearly half of Gaza's population. Here's what it means for the war |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/10/19/1206479861/israel-gaza-hamas-children-population-war-palestinians |access-date=5 February 2024 |work=[[NPR]] |archive-date=9 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240209080904/https://www.npr.org/2023/10/19/1206479861/israel-gaza-hamas-children-population-war-palestinians |url-status=live}}</ref>

Ahmed al-Fara, the head of pediatrics at [[Nasser Hospital|Nasser Medical Complex]] in [[Khan Younis]], stated due to the lack of water during the war, he was witnessing the "most serious epidemic of [[gastroenteritis]]" among children he had ever seen.<ref name="aljazeeralive20231116">{{cite web |title=Overcrowding at hospitals grows as more move south |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/16/israel-hamas-war-live-israel-rejects-un-security-council-gaza-resolution?update=2491642 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=16 November 2023 |archive-date=3 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240303002515/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/16/israel-hamas-war-live-israel-rejects-un-security-council-gaza-resolution?update=2491642 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Catherine M. Russell]], the executive director of [[UNICEF]], toured Gaza on 15 November 2023, stating many children were lacking medical care.<ref>{{cite web |title=First Person: UNICEF chief in Gaza visit, bears witness to grave violations against children |url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2023/11/1143617 |website=UN News |date=15 November 2023 |publisher=United Nations |access-date=15 November 2023 |archive-date=15 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231115172240/https://news.un.org/en/story/2023/11/1143617 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 28 December, [[UNOCHA]] stated 50 percent of all children in the Gaza Strip were experiencing dehydration, malnutrition, respiratory and skin diseases.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel Flash Update #79 |url=https://www.ochaopt.org/content/hostilities-gaza-strip-and-israel-flash-update-79 |website=UNOCHA |date=28 December 2023 |publisher=United Nations |access-date=29 December 2023 |archive-date=29 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229122556/https://www.ochaopt.org/content/hostilities-gaza-strip-and-israel-flash-update-79 |url-status=live }}</ref> Cases of diarrhea in children under the age of five has increased by about 2,000% since 7 October per a UNICEF report.<ref name="cnn20240130">{{Cite web |last1=Rahimi |first1=Rosa |last2=Noor Haq |first2=Sana |date=30 January 2024 |title='We are dying slowly.' Children go to bed hungry and parents scavenge for food as famine looms in Gaza |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/01/30/middleeast/famine-looms-in-gaza-israel-war-intl/index.html |access-date=9 February 2024 |website=CNN |language=en |archive-date=9 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240209210112/https://www.cnn.com/2024/01/30/middleeast/famine-looms-in-gaza-israel-war-intl/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> A UN spokesperson indicated that between 7 October 2023 and 4 January 2024, disease had skyrocketed in Gaza with more than 400,000 cases of infectious disease reported, which included about 180,000 people with [[Upper respiratory tract infection|upper respiratory infections]] and more than 136,000 cases of [[diarrhea]], with half of cases presenting in children under 5.<ref name="pbs20240104">{{Cite web |last1=Jobain |first1=Najib |last2=Jeffery |first2=Jack |date=4 January 2024 |title=Strike kills 12 people, mostly children, in Gaza area declared safe by Israel |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/strike-kills-12-people-mostly-children-in-gaza-area-declared-safe-by-israel |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=[[PBS NewsHour]] |language=en-us |archive-date=13 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213185328/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/strike-kills-12-people-mostly-children-in-gaza-area-declared-safe-by-israel |url-status=live }}</ref> By July 2024, WHO stated more than 150,000 people had contracted skin infections, with malnourished children most susceptible due to their weakened immune systems.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dangerous skin diseases spreading among children in Gaza |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2024/7/3/dangerous-skin-diseases-spreading-among-children-in-gaza |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=10 July 2024 |archive-date=10 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710042727/https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2024/7/3/dangerous-skin-diseases-spreading-among-children-in-gaza |url-status=live }}</ref>

According to statistics published by the [[World Health Organization|World Health Organization (WHO)]], in January 2024, only about 30% of medics were still working due to the widespread effects of the war in Gaza.<ref name="reuters20240104">{{Cite web |last1=Barbakh |first1=Arafat |last2=Fick |first2=Maggie |last3=Farge |first3=Emma |date=4 January 2024 |title=Gaza's child amputees face further risks without expert care |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/gazas-child-amputees-face-further-risks-without-expert-care-2024-01-04/ |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=[[Reuters]] |archive-date=10 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510233733/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/gazas-child-amputees-face-further-risks-without-expert-care-2024-01-04/ |url-status=live }}</ref> An amputee patient in a southern Gazan hospital stated that medication comes through the crossing into Gaza every four days but its not a guarantee that patients receive medication, and that in some hospitals patients have to pay for medication and food up front.<ref name="cbc20240129">{{Cite web |last1=Barghout |first1=Caroline |last2=Chughtai |first2=Waqas |last3=Hassan |first3=Yasmine |last4=El Saife |first4=Mohamed |date=29 January 2024 |title='No one looks at me': 12-year-old amputee in Gaza on what the war cost him |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/gaza-amputees-children-1.7093914 |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=CBC |archive-date=13 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213161804/https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/gaza-amputees-children-1.7093914 |url-status=live }}</ref> Other medications such as [[Diabetes medication|insulin pens]] were temporarily placed on restricted items to be allowed into Gaza by the Israeli government officials. This caused the UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Palestine Jamie McGoldrick to state; "On the goods that are being prohibited, it’s a full range...Some of it is medical material such as basic drugs and material for treating not just trauma but for chronic illnesses...One example would be most recently the pens that are used for insulin for children"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Qiblawi |first=Tamara |date=1 March 2024 |title=Anesthetics, crutches, dates: The aid Israel is arbitrarily keeping from Gaza |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/03/01/middleeast/gaza-aid-israel-restrictions-investigation-intl-cmd/index.html |access-date=7 March 2024 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en}}</ref> A Canadian doctor returning from two weeks in Gaza stated he had seen the "sickest child I had ever seen in my medical career".<ref>{{cite web |title=Canadian doctor recounts effects of food crisis in Gaza |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/3/5/israels-war-on-gaza-live-israeli-attacks-on-aid-seekers-continue?update=2749991 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=8 March 2024 |archive-date=8 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240308034536/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/3/5/israels-war-on-gaza-live-israeli-attacks-on-aid-seekers-continue?update=2749991 |url-status=live }}</ref> By July 2024, children in tent camps were infected with a number of skin diseases.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shurafa |first1=Wafaa |title=Lice, scabies, rashes plague Palestinian children as skin disease runs rampant in Gaza's tent camps |url=https://apnews.com/article/palestinians-gaza-skin-diseases-israel-war-c30b26d4c4cad0e3f0069efc05d433ad |website=[[Associated Press]] |date=30 July 2024 |access-date=18 August 2024 |archive-date=23 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923043536/https://apnews.com/article/palestinians-gaza-skin-diseases-israel-war-c30b26d4c4cad0e3f0069efc05d433ad |url-status=live }}</ref>

By the summer of 2025, Gaza's healthcare system had been sharply curtailed, with most hospitals in Gaza damaged or out of service.<ref name="thoofi">{{cite web | last1=Ferguson | first1=Sarah | last2=Su | first2=Tong | title=Thousands of Injured Children in Gaza Need Urgent Medical Evacuation | website=UNICEF USA | date=2025-09-23 | url=https://www.unicefusa.org/stories/thousands-injured-children-gaza-need-urgent-medical-evacuation | access-date=2025-09-24}}</ref><ref name="thonee" /> This makes it impossible to access even basic care and leads to growing obstacles for those in need of specialized treatment and support.<ref>{{cite web | title=First group of Gazan children arrive for specialist NHS treatment | website=GOV.UK | date=2025-09-17 | url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/first-group-of-gazan-children-arrive-for-specialist-nhs-treatment | access-date=2025-09-24}}</ref> The humanitarian consequences fall especially hard on children.<ref name="medcri" />

===Medical facilities===
====Children's hospitals====
[[File:Damage in Gaza Strip during the October 2023 - 40 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Wounded child at Al-Shifa Hospital]]
In November 2023, reports indicated that medical care at [[Al-Rantisi Hospital|Al-Rantisi]] and Al-Nasr children's hospitals has nearly come to a halt. Only a small generator provided power to the intensive care and neonatal intensive care units. Al-Rantisi Hospital faced intense attacks and hostilities. Furthermore, Al-Nasr Children's Hospital has once again suffered damage, including vital equipment. Another children's hospital in the northern region has ceased operations due to both damage and a shortage of fuel. Additionally, a specialized maternity hospital is in dire need of fuel to continue functioning.<ref name="UNICEF101123">{{cite web | title=Lives of one million children 'hanging by a thread,' as child health services almost collapse across the Gaza Strip | website=[[UNICEF]] | date=2023-11-10 | url=https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/lives-one-million-children-hanging-thread-child-health-services-almost-collapse | access-date=16 January 2024}}</ref>

On 15 February 2024, the United Nations reported that Israel had destroyed its clinic for visually impaired children, stating the "centre was available to all visually impaired children across the Gaza Strip and provided braille machines, canes, [and] visual aids."<ref>{{cite web |title=UNRWA says facility for visually impaired children has been totally destroyed |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/2/15/israels-war-on-gaza-live-four-dead-as-israel-hits-city-in-lebanons-south?update=2710855 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=17 February 2024}}</ref>

====Medical evacuations====
Due to the destruction of Gaza's healthcare system, medical evacuation is necessary for access to specialized treatment unavailable in the Gaza Strip.<ref name=thoofi/><ref name=thonee>{{cite web | title=Medical evacuation from Gaza: Thousands need care no longer available in the Strip | website=Doctors Without Borders - USA | date=2025-07-17 | url=https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/medical-evacuation-gaza-thousands-need-care-no-longer-available-strip | access-date=2025-09-24}}</ref>

Evacuation planning for children with medical concerns such as cancer out of Gaza and to continue treatment began in mid-October 2023, with discussions and negotiations among the United States, Egypt, Israel and Palestinian health officials along with [[World Health Organization]] and [[St. Jude Children's Research Hospital]] representatives. Many families and officials involved in Gaza have described a difficult process with damage to transportation avenues and communication networks causing many to miss crossing or pick-up times, while others were not allowed to evacuate with their children.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=LaFraniere |first1=Sharon |last2=Green |first2=Erica |date=15 November 2023 |title=Inside the Desperate Effort to Evacuate Young Cancer Patients From Gaza |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/14/us/politics/gaza-hospitals-cancer-israel.html |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=The New York Times |archive-date=16 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240116015400/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/14/us/politics/gaza-hospitals-cancer-israel.html |url-status=live }}</ref> After repeated airstrike damage and lack of fuel at least two dozen premature babies were evacuated out of Gaza hospitals to Egypt to continue the specialized care they needed. Those that were evacuated were suffering from life-threatening conditions including dehydration, vomiting, hypothermia and sepsis due to the lack of medicine and fuel.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kekatos |first1=Mary |last2=Cobern |first2=Dr. Jade |date=21 November 2023 |title=Dozens of premature infants were evacuated from Gaza. Here's the care doctors say they will need |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Health/dozens-premature-infants-evacuated-gaza-egypt-care-doctors/story?id=105032358 |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=ABC News |language=en |archive-date=6 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206194204/https://abcnews.go.com/Health/dozens-premature-infants-evacuated-gaza-egypt-care-doctors/story?id=105032358 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Al-Mughrabi |first1=Nidal |last2=Williams |first2=Dan |date=20 November 2023 |title=Premature Gaza babies evacuated to Egypt as Israeli tanks encircle second hospital |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-tanks-reported-near-hospital-embattled-north-gaza-2023-11-20/ |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=Reuters |archive-date=13 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213135138/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-tanks-reported-near-hospital-embattled-north-gaza-2023-11-20/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Injured children were also evacuated with Turkey offering treatment and resources to at least two groups of children that were receiving intensive care treatment.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Gocumlu |first1=Burcu Calik |last2=Erdogan |first2=Muhammed Nuri |last3=Karaaslan |first3=Yesim Sert |date=23 November 2023 |title=Turkish health minister welcomes 3 injured children evacuated from Gaza |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/turkish-health-minister-welcomes-3-injured-children-evacuated-from-gaza/3062934 |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=www.aa.com.tr |archive-date=6 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206194205/https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkiye/turkish-health-minister-welcomes-3-injured-children-evacuated-from-gaza/3062934 |url-status=live }}</ref>

It was reported in early March 2024, that about 300 children had been evacuated to Qatar with the majority being wounded and needing treatment but some being parents or a supporter. Many described the separation from family members as excruciating, with some children being unable to talk to their parents, living with relatives in Gaza or having to monitor and parent younger siblings while their parents care for their injured siblings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shahld Ahmed |first=Akbar |date=5 March 2024 |title=These Injured Palestinians Made It Out Of Gaza. Their Loved Ones Did Not — And The Distance Is Agony. |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/injured-palestine-qatar-gaza-families_n_65e76032e4b0f9d26cac8ef1 |access-date=7 March 2024 |website=HuffPost |language=en |archive-date=8 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240308054311/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/injured-palestine-qatar-gaza-families_n_65e76032e4b0f9d26cac8ef1 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 16 August 2025, the [[U.S. State Department]] announced that it had suspended the issuance of visitor visas to people from the Gaza Strip, including children who require urgent medical care.<ref>{{cite news |title=State Department stopping issuance of visitor visas for 'individuals from Gaza' |url=https://abcnews.go.com/US/state-department-stopping-issuance-visitor-visas-individuals-gaza/story?id=124725360|work=ABC News}}</ref>

In January–April 2024, medical evacuations for children from Gaza averaged about 296 per month; by late 2024 the rate had fallen to under one per day. In October 2024, UNICEF said children were dying not only from the violence itself but also because survivors were often unable to leave Gaza for urgent, life-saving treatment.<ref name=thoofi/> By July/September 2025, an estimated 2,500-4,500 of critically wounded children are waiting for permits to be evacuated for care.<ref name=thoofi/><ref name=thonee/>

===Preventive and systemic care===

==== Hygiene ====
[[File:A displaced child takes care of his brother in Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip.jpg|thumb|A displaced child takes care of his brother in Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip]]
In December 2023, [[ActionAid]] reported that there was little water for washing and some shelters only had one shower for every 700 individuals and one toilet for every 150.<ref name="france24live20231211">{{Cite web |date=11 December 2023 |title=Menstrual periods an ordeal, health risk for Gaza women and girls |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231211-menstrual-periods-an-ordeal-health-risk-for-gaza-women-and-girls |access-date=11 March 2024 |website=France 24 |language=en |archive-date=11 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240311150439/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231211-menstrual-periods-an-ordeal-health-risk-for-gaza-women-and-girls |url-status=live }}</ref> UNICEF announced on 7 March 2024 that they were distributing wellbeing kits to adolescent girls in Rafah, who reported being unable to "shower more than once a week. The shelters are crowded with people, and there is little water. It is difficult to maintain personal hygiene".<ref>{{cite web |title=UNICEF distributing wellbeing kits to adolescent girls in Rafah |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/3/7/israels-war-on-gaza-live-20-starve-to-death-in-gaza-more-feared-dead?update=2756621 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=9 March 2024 |archive-date=9 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240309172448/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/3/7/israels-war-on-gaza-live-20-starve-to-death-in-gaza-more-feared-dead?update=2756621 |url-status=live }}</ref>

It was reported in late February 2024 that there were 690,000 menstruating women and children in Gaza, that have limited access to [[Feminine hygiene|menstrual hygiene supplies]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 February 2024 |title=Crisis in the occupied Palestinian territory |url=https://www.unfpa.org/occupied-palestinian-territory |access-date=11 March 2024 |website=www.unfpa.org |language=en}}</ref> Some women and children have utilized period blocking pills, but those can be hard to find and many are unable to take them for medical reasons.<ref name="npr20240111">{{Cite web |last1=Batrawy |first1=Aya |last2=Bakr Bashir |first2=Abu |date=11 January 2024 |title=Another layer of misery: Women in Gaza struggle to find menstrual pads, running water |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2024/01/11/1224201620/another-layer-of-misery-women-in-gaza-struggle-to-find-menstrual-pads-running-wa |access-date=11 March 2024 |website=NPR |archive-date=11 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240311150439/https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2024/01/11/1224201620/another-layer-of-misery-women-in-gaza-struggle-to-find-menstrual-pads-running-wa |url-status=live }}</ref> One girl sheltering in a UNRWA school in [[Maghazi refugee camp|Maghazi]] told reporters that she had begun washing used pads to reuse them, while another indicated that due to the stress of the war she had been having her period more often, about twice a month.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mousa |first=Aseel |date=5 March 2024 |title='My period has become a nightmare': life in Gaza without sanitary products |url=https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2024/mar/05/my-period-has-become-nightmare-life-in-gaza-without-sanitary-products |access-date=11 March 2024 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> A mom of five daughters told reporters that they were all utilizing [[Pampers]] diapers for their periods, and had to cut the diapers in half due to costs while others have utilized rags, old clothes, towels or corners of tents causing chafing and skin infections.<ref name="france24live20231211" /><ref name="npr20240111" />

In June 2024, children suffered from intestinal infections and hepatitis C or A, due to the destruction of Gaza's [[Water supply and sanitation in Palestine|water supply and sanitation systems]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Donnison |first1=Jon |title=Gaza's water system, destroyed by war, is sickening its children |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd119dz515wo?xtor=AL-72-%5Bpartner%5D-%5Bbbc.news.twitter%5D-%5Bheadline%5D-%5Bnews%5D-%5Bbizdev%5D-%5Bisapi%5D&at_link_type=web_link&at_link_id=CD132008-2F8B-11EF-B975-BCE22307FCC8&at_link_origin=BBCWorld&at_bbc_team=editorial&at_campaign=Social_Flow&at_medium=social&at_ptr_name=twitter&at_format=link&at_campaign_type=owned |website=BBC |date=21 June 2024 |access-date=4 July 2024}}</ref>

====Vaccinations====
{{See also|COVID-19 pandemic in Palestine#Vaccines|2024 Gaza Strip polio outbreak}}
Shortly after the 7 October attacks and Israel's retaliation in October 2023, preventable diseases were expected to rise due to disruption in vaccination abilities. Childhood vaccinations had already dropped due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Palestine|COVID-19 pandemic]], and experts cautioned about the spread of infectious diseases such as [[COVID-19]] and [[measles]] that could be contained primarily with vaccinations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edwards |first=Erika |date=22 October 2023 |title=Tainted water and viruses put Gaza residents, especially kids, at further risk |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/tainted-water-viruses-put-gaza-residents-especially-kids-risk-rcna120868 |access-date=11 March 2024 |website=NBC News |language=en |archive-date=29 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240329030603/https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/tainted-water-viruses-put-gaza-residents-especially-kids-risk-rcna120868 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In mid-December 2023, the [[Gaza Health Ministry]] stated it had run out of vaccinations for children, which would have catastrophic repercussions.<ref name="france24live20231213">{{cite web |title=Gaza health ministry says out of children's vaccines |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231213-gaza-health-ministry-says-out-of-children-s-vaccines |website=[[France24]] |date=13 December 2023 |access-date=13 December 2023 |archive-date=13 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213131846/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231213-gaza-health-ministry-says-out-of-children-s-vaccines |url-status=live }}</ref> An UNOCHA representative stated the organization was having difficulty delivering childhood vaccines.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vaccines received, but getting them to babies across Gaza is impossible: UN |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/1/1/israel-hamas-war-live-new-year-in-gaza-under-non-stop-israeli-bombardment?update=2591421 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=2 January 2024 |archive-date=2 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240102002816/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/1/1/israel-hamas-war-live-new-year-in-gaza-under-non-stop-israeli-bombardment?update=2591421 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 1 January 2024 it was reported by the Palestinian Health Ministry that Israel had allowed and would facilitate the transport of vaccines into Gaza through the [[Rafah Border Crossing|Rafa crossing]]. It was cautioned that the disbursement of the vaccines would be difficult due to displacement and destruction of infrastructure.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 January 2024 |title=Childhood vaccine doses enter Gaza through Rafah crossing |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/thousands-doses-childhood-vaccines-enter-gaza-palestinian-health-ministry-2024-01-01/ |access-date=7 March 2024 |website=Reuters}}</ref> On 29 January 2024, UNICEF reported that 16,000 children were at risk of missing routine vaccinations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Routine vaccines are saving children lives in the Gaza Strip |url=https://www.unicef.org/sop/stories/routine-vaccines-are-saving-children-lives |website=UNICEF |access-date=30 January 2024 |archive-date=30 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240130055356/https://www.unicef.org/sop/stories/routine-vaccines-are-saving-children-lives |url-status=live }}</ref>

In July 2024, a [[2024 Gaza Strip polio outbreak|polio outbreak]] occurred in Gaza,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Polio in Gaza: WHO 'extremely worried' about possible outbreak |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crgrxjn9rkpo |access-date=23 July 2024 |website=www.bbc.com |date=23 July 2024 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=30 July 2024 |title=Polio cases 'very likely' in Gaza population, WHO says |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/polio-cases-very-likely-gaza-population-who-says-2024-07-30/ |access-date=30 July 2024 |work=Reuters}}</ref> marking the first appearance of the virus there in 25 years,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Al-Taher |first=Nada |date=30 July 2024 |title=Gaza declares polio epidemic 25 years after disease was eradicated in enclave |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2024/07/30/gaza-declares-polio-epidemic-25-years-after-disease-was-eradicated-in-enclave/ |access-date=30 July 2024 |website=The National |language=en}}</ref> and it remains ongoing. In order to contain the polio virus outbreak and limit further transmission, the [[WHO]] held two vaccination drives, one in September 2024 that reached 90% of children under 10, and one in February 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/who-confident-that-polio-vaccine-drive-in-gaza-hit-target-of-90-of-kids-under-10/|title=WHO 'confident' that polio vaccine drive in Gaza hit target of 90% of kids under 10 &#124; The Times of Israel|website=[[The Times of Israel]] |date=12 September 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Humanitarian access improves quality of polio vaccination campaign in the Gaza Strip | website=World Health Organization (WHO)| date=2025-02-28 | url=https://www.who.int/news/item/28-02-2025-humanitarian-access-improves-quality-of-polio-vaccination-campaign-in-the-gaza-strip | ref={{sfnref|	World Health Organization (WHO) |2025}} | access-date=2025-09-24}}</ref>

=== Survival and physical conditions ===

|url=https://www.msn.com/en-in/video/news/voices-from-gaza-father-loses-daughter-to-malnutrition-amid-blockade-and-dire-living-conditions/vi-AA1oSp9m |website=MSN |publisher=Al Jazeera English |access-date=10 September 2024 |archive-date=1 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201202133/https://www.msn.com/en-in/video/news/voices-from-gaza-father-loses-daughter-to-malnutrition-amid-blockade-and-dire-living-conditions/vi-AA1oSp9m |url-status=live }}</ref>

In October 2024, [[Save the Children]] reported that of the approximately 3000 under five-years-old children they had screened, about 20 percent had moderate acute malnutrition and four percent had severe acute malnutrition.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Devi |first1=Sharmila |title=Child health in Gaza |journal=The Lancet |date=October 2024 |volume=404 |issue=10463 |pages=1630–1631 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(24)02349-3 |pmid=39492346 |url=https://www.thelancet.com/action/showPdf?pii=S0140-6736%2824%2902349-3 |access-date=30 October 2024|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

From 2 March until 26 May 2025, [[Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israel completely blocked]] all supplies from entering Gaza, making it the longest complete closure in the history of the blockade.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2025 |title=Gaza aid dries up as Israeli blockade enters a third month |url=https://apnews.com/article/gaza-aid-hunger-israel-hamas-b7429c043bc9d01717713eab21bae546 |access-date=7 May 2025 |website=AP News |language=en |archive-date=7 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250507114924/https://apnews.com/article/gaza-aid-hunger-israel-hamas-b7429c043bc9d01717713eab21bae546 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2 May 2025 |title=Gaza tensions flare over dwindling supplies as blockade persists, aid worker says |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/gaza-tensions-flare-over-dwindling-supplies-blockade-persists-aid-worker-says-2025-05-02/ |access-date=2 May 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Since 26 May 2025, the [[United States]]- and Israeli-backed [[Gaza Humanitarian Foundation]] has facilitated limited and largely ineffective aid distribution.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gaza: Nearly 1,400 Palestinians killed while seeking food, as UN warns airdrops are no solution |url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/08/1165552 |work=UN News}}</ref> In June 2025, UNICEF-supported clinics in Gaza reported a sharp rise in child malnutrition: 16,736 children were treated between January and May 2025, including 5,119 in May alone. This was nearly 50% more than in April and over double the February figure. Of these, 636 had severe acute malnutrition, the deadliest form, which has risen by about 146% since February. UNICEF warns that without large-scale aid deliveries, acute malnutrition could reach its highest level since the conflict began, despite wasting being virtually absent 20 months earlier.<ref>{{cite web | title=More than 5,000 children diagnosed with malnutrition in the Gaza Strip in May | website=UNICEF, for every child | date=2025-06-19 | url=https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/more-5000-children-diagnosed-malnutrition-gaza-strip-may | access-date=2025-09-24}}</ref>

In December 2023, an Israeli shell struck the largest fertility clinic in Gaza; the explosion knocked the lids off five liquid nitrogen tanks, causing temperature within the tanks to rise and destroying more than 4,000 embryos and 1,000 specimens of unfertilized eggs and sperm. According to [[Bahaeldeen Ghalayini]], the obstetrician and gynaecologist who founded the clinic, the corner of the building was hit by a single shell, destroying the ground floor embryology lab; he does not know whether the strike was intentional or not.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salem |first1=Saleh |last2=Creidi |first2=Imad |last3=Mills |first3=Andrew |title=Gaza's IVF embryos destroyed by Israeli strike |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/5000-lives-one-shell-gazas-ivf-embryos-destroyed-by-israeli-strike-2024-04-17/ |website=Reuters |access-date=23 April 2024 |archive-date=20 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420081404/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/5000-lives-one-shell-gazas-ivf-embryos-destroyed-by-israeli-strike-2024-04-17/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====Premature babies====

=== Trauma and aftermath ===
====Wounded child, no surviving family====
One of the most difficult aspects of the medical crisis in Gaza is “wounded child, no surviving family” (WCNSF). As of February 2025, the [[United Nations]] has reported roughly 25,000 such cases in Gaza; with no relatives left, clinicians become the children's sole caregivers and advocates, which complicates treatment decisions and long-term care planning.<ref name=medcri/> For children lacking any family support, the confusion and distress that accompany serious injuries are magnified many times over.<ref name=nofamn/> Disrupted access to healthcare also triggers cascading physical, psychological, and social harms that demand responses beyond routine medical practice. Providers must address immediate needs as well as rehabilitation, mental-health support, and coordination with social services without family involvement. These challenges differ markedly from typical adult care.<ref name=medcri>{{cite journal | last1=Nasari | first1=Alaha | last2=Marzouk | first2=Sammer | last3=Mowafi | first3=Hani | last4=Al-Hajj | first4=Samar | title=The medical crisis of war-injured children in Gaza and Lebanon | journal=Nature Medicine | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=31 | issue=3 | date=2025-02-03 | issn=1078-8956 | doi=10.1038/s41591-024-03474-w | pages=715–716 | pmid=39901046 }}</ref>

====Mental health====
[[File:Fars Photo of Casualties in Gaza Strip during 2023 War 31.jpg|thumb|Injured child, 17 October 2023]]

Before the war, there were high numbers of children in Gaza that had documented high levels of [[Distress (medicine)|emotional distress]] and mental illness, with a study in 2011 found that among Palestinian children [[Post-traumatic stress disorder|PTSD]] rates were between 23 and 70%,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dimitry |first=L. |date=March 2012 |title=A systematic review on the mental health of children and adolescents in areas of armed conflict in the Middle East |journal=Child: Care, Health and Development |volume=38 |issue=2 |pages=153–161 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-2214.2011.01246.x |issn=1365-2214 |pmid=21615769 }}</ref> while a UNICEF study in 2021 found one in three children in Gaza needed care for conflict-related trauma.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chatterjee |first=Rhitu |date=10 November 2023 |title=How a history of trauma is affecting the children of Gaza |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2023/11/10/1211672951/israel-hamas-war-mental-health-gaza-children |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=NPR |archive-date=14 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240214184329/https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2023/11/10/1211672951/israel-hamas-war-mental-health-gaza-children |url-status=live }}</ref>

After 16 days of sustained air strikes and explosions, children had developed severe trauma, with symptoms including convulsion, aggression, bed-wetting, and nervousness. 90% of children in pediatric hospitals in Gaza exhibited or reported symptoms of anxiety, the majority exhibited post-traumatic stress symptoms, and 82% reported fears of imminent death.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sherwood |first1=Harriet |date=22 October 2023 |title=Children in Gaza 'developing severe trauma' after 16 days of bombing |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/oct/22/children-in-gaza-developing-severe-trauma-after-16-days-of-bombing |work=[[The Guardian]] |quote=Children had "started to develop serious trauma symptoms such as convulsions, bed-wetting, fear, aggressive behaviour, nervousness, and not leaving their parents’ sides." The "lack of any safe place has created a general sense of fear and horror among the entire population and children are most impacted," he said. |access-date=3 April 2024 |archive-date=22 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022134849/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/oct/22/children-in-gaza-developing-severe-trauma-after-16-days-of-bombing |url-status=live }}</ref>

21 February 2024, the chair of the Norwegian Refugee Council warned that all children in Gaza would likely suffer from trauma due to the war.<ref>{{cite web |title='Israel's war has traumatized all children in Gaza' |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/2/21/israels-war-on-gaza-live-us-ceasefire-veto-a-new-low-as-hunger-spreads?update=2722818 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=22 February 2024 |archive-date=9 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409034356/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/2/21/israels-war-on-gaza-live-us-ceasefire-veto-a-new-low-as-hunger-spreads?update=2722818 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 23 February 2024, the director of [[Doctors Without Borders]] reported, "Psychological injuries have led children as young as five to tell us that they would prefer to die."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=Michelle |title=MSF slams US on Gaza at UN, says children as young as 5 want to die |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/msf-slams-us-gaza-un-says-children-young-5-want-die-2024-02-22/#:~:text=%22There%20is%20a%20repeated%20displacement,they%20would%20prefer%20to%20die.%22 |website=Reuters |date=22 February 2024 |access-date=24 February 2024 |archive-date=25 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240425172135/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/msf-slams-us-gaza-un-says-children-young-5-want-die-2024-02-22/#:~:text=%22There%20is%20a%20repeated%20displacement,they%20would%20prefer%20to%20die.%22 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Save the Children]] found, "Children in Gaza are going through a period of mass-scale shock and grief. This war and the physical and mental scars it is leaving on children is further eroding their resilience."<ref>{{cite web |title="Complete psychological destruction": Children in Gaza have suffered "relentless mental harm" during five months of war |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/occupied-palestinian-territory/complete-psychological-destruction-children-gaza-have-suffered-relentless-mental-harm-during-five-months-war-save-children |website=ReliefWeb |date=12 March 2024 |publisher=Save the Children |access-date=15 March 2024 |archive-date=8 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240408143936/https://reliefweb.int/report/occupied-palestinian-territory/complete-psychological-destruction-children-gaza-have-suffered-relentless-mental-harm-during-five-months-war-save-children |url-status=live }}</ref> In July 2024, Julia Wendt, the emergency child protection coordinator with the [[International Rescue Committee]], stated children in Gaza were suffering from nightmares and bedwetting due to the mental toll of the war.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Khaled |first1=Fatma |title=Bedwetting, nightmares and shaking. War in Gaza takes a mental health toll, especially on children |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/bedwetting-nightmares-shaking-war-gaza-takes-mental-health-112054042#:~:text=For%20children%2C%20the%20mental%20toll,lost%20all%20sense%20of%20security. |website=ABC News |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=28 July 2024 |archive-date=29 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240729122834/https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/bedwetting-nightmares-shaking-war-gaza-takes-mental-health-112054042#:~:text=For%20children%2C%20the%20mental%20toll,lost%20all%20sense%20of%20security. |url-status=live }}</ref> In September 2024, children's hair was turning prematurely grey due to their high levels of stress.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Osman |first1=Nadda |last2=Ibrahim |first2=Sally |title=Gaza: Children's hair greying, falling out from shock and trauma |url=https://www.newarab.com/news/gaza-childrens-hair-greying-falling-out-shock-and-trauma |website=The New Arab |access-date=15 September 2024 |archive-date=15 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240915053615/https://www.newarab.com/news/gaza-childrens-hair-greying-falling-out-shock-and-trauma |url-status=live }}</ref> In October 2024, Dr. Bahzad Al-Akhras, a psychiatrist in Al-Mawasi, described the psychological impacts of the war on children, stating they were "learning that nothing is secure, nothing is stable. They have learnt to continuously escape, not to trust others, not to trust life itself."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ahmed |first1=Kaamil |last2=González Paz |first2=Ana Lucía |title='I hate the night': Life in Gaza amid the incessant sounds of war |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-interactive/2024/oct/17/i-hate-the-night-life-in-gaza-amid-the-incessant-sounds-of-war |website=The Guardian |date=17 October 2024 |access-date=1 November 2024}}</ref>

Caitlin Procter, a researcher at the Centre on Conflict, Development and Peacebuilding in Geneva, highlighted the severe psychological impact on children in Gaza. Some have witnessed the brutal killings of their parents by soldiers, while others have seen their homes destroyed by bombings. Many children endure extreme conditions of cold, hunger, and loneliness, spending days wandering the streets alone. The overwhelming situation has left even mental health experts in Gaza feeling helpless and in need of support. In Rafah, located in the southern part of the Palestinian territory, Karyn Beattie from the NGO Save the Children described the dire situation where displaced Gazan children, some as young as pre-teens, are forced to work as breadwinners, selling aid items to afford basic necessities.<ref>[https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2024/04/05/israel-s-war-in-gaza-has-already-proved-particularly-devastating-for-children_6667509_4.html Israel's war in Gaza is particularly devastating for children] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420121837/https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2024/04/05/israel-s-war-in-gaza-has-already-proved-particularly-devastating-for-children_6667509_4.html |date=20 April 2024 }} Retrieved 6 April 2024</ref>

By October 2025, large numbers of children were seen on the streets during the day, many showing unusually aggressive behavior. The psychological damage suffered by Gaza's younger generation is described as beyond measure.<ref name=nofamn/>

== Military detention ==
Annually, the Israeli military arrests approximately 500 to 700 Palestinian children, all under the age of 18. As reported by Addameer, a Palestinian NGO, about 200 of these children remain incarcerated in Israeli prisons. Following the commencement of Israel's aggressive actions in Gaza on 7 October, there has been a noticeable surge in detentions - with over 450 children being taken into custody at various points, as stated by the Palestinian Commission for Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs. Since the year 2000, an estimated 13,000 children have been subject to arbitrary detention, interrogation, trial in military courts, and imprisonment.<ref>[https://www.trtworld.com/magazine/palestinian-childrens-day-puts-spotlight-on-israels-war-on-kids-17657201 Palestinian Children’s Day puts spotlight on Israel’s war on kids] Retrieved 6 April 2024</ref>

Many Palestinian children are detained in nighttime operations, with some being placed in administrative detention without a fair trial or formal charges. According to Lawyers for Palestinian Human Rights, there are numerous significant human rights issues associated with these procedures.<ref>[https://time.com/6548068/palestinian-children-israeli-prison-arrested/ The Traumatic Arrests of Children] Retrieved 11 March 2024</ref>

In May 2024, the Israeli military publicly identified several Palestinian children, alleging that they had been acting as Hamas informants, leading the [[United Nations Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories]] to state the Israeli army often forces detained Palestinian children to become informants.<ref>{{cite web |title=Israeli military claims to expose Palestinian minors as 'Hamas informants' |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/5/18/israels-war-on-gaza-live-battles-in-jabalia-and-rafah-as-israel-advances?update=2908134 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524014644/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/5/18/israels-war-on-gaza-live-battles-in-jabalia-and-rafah-as-israel-advances?update=2908134 |archive-date=24 May 2024 |access-date=24 May 2024 |website=Al Jazeera}}</ref>

In April 2025, it was reported that Walid Ahmad was the first Palestinian child to die in Israeli prisons. Ahmad was arrested six months prior to his death and kept at the [[Megiddo Prison]] after being accused of throwing stones at soldiers in the occupied West Bank.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frankel |first=Julia |date=1 April 2025 |title=A Palestinian from the West Bank is first detainee under 18 to die in Israeli prison, officials say |url=https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-palestinian-prisoner-teenager-dead-874271e9c7afe095310143233aec0d38 |access-date=2 April 2025 |website=AP News |language=en |archive-date=1 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401183217/https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-palestinian-prisoner-teenager-dead-874271e9c7afe095310143233aec0d38 |url-status=live }}</ref>

From the beginning of the Gaza war, reports emerged of children being killed and maimed.<ref name= humsi1>{{cite web | title=UNICEF in the State of Palestine Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1  | url=https://www.unicef.org/sop/media/2606/file/UNICEF%20in%20the%20State%20of%20Palestine%20Escalation%20Humanitarian%20Situation%20Report%20No.1.pdf | access-date=2025-10-15}}</ref> Children were also killed in Israeli airstrikes, including in areas designated as “safe zones” by the IDF.<ref name="pbs20240104" /> The numbers rose rapidly. During the first week of the war in October 2023, at least 447 children were killed.<ref name= humsi1/> By 3 December 2023, the number had reached an estimated 6,150 children,<ref>{{cite web |title=WATCH: Palestinian boy's farewell to brother killed in Israeli air raid |url-status=live }}</ref> rising to about  an estimated 10,000 by mid-January 2024, with thousands more believed to be buried under rubble.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gaza: 10,000 children killed in nearly 100 days of war |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/occupied-palestinian-territory/gaza-10000-children-killed-nearly-100-days-war |website=ReliefWeb |date=11 January 2024 |publisher=Save the Children estimate down from 14,500 children to 7,797 identified child deaths,<ref>{{cite web | title=Gaza War: UN revises death toll for women and children | website=ReliefWeb | date=2024-05-17 | reported at roughly 14,500.<ref>{{cite web | title=Humanitarian Situation Report No. 34 | been reported killed.<ref name=hums42/>

In March 2024, the United Nations stated that more children had died in Gaza between October 2023 and February 2024 than the sum of all global conflicts from 2019 to 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lim |first1=Clarissa-Jan |title=More children killed in Gaza in four months than in four years of war globally: report |url=https://www.msnbc.com/top-stories/latest/death-toll-children-gaza-israel-rcna143269 |website=MSNBC |date=14 March 2024 |access-date=14 March 2024 |archive-date=14 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314163954/https://www.msnbc.com/top-stories/latest/death-toll-children-gaza-israel-rcna143269 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Catherine M. Russell]], the head of UNICEF, stated, "We haven’t seen that rate of death among children in almost any other conflict in the world".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Singh |first1=Kanishka |title=UNICEF says over 13,000 children killed in Gaza in Israel offensive |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/unicef-says-over-13000-children-killed-gaza-israel-offensive-2024-03-17/ |website=Reuters |date=18 March 2024 |access-date=21 March 2024 |archive-date=18 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240318091312/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/unicef-says-over-13000-children-killed-gaza-israel-offensive-2024-03-17/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In late September 2024, [[Oxfam]] and [[Action on Armed Violence]] reported that the number of children killed in Gaza over the past year was the highest recorded in a single year for any conflict worldwide in the last 20 years.<ref>{{cite web |title=More women and children killed in Gaza by Israeli military than any other recent conflict in a single year |url=https://www.oxfam.org/en/press-releases/more-women-and-children-killed-gaza-israeli-military-any-other-recent-conflict |website=[[Oxfam]] |date=October 2024 |access-date=8 October 2024 |archive-date=8 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008001759/https://www.oxfam.org/en/press-releases/more-women-and-children-killed-gaza-israeli-military-any-other-recent-conflict |url-status=live }}</ref>

Warning of the joint threats of starvation and disease, a UNICEF spokesperson stated in February 2024: "The Gaza Strip is poised to witness an explosion in preventable child deaths which would compound the already unbearable level of child deaths in Gaza".<ref>{{cite web |title=CHILDREN'S LIVES THREATENED BY RISING MALNUTRITION IN THE GAZA STRIP |url=https://www.unicef.org.uk/press-releases/childrens-lives-threatened-by-rising-malnutrition-in-the-gaza-strip/#:~:text=“The%20Gaza%20Strip%20is%20poised,and%20Supply%20Operations%2C%20Ted%20Chaiban. |website=UNICEF |access-date=21 February 2024 |archive-date=21 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221062329/https://www.unicef.org.uk/press-releases/childrens-lives-threatened-by-rising-malnutrition-in-the-gaza-strip/#:~:text=“The%20Gaza%20Strip%20is%20poised,and%20Supply%20Operations%2C%20Ted%20Chaiban. |url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 2025, [[Killing of al-Najjar children|nine of Alaa al-Najjar's ten children]], a paediatric specialist working at [[Nasser Hospital]], were killed by an Israeli airstrike at their home in Khan Yunis, the eldest of the children aged 13 and the youngest aged six months. Her husband and tenth child were also injured from the attack, and her husband Hamdi later succumbed to his injuries.<ref>{{cite web|title= Gaza doctor grieves her nine children killed in Israeli strike|url= https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/gaza-doctor-receives-bodies-her-seven-children-while-duty|website=Middle East Eye|date=24 May 2025|last=Hussaini|first=Maha|access-date=25 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Father of nine children killed by Israeli strike still in critical condition|url= https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp8djlg3zq5o.amp|website=BBC News|date=25 May 2025|last=Moench|first=Mallory|access-date=25 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= 'Death is sometimes kinder': Gaza doctor's relatives recount horror of deadly Israeli strike|url= https://trt.global/world/article/66931bd994cd|website=TRT Global|date=25 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Gaza doctor who lost nine children in Israeli airstrike dies from wounds in same attack|url= https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/01/gaza-doctor-who-lost-nine-children-in-israeli-airstrike-dies-from-wounds-in-same-attack|website=The Guardian|date=1 June 2025|author1=Lorenzo Tondo|author2=Malak A. Tantesh|access-date=1 June 2025}}</ref>

====Sniper killings====
In February 2024, an American doctor returning from the Gaza Strip wrote an op-ed in the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' stating that she had witnessed children being deliberately targeted by Israeli snipers, writing, "On one occasion, a handful of children, all about ages 5 to 8, were carried to the emergency room by their parents. All had single sniper shots to the head... None of these children survived."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Galaria |first1=Irfan |title=I'm an American doctor who went to Gaza. What I saw wasn't war — it was annihilation |url=https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2024-02-16/rafah-gaza-hospitals-surgery-israel-bombing-ground-offensive-children |newspaper=LA Times |date=16 February 2024 |access-date=18 February 2024 |archive-date=18 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240218012619/https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2024-02-16/rafah-gaza-hospitals-surgery-israel-bombing-ground-offensive-children |url-status=live }}</ref> A Canadian doctor returning from a week in Gaza stated she had seen [[crimes against humanity]], including small children "dying of hunger, bombs, sniper shots."<ref>{{cite web |title=The world has failed the children of Gaza: Canadian doctor |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/2/25/israels-war-on-gaza-live-rafah-strikes-further-harming-aid-efforts-un?update=2732212 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=26 February 2024 |archive-date=9 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009192436/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/2/25/israels-war-on-gaza-live-rafah-strikes-further-harming-aid-efforts-un?update=2732212 |url-status=live }}</ref> Israeli drone footage released in March 2024 showed Israeli snipers killing an unarmed boy in [[Jabalia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Israeli drone footage documents sniping of a Palestinian boy |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/3/10/israels-war-on-gaza-live-israel-is-restricting-lifesaving-aid-unrwa?update=2762254 |website=Al Jazeera |access-date=13 March 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref> In April 2024, doctors said they were seeing "a steady stream of children, elderly people and others who were clearly not combatants with single bullet wounds to the head or chest."<ref>{{cite news |last1=McGreal |first1=Chris |title='Not a normal war': doctors say children have been targeted by Israeli snipers in Gaza
