==== Community homes and social centers ====
{{Multiple image
| image1      = Hôpital HEAL AFRICA à Goma.jpg
| caption1    = Hospital Heal Africa
| image2      = Hôpital de keyshero Goma vue de devant.jpg
| caption2    = Hospital of Keyshero
| total_width = 160
| direction   = vertical
}}

Beyond formal schooling, Goma hosts numerous literacy centers that provide [[Vocational education|vocational training]] and [[language education]], including community homes and [[Community centre|social centers]] such as the Karisimbi Social Promotion Center (''Centre de promotion sociale de Karisimbi''; CPS-K), the CBCA-Virunga Social Animation Center (''Centre d'animation sociale CBCA-Virunga''), and the Center for Physically Disabled People (''Centre pour Handicapés physiques''); together, these institutions support 3,846 people (2011 estimates), while 1,381 abandoned or street children were registered in 2008 and placed under the care of the Kinyogote Center.<ref name=":25" />

=== Health care ===
A range of medical and health-related training institutions operate throughout the city, including the Goma Provincial Hospital (''hôpital provincial de Goma''), [[Tertiary referral hospital|referral hospitals]] such as CBCA Ndosho, CBCA Virunga, and Charité Maternelle, as well as private [[Clinic|clinics]], public [[Community health center|health centers]] and posts, and nutrition centers in areas such as Birere, Notre-Dame d'Afrique, and Mugunga.<ref name=":25" />

=== Religion ===
Goma is home to several Christian churches and temples including the churches of the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Goma]], [[Kimbanguism|Kimbanguist Church]], [[Baptist Community of Congo]] ([[Baptist World Alliance|World Baptist Alliance]]), the Baptist Community in the Center of Africa (World Baptist Alliance), [[Assemblies of God]], [[Province of the Anglican Church of the Congo|Province of the Anglican Church of Congo]] ([[Anglican Communion]]), Presbyterian Community in Congo ([[World Communion of Reformed Churches]]). There are also Muslim [[mosque]]s.<ref name=":42" />

Goma hosts a Catholic priest seminary ''Redemptoris Mater'' run by the [[Neocatechumenal Way]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013 |title=Seminario Redemptoris Mater di Goma (Congo) |url=https://www.sanpietroapostolo.org/seminari/Goma.htm |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=Sanpietroapostolo.org |language=it}}</ref>

== Economy ==
[[File:Paysanne cultivant son champ de manioc sur les hauteurs du lac vert (23983084781).jpg|thumb|Cassava cultivation on the highlands surrounding the [[Volcanic crater lake|crater lake]] Lac Vert in the Mugunga quarter|224x224px]]

=== Agriculture ===
Goma's economy relies mainly on [[agriculture]], with a significant proportion of its population making a living by buying and selling farm products. Because the local currency is unstable, many transactions are carried out in foreign currencies.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web |last=Muhindo |first=Yusuf |date=2020 |title=L'elevage des poules pondeuses et son impact sur la vie economique dans la ville de goma de 2018–2020 |trans-title=Raising laying hens and its impact on economic life in the city of Goma from 2018–2020 |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/10/22/13203/m_Lelevage-des-poules-pondeuses-et-son-impact-sur-la-vie-economique-dans-la-ville-de-goma-de-2018-29.html |access-date=22 February 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Développement Rural de Goma |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> Primarily centered on the production of [[raw material]]s, including plant agriculture, [[fishing]], [[hunting]], and [[fish farming]], these activities typically employ artisanal methods and old production techniques. Agricultural products are primarily sourced from neighboring [[Masisi Territory]] and [[Rutshuru Territory]], along with resources from [[Lake Kivu]], which hosts thriving [[fish market]]s along its shores twice a week. Cultivation primarily focuses on garden crops and selected [[Staple food|staples]] such as [[legume]]s, [[maize]], and [[tuber]]s.<ref name=":16" /> 

[[File:Lac vert RDC.jpg|thumb|237x237px|Lac Vert of Mount Mugunga in Goma, situated southwest of the [[Mount Nyiragongo|Nyiragongo volcano]] and northeast of [[Lake Kivu]]|left]]
During the colonial period, economic development was encouraged through [[plantation]] farming in North Kivu's fertile highlands, which established the region as a critical "food basket" for the [[Belgian Congo]].<ref name=":33">{{Cite web |last1=Vlassenroot |first1=Koen |last2=Büscher |first2=Karen |date=November 2009 |title=The City as Frontier: Urban Development and Identity Processes in Goma |url=https://www.lse.ac.uk/international-development/Assets/Documents/PDFs/csrc-working-papers-phase-two/wp61.2-city-as-frontier.pdf |access-date=28 December 2024 |website=lse.ac.uk |publisher=[[London School of Economics|London School of Economics and Political Science]] |pages=5–6}}</ref> Legislative frameworks, including the Draft Decree and Royal Decree of 12 December 1939, laid the foundation for agricultural oversight. This initiative culminated in the establishment of OPAC (''Office des Produits Agricoles de Costermansville'') on 4 February 1948, which was subsequently renamed OPAK (''Office des Produits Agricoles du Kivu''; currently known as ''Office Nationale du Café'', ONC).<ref name=":44">{{Cite web |title="AGRI": Service de l'Agriculture |trans-title="AGRI": Agriculture Service |url=https://www.arch.be/docs/invent/archives-africaines/AGRI.pdf |access-date=22 January 2025 |website=[[National Archives of Belgium]] |publisher=[[Minister of the Colonies (Belgium)|Minister of the Colonies]] |pages=32–33 |language=fr}}</ref><ref name=":43" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mirimo |first=Yves Imoa |date=2015 |title=Mise en place d'un système informatisé pour la gestion des produits agricoles prêts à l'exportation: cas de l'office national du café (secteur de Goma) |trans-title=Implementation of a computerized system for the management of agricultural products ready for export: the case of the national coffee office (Goma sector) |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/10/17/10069/m_Mise-en-place-d-un-systeme-informatise-pour-la-gestion-des-produits-agricoles-prts--l-exportat7.html |access-date=23 January 2025 |publisher=Institut Supérieur d'Informatique et de Gestion de Goma |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> These agencies oversaw the production and export of [[Cash crop|cash crops]] such as ''[[Coffea arabica]]'' and [[pyrethrum]].<ref name=":44" /> At that time, large amounts of food products, including [[Grain|grains]], [[root crops]], meat, and [[palm oil]], passed through Goma for redistribution to urban epicenters such as [[Kinshasa]] and [[Kisangani]].<ref name=":33" /> The construction of a port in Kyeshero, later repositioned nearer to central Goma, augmented [[Trade route|trade routes]] by linking the city to a north–south [[economic corridor]] extending through [[Bunia]], Rutshuru, [[Bukavu]], [[Uvira]], and [[Kalemie]].<ref name=":33" /> While the colonial economy also invested in resource extraction, North Kivu's mining sector remained underdeveloped relative to mineral-rich regions like [[Ituri Province|Ituri]] and [[South Kivu]].<ref name=":33" /> Consequently, Goma's prominence as a mineral trading hub was relatively subdued until the 1980s, but trade routes connecting Goma to markets in Uganda and Rwanda remained active and continued to support local commerce after independence.<ref name=":33" />

In the post-independence era, these historical trade networks gained significance as the local population increasingly relied on informal and transborder economic activities to circumvent the exploitative practices of the [[Zaire|Zairean state]].<ref name=":33" /> By the 1980s, a substantial portion of agricultural production, including [[papaya]], [[tea]], ''[[cinchona]]'', and coffee, was smuggled or exported through informal channels, with [[Goma International Airport]] playing a key role in this clandestine commerce.<ref name=":33" /> Estimates from 1985–1986 suggest that up to 60% of local coffee production bypassed formal export systems.<ref name=":33" /> In 2001, the ''Compagnie pour la Promotion des Activités Café'' (COOPAC) was established and headquartered in the Les Volcans ''quartier'' of the [[Goma (commune)|Goma commune]].<ref name=":43" /> It has since become a major organization in the coffee sector in eastern Congo and an integrated coffee processing chain, including a [[Husk|hulling]] facility established in 2004 and a washing station situated along the shores of Lake Kivu.<ref name=":43" /> The city is also home to Maizeking, an industrial enterprise specializing in the manufacturing of products derived from [[Maize|corn]], [[sorghum]], [[Soybean|soybeans]], and [[wheat]].<ref name=":46">{{Cite web |last=Adamo |first=Pierre Divin |date=2018 |title=Analyse de l'offre et de la demande des feuilles de manioc a Goma |trans-title=Analysis of supply and demand for cassava leaves in Goma |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/07/21/11952/m_Analyse-de-loffre-et-de-la-demande-des-feuilles-de-manioc-a-Goma12.html |access-date=7 February 2025 |publisher=[[University of Goma]] |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref>

=== Secondary and tertiary sectors ===
The [[Secondary sector of the economy|secondary sector]] is relatively underdeveloped.<ref name=":16" /> Notable manufacturing enterprises include the MTC (Master Tabac Congo) conglomerate producing premium-grade [[cigarette]]s, coffee processing factories like SOTRAKI and ONC as well as food production companies such as Au Bon Pain and Boulangerie Mont Carmel, which manufacture baked goods.<ref name=":16" /> Other industrial entities include [[Nyiragongo Cement]], a [[cement]] production facility; Mbinza, a [[mattress]] manufacturing company; and La Chocolaterie Lowa, a Congolese [[chocolate]] producer.<ref name=":46" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fula |first=Nadine |date=27 August 2020 |title=RDC: Julien Paluku en visite d'inspection dans les industries du Nord-Kivu bénéficiaires des financements du FPI! |trans-title=DRC: Julien Paluku on an inspection visit to the industries in North Kivu benefiting from FPI funding! |url=https://zoom-eco.net/a-la-une/rdc-julien-paluku-en-visite-dinspection-dans-les-industries-du-nord-kivu-beneficiaires-des-financements-du-fpi/ |access-date=7 February 2025 |website=Zoom-eco.net |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Malu-Malu |first=Muriel Devey |date=21 January 2022 |title=RDC: Alexis Kalinda et les ambitions du chocolat "made in Goma" |trans-title=DRC: Alexis Kalinda and the ambitions of chocolate "made in Goma" |url=https://www.jeuneafrique.com/1274240/economie-entreprises/rdc-alexis-kalinda-et-les-ambitions-du-chocolat-made-in-goma/ |access-date=3 April 2025 |website=[[Jeune Afrique]] |language=fr-FR}}</ref> Additionally, the city has a growing bottled water industry and photographic processing facilities, such as Fujicolor.<ref name=":16" />

[[Financial services|Financial industry]] is significant in the city, with [[bank]]ing and [[Non-bank financial institution|non-banking financial institutions]] serving the population.<ref name=":16" /> Banking institutions like [[Central Bank of the Congo]], Banque Privée du Congo, [[Bank of Africa]], Banque Commerciale et de Développement, Banque Internationale de Crédit, Banque Internationale pour l'Afrique Central, [[Equity Banque Commerciale du Congo]], [[Standard Bank]], First International Bank, [[Trust Merchant Bank]], [[Rawbank]], [[Afriland First Bank]], [[Access Bank plc|Acces Bank]], [[Ecobank Group|Eco Bank]] Democratic Republic of the Congo, and others provide financial services,<ref name=":16" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chiza |first=René Mushamuka |date=2013 |title=Analyse des déterminants de la diversification des produits dans les IMF de la ville de Goma |trans-title=Analysis of the determinants of product diversification in MFIs in the city of Goma |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/11/19/11223/m_Analyse-des-determinants-de-la-diversification-des-produits-dans-les-IMF-de-la-ville-de-Goma23.html |access-date=31 December 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur d'Informatique et de Gestion de Goma |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> while non-banking institutions, including 17 microfinance organizations, fortified with credit components cater to various fiscal needs within the city.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hilditch |first=Simon |date=20 August 2016 |title=Cartographie des institutions et des programmes de microfinance dans les villes frontalières en RDC, au Rwanda et au Burundi |trans-title=Mapping of microfinance institutions and programs in the border towns of Goma-Gisenyi, Bukavu-Kamembe and Uvira-Gatumba, in the DRC, Rwanda and Burundi |url=https://www.international-alert.org/app/uploads/2021/09/DRC-Microfinance-Institutions-FR-2016.pdf |access-date=28 December 2024 |website=[[International Alert]] |page=5 |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Oval, London, England, United Kingdom}}</ref><ref name=":16" /> Notably, microfinance entities like SOMIF/NFT, IMF Hekima, PAIDEK, [[:fr:SMICO|Sociéte de Microcrédit Congolais]], SOMIFI/REJEDE, COOPEC-Imara, COOPEC-Tumanini, and IMF PAIF, as well as NGOs like the Initiative Congolaise pour la Gestion Autonome des Populations (ICGP), the Association of Support for Grassroots Initiatives, Association d'Appui aux Initiatives de Base (APIBA), Organisation des Femmes pour le Développement (OFED), Solidarité et Fraternité dans l'Action, and Association de diabétiques du Congo (ADIC), contribute to economic development by supporting [[Small business|small businesses]] and entrepreneurial ventures.<ref name=":16" /> The city is also home to quasi-public non-bank financial institutions exemplified by [[:fr:Sonas_(république_démocratique_du_Congo)|Société Nationale d'Assurance]] (SONAS), Institution Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (INSS), [[:fr:Caisse_générale_d'épargne_du_Congo|Caisse Générale d'Épargne et de Crédit]] (CADECO), and [[Congolese Posts and Telecommunications Corporation|Société Congolaise des Postes et Télécommunications]] (SCPT).<ref name=":16" />

Goma benefits from support organizations like [[United Nations Development Programme|UNDP]], UWEKI, and CAFED, which foster entrepreneurship, provide training, and facilitate access to resources for local businesses.<ref name=":16" />

=== Tourism ===
Goma is a popular tourist destination and offers a variety of attractions.<ref name=":17" /> [[Virunga National Park]], located north of Goma, boasts more than 3,000 [[fauna]]l and [[Flower|floral]] species.<ref name="Plumptre_al2007">{{cite journal |author1=Plumptre, A. J. |author2=Davenport, T. R. |author3=Behangana, M. |author4=Kityo, R. |author5=Eilu, G. |author6=Ssegawa, P. |author7=Ewango, C. |author8=Meirte, D. |author9=Kahindo, C. |author10=Herremans, M. |author11=Peterhans, J. K. |name-list-style=amp |year=2007 |title=The biodiversity of the Albertine Rift |journal=Biological Conservation |volume=134 |issue=2 |pages=178–194 |bibcode=2007BCons.134..178P |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2006.08.021}}</ref> [[Tchegera Island]] is located southwest of Goma.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Muhima |first=G. B. |date=2023 |title=Lac Kivu : l'île Tchegera, un paradis terrestre |trans-title=Lake Kivu: Tchegera Island, an earthly paradise |url=https://kivumorningpost.cd/2023/05/03/lac-kivu-lile-tchegera-un-paradis-terrestre/ |access-date=13 February 2024 |work=Kivu Morning Post |language=fr-FR}}</ref> The intercultural [[ballet]] has regularly participated in fairs and cultural events, including the annual Goma Tourist Fair (''foire touristique de Goma''; FOTOGO), organized by the National Tourism Office (''Office National du Tourisme''; ONT) since 2007. The troupe has also recently performed at the Goma Agricultural Fair (''foire agricole de Goma''), where they received the FAGOP award.<ref name=":49" />

== Infrastructure ==
{{Multiple images
| image1       = PXL 20221125 133918358~2.jpg
| image2       = 
| footer       = An aerial view of Goma
| footer_align = center
| direction    = horizontal
| total_width  = 230
}}

Urbanization in Goma is in a state of progressive expansion, though the [[cityscape]] remains predominantly characterized by horizontal, [[Low-rise building|low-rise structures]].<ref name=":110" /> Concentrated largely around [[National Road 2 (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|National Road 2]], commercial activity is vigorous, with numerous bars, shops, ''Nganda'' (local eateries), and hotels lining this central corridor.<ref name=":110" /> Major commercial zones such as Supermatch, [[Nyiragongo Cement]], and several key stations like Ihusi, IBB Service, AFRICOM, Ni Yetu, Tout Jeune, and GPI dominate the city's urban landscape.<ref name=":110" />

While low-rise architecture remains the prevailing style due to its affordability and practicality, multi-[[Storey|story]] buildings are beginning to emerge.<ref name=":110" /> Goma's traditional wood board construction, popular due to its speed and cost-efficiency, is increasingly complemented by more durable vertical structures, which require significantly more extended construction periods due to the materials and techniques involved.<ref name=":110" />

One of the most notable developments in Goma is the Birere ''quartier'', also known as Mikeno.<ref name=":333">{{Cite web |last1=Vlassenroot |first1=Koen |last2=Büscher |first2=Karen |date=November 2009 |title=The City as Frontier: Urban Development and Identity Processes in Goma |url=https://www.lse.ac.uk/international-development/Assets/Documents/PDFs/csrc-working-papers-phase-two/wp61.2-city-as-frontier.pdf |access-date=28 December 2024 |website=lse.ac.uk |publisher=[[London School of Economics|London School of Economics and Political Science]] |pages=9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kitwanda |first=Samuel Habamungu |date=2015 |title=L'internet et son impact dans les organisations de Goma, cas spécifique de la RVA Goma |trans-title=The Internet and its impact on Goma organizations, specific case of RVA Goma |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/12/21/12503/m_Linternet-et-son-impact-dans-les-organisations-de-Goma-cas-specifique-de-la-RVA-Goma9.html |access-date=30 December 2024 |publisher=Université du CEPROMAD (UNIC–GOMA) |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> The area, located within the [[Goma (commune)|Goma commune]], is recognized as the city's oldest residential ''quartier''. It is characterized by its multi-ethnic demographic and serves as a focal point for informal cross-border trade, housing numerous stores, warehouses, restaurants, and popular clubs known as '''ngandas''<nowiki/>'.<ref name=":333" /> Birere occupies part of the "''zone tampon''", the neutral buffer zone between DRC and Rwanda, and remains a key location for economic activity, despite numerous efforts to shift the city's commercial heart to safer areas after the 2002 Nyiragongo volcanic eruption.<ref name=":333" /> The presence of the "''petite barrière''", a pedestrian border crossing, facilitates the illicit trade of small goods and provides a source of income for many Congolese and Rwandans.<ref name=":333" />

==== Air ====
[[Aviation]] is a significant transport mode linking Goma with [[Domestic flight|domestic]] and [[International flight|international]] destinations. [[Goma International Airport]], which serves as the city's principal gateway, handles passenger and cargo traffic and facilitates two international routes to [[Entebbe]] and [[Nairobi]], serviced by [[Ethiopian Airlines]] and [[Jambojet]].<ref name=":17">{{Cite web |last=Kwiraviwe |first=Jonas Muhindo |title=Chapitre I: Descripion de la ville de Goma |trans-title=Chapter I: Description of the city of Goma |url=https://www.africmemoire.com/part.3-chapitre-i-descripion-de-la-ville-de-goma-1055.html |access-date=27 February 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Développement Rural des Grands Lacs (ISDR-GL) |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Conbgo}}</ref> The aviation industry in Goma has changed over the years with the emergence and departure of carriers. While enterprises such as Virunga Air, Charter, and [[Sunair]] have ceased operations, stalwart aviation entities like société de Transports et Messageries au Kivu SARL (TMK), alongside [[Wimbi Dira Airways]] and [[Hewa Bora Airways]] persist in operating and rendering their services.<ref name=":17" />

==== Maritime ====
{{Multiple image
| image1        = La ville de Goma.png
| image2        = 
| footer        = 
| total_width   = 200
| direction     = vertical
| footer_align  = center
| caption1      = A view of Goma taken from the port
| caption_align = center
| align         = left
}}

[[Maritime transport]] connects Goma with nearby cities like [[Bukavu]] in the [[South Kivu|South Kivu Province]]. Boats and ferries operated by companies such as the ''[[Société nationale des chemins de fer du Congo|Société Nationale des Chemins de fer du Congo]]'' (SNCC) and private operators like Rafiki and Ihusi Hotel facilitate the movement of people and [[merchandise]] goods across Lake Kivu.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Karumba |first=Janvier Bagula |date=2011 |title=De l'opportunité du développement du tourisme au nord Kivu. Cas de la ville de Goma |trans-title=The opportunity for tourism development in North Kivu. Case of the city of Goma |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/01/14/8505/m_De-l-opportunite-du-developpement-du-tourisme-au-nord-Kivu-Cas-de-la-ville-de-Goma27.html |access-date=27 February 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Tourisme de Goma (ISTou-Goma) |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref><ref name=":17" /> Notably, boats such as Emmanuel 2, assembled locally, provide an alternative mode of transport, significantly reducing travel time compared to road travel.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=12 July 2018 |title=Lake Kivu becomes major transport hub |url=https://www.africanews.com/2018/07/12/lake-kivu-becomes-major-transport-hub/ |access-date=27 February 2024 |website=[[Africanews]] |publication-place=Lyon, France}}</ref>

==== Road ====
{{Multiple image
| image1       = Avenue des orchidées vue du sud-ouest.jpg
| image2       = 
| footer       = A road in Goma
| total_width  = 200
| direction    = vertical
| footer_align = center
}}

[[Road transport]], presided over by private operators, is vital for intra-city and inter-city travel, encompassing a network of paved and unpaved routes.<ref name=":17" /><ref name=":110">{{Cite web |last=John |first=Luendo Malira |date=September 2018 |title=Essai d'etude sur le reamenagement urbain de la ville de Goma |trans-title=Study essay on the urban redevelopment of the city of Goma |url=https://www.istougoma.ac.cd/pdf/publication/642ac6221e32a.pdf |access-date=4 October 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Tourisme de Goma (ISTOU-Goma) |pages=27–30 |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> [[National Road 2 (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|National Road No. 2]] bisects the urban landscape, supplemented by smaller road segments, though their cumulative length is at most three kilometers.<ref name=":110" /> The city's road transport system comprises various vehicles, including car, trucks, buses and motorcycles, with car and motorcycle taxis facilitating the majority of shuttle services.<ref name=":110" /> 

Car taxis, often referred to as city taxis, are predominantly used for [[passenger transport]], while luggage taxis cater to the movement of goods. Motorcycle taxis, commonly employed for passenger and small package deliveries, play a vital role in local mobility.<ref name=":110" /> Goma's location on the Rwandan border ensures its connectivity to [[Gisenyi]], with regular bus services facilitating travel between Goma and [[Kigali]] in less than four hours.<ref name=":17" /> 

Goma's road network connects to [[Masisi, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Masisi]], [[Walikale]], [[Kisangani]], [[Rutshuru]], [[Butembo]], [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[Kasindi]], [[Bunia]], and [[Bukavu]], among other destinations. Motorcycles operate day and night, with different drivers serving distinct shifts.<ref name=":1102">{{Cite web |last=John |first=Luendo Malira |date=September 2018 |title=Essai d'etude sur le reamenagement urbain de la ville de Goma |trans-title=Study essay on the urban redevelopment of the city of Goma |url=https://www.istougoma.ac.cd/pdf/publication/642ac6221e32a.pdf |access-date=4 October 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Tourisme de Goma (ISTOU-Goma) |page=27 |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> Although major roads in Goma have improved, some residential avenues remain underdeveloped. Numerous roads are obstructed, either by improperly constructed homes, mountains of discarded waste, or incomplete construction projects.<ref name=":1102" />

=== Mobile networks and media ===
Goma offers [[cellular network]] services such as [[Supercell (mobile network)|SuperCell]], [[Bharti Airtel|Airtel]], [[Vodacom]], [[Orange RDC]] (formerly ''Congo Chine Télécoms''), and [[Millicom|Tigo]], which facilitate communication exchanges locally and internationally and play an integral role in business transactions, [[Social relation|social interactions]], and [[emergency service]]s.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Buchekabiri |first=Ephrem Chiruza |date=2013 |title=Analyse de la population de la ville de goma sur les programmes de la radio television communautaire Tayna Â« rtct Â» 2011–2012 |trans-title=Analysis of the population of the city of Goma on the programs of the community radio television Tayna "rtct" 2011–2012 |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/01/17/9500/m_Analyse-de-la-population-de-la-ville-de-goma-sur-les-programmes-de-la-radio-television-communautaire4.html |access-date=13 February 2024 |publisher=Université du CEPROMAD |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref>

The city has a variety of [[Swahili language|Swahili]], [[Lingala]], and [[French language|French]] language radio stations, including [[Radio-Télévision nationale congolaise|RTNC Goma]], [[Radio Okapi]], RSI (''Radio Sauti'' ''ya Injili''), Radio La Colombe, RTCT (''Radio Télévision Communautaire Taina''), RTC (''Radio Télévision la Colombe''), Kivu 1, Mishapi Voice TV, Mutaani, RSM (''Radio Sauti'' ''ya Matumaini''), VBR (Virunga Business Radio), Pool FM, RAO FM (Radio Alpha Omega), COMICO, Emmanuel TV, and Source de Vie, offering various news, [[entertainment]], [[Religious broadcasting|religious programming]], and cultural content.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":43" />

== Crime ==
{{Multiple image
| image1       = 
| image2       = Joint Patrol UNPOL, FARDC, and PNC - 20 May 20 Goma, DRC (49919593692).jpg
| footer       = As part of efforts to secure Goma and its surrounding areas, a joint 19-hour night patrol was conducted in May 2020 by [[United Nations Police]], the [[Congolese National Police]], and the [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo]].
| total_width  = 240
| footer_align = center
}}

Since early 2019, violent crimes such as [[murder]]s, [[Robbery|robberies]], and [[kidnapping]]s have plagued outlying ''quartiers'', notably [[Ndosho]] and Mugunga in [[Karisimbi (commune)|Karisimbi commune]].<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last1=Hendriks |first1=Maarten |last2=Büscher |first2=Karen |date=September 2019 |title=Insecurity in Goma: Experiences, actors and responses |url=https://riftvalley.net/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/Insecurity-in-Goma-by-Maarten-Hendriks-and-Karen-Buscher-RVI-Usalama-Project-2019.pdf |access-date=2024-03-02 |website=Riftvalley.net |publisher=Rift Valley Institute |pages=22–27 |publication-place=Nairobi, Kenya}}</ref> Ndosho, known for its bustling [[Marketplace|markets]] and [[brothel]]s, is characterized by high crime rates and [[Ethnic conflict|ethnic heterogeneity]], while Mugunga, predominantly populated by [[Hutu]]s, formerly hosted extensive refugee camps in the aftermath of the [[Rwandan genocide]], alongside sizable [[internally displaced persons|IDPs]] settlements during periods of heightened conflict between the [[National Congress for the Defence of the People|CNDP]] (and subsequently [[M23 rebellion (2012–2013)|M23]]) and the [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|FARDC]] from 2008 to 2010 and 2012 to 2013.<ref name=":22" /> Although the camps have been dismantled, the ''quartier'' is characterized by a high number of former IDPs ([[Hunde people|Hunde]] and Hutu) who settled in Mugunga. Both ''quartiers'' border [[Virunga National Park]] to the north and the main road to [[Sake, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Sake]] to the south, dividing the [[Goma (commune)|Goma]] and [[Karisimbi (commune)|Karisimbi]] communes, with diurnal activities centered along this road.<ref name=":22" />

A significant number of Mugunga's inhabitants, including [[Brigandage|brigands]] and ''maibobo'' ([[street children]]), gravitate towards Ndosho during daylight hours, lured by its superior commercial prospects. Throughout the day, encounters with insecurity primarily revolve around [[pickpocketing]], [[extortion]] by ''maibobo'', [[gang]]-related [[harassment]], and coercive measures employed by security personnel in Ndosho.<ref name=":22" /> Brigandage and petty crime have evolved into a viable means of subsistence for many and are part of an urban economy of survival and enrichment. Pilfered [[Merchandising|merchandise]] goods are openly sold in the markets, with numerous criminals attaining notoriety within their ''quartiers'' and certain gang leaders achieving city-wide renown.<ref name=":22" /> 

During the night, security conditions worsen and become more violent. Most residents return to their homes, while mixed patrols of the [[Congolese National Police|Police Nationale Congolaise]] (PNC) and Police Militaire (PM) units, along with gangs, prowl around the streets. Without [[pedestrian]] [[traffic]] and under the cloak of darkness, it becomes easier for bandits, thieves, and even unscrupulous police and military officers to operate.<ref name=":22" />

== Internally displaced populations ==
{{Multiple image
| image1      = Rwandan refugee camp in east Zaire.jpg
| caption1    = Refugee camp for displaced Rwandans in Kimbumba, 20 km from Goma, Zaire, following the 1994 [[Rwandan genocide]]
| image2      = Kibumba refugee camp at Goma, 6506675, 330-CFD-DF-ST-99-05606.jpg
| caption2    = Kibumba refugee camp in Goma on August 3, 1994. Approximately 1.2 million Rwandan refugees fled to Zaire following the outbreak of the [[Rwandan Civil War]].
| image3      = 1994 refugee camp near Goma 22 August DF-ST-98-00484.jpeg
| caption3    = Refugee camp near Goma, Zaire, 1994, providing shelter to those fleeing the Rwandan Civil War.
| total_width = 200
| perrow      = 1
}}

For over three decades, Goma has served as a major site for [[internally displaced person]]s (IDPs), predominantly due to the recurrent waves of violence and humanitarian emergencies besieging the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and adjacent regions.<ref name=":28">{{Cite news |last1=Bashizi |first1=Arlette |last2=Kitsa |first2=Fidèle |date=4 April 2024 |title=Crowded camps and local aid: How DR Congo's M23 conflict is impacting Goma |url=https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/news-feature/2024/04/04/crowded-camps-and-local-aid-how-dr-congos-m23-conflict-impacting-goma |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=[[The New Humanitarian]] |location=Geneva, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Living Conditions of displaced persons and host communities in urban Goma, DRC |url=https://www.nrc.no/globalassets/pdf/reports/living-conditions-of-displaced-persons-and-host-communities-in-urban-goma-drc.pdf |website=[[Norwegian Refugee Council]] |page=6 |publication-place=Oslo, Norway}}</ref> The displacement crisis commenced in the aftermath of the 1994 [[Rwandan genocide]], during which approximately 1.2 million refugees,<ref>{{Cite web |title=10The Rwandan genocide and its aftermath |url=https://www.unhcr.org/sites/default/files/legacy-pdf/3ebf9bb60.pdf |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] |page=2 (246) |publication-place=Geneva, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland}}</ref> predominantly Hutus, entered eastern Congo, with between 500,000 and 850,000 people arriving in Goma over a span of five days in mid-July 1994.<ref name=":29">{{Citation |last1=Migration |first1=National Research Council (US) Roundtable on the Demography of Forced |title=The Evolution of Mortality Among Rwandan Refugees in Zaire Between 1994 and 1997 |date=2001 |work=Forced Migration & Mortality |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK223348/ |access-date=13 November 2024 |publisher=National Academies Press (US) |language=en |last2=Reed |first2=Holly E. |last3=Keely |first3=Charles B.}}</ref> This mass migration was one of the largest cross-border movements in recent history, with many refugees establishing makeshift camps around Goma.<ref name=":29" />

The late 1990s witnessed a surge in the IDP crisis amidst the First and Second Congo Wars, with hundreds of thousands fleeing escalating rural violence and relocating to Goma and its environs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 October 2020 |title=The DR Congo Crisis: many tragedies combined |url=https://www.worldvision.ca/stories/dr-congo-crisis-facts-and-how-to-help |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=Worldvision.ca |language=en-CA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 October 2024 |title=Why is the Democratic Republic of Congo wracked by conflict? |url=https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/campaigns/2024/10/why-is-the-democratic-republic-of-congo-wracked-by-conflict/ |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[Amnesty International]] |language=en |publication-place=London, England, United Kingdom}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2000 |title=Democratic Republic of Congo Update Dec 2000 – Democratic Republic of the Congo |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/democratic-republic-congo-update-dec-2000 |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[ReliefWeb]] |language=en |publication-place=New York, New York, United States}}</ref> By December 2006, estimates suggested at least 80,000 IDPs resided within and around the city,<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 September 2007 |title=Situation sécuritaire toujours préoccupante au Nord Kivu |trans-title=Security situation still worrying in North Kivu |url=https://www.radiookapi.net/emissions-2/dialogue-entre-congolais/2007/09/12/situation-securitaire-toujours-preoccupante-au-nord-kivu |access-date=8 November 2024 |website=[[Radio Okapi]] |language=fr}}</ref> a figure that escalated to roughly 640,000 by September 2007 in camps dispersed across North Kivu.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 September 2007 |title=Situation sécuritaire toujours préoccupante au Nord Kivu |trans-title=Security situation still worrying in North Kivu |url=https://www.radiookapi.net/emissions-2/dialogue-entre-congolais/2007/09/12/situation-securitaire-toujours-preoccupante-au-nord-kivu |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[Radio Okapi]] |language=fr}}</ref> Another spike in displacement transpired between 2012 and 2013, correlating with the [[March 23 Movement|emergence of M23]]. During this period, more than 500,000 people sought refuge in Goma.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Beytrison |first1=Fran |last2=Kalis |first2=Olivia |date=May 2023 |title=Repeated displacement in eastern DRC |url=https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:bc0fa2ef-e96b-4e42-a1dd-8f5dfb847ac0/download_file?file_format=pdf&safe_filename=beytrison-kalis%2B-%2BEnglish.pdf&type_of_work=Journal+article |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=Ora.ox.ac.uk |page=1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 April 2013 |title=Global Overview 2012: People internally displaced by conflict and violence – Democratic Republic of the Congo |url=https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/idmc/2013/en/34734 |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=RefWorld |language=en}}</ref> 

The [[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]], which involved the M23, the FARDC, and other armed groups across North Kivu, has forced an estimated 1.1 million people from their homes as of 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2023 |title=UNICEF: DR-Congo Humanitarian |url=https://www.unicef.org/media/151311/file/DR-Congo-Humanitarian-SitRep-(L3-Emergency-Scale-Up),-31-December-2023.pdf |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=Unicef.org |publisher=[[UNICEF]] |page=1 |publication-place=New York, New York, United States}}</ref> with over 600,000 seeking refuge in severely overcrowded and unsanitary displacement camps around Goma.<ref name=":23" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 February 2024 |title=Humanitarian emergency in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu (DRC): A worsening crisis in 2024 – Democratic Republic of the Congo |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/humanitarian-emergency-ituri-north-kivu-and-south-kivu-drc-worsening-crisis-2024#:~:text=Approximately%201.7%20million%20people%20are,in%20Goma,%20the%20provincial%20capital. |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[ReliefWeb]] |publisher=[[World Food Programme]] |language=en |publication-place=Rome, Italy}}</ref> The [[M23 campaign (2022–present)#2025 Goma and Bukavu offensives|2025 M23 offensives toward Goma and Bukavu]] generated widespread insecurity, economic disruption, shortages of basic goods, and severe limitations on movement, a situation that was also aggravated by orders from ''[[de facto]]'' authorities to dismantle IDP camps that forced repeated displacement. A rapid multisectoral assessment carried out by [[Tearfund]] in April 2025 examined humanitarian conditions among IDPs in the health zones of Baraka, Mugunga, Mugunga 3, Buhimba, Munigi, and Kanyaruchinya, spanning Goma and the neighboring [[Nyiragongo Territory]].<ref name=":47">{{Cite web |date=April 2025 |title=Ville de Goma: Aires de sante de Baraka, Mugunga, Mugunga 3 et Buhimba et en territoire de Nyiragongo: Aires de sante de Munigi et Kanyaruchinya, du 14 au 17 avril 2025 |trans-title=City of Goma: Health areas of Baraka, Mugunga, Mugunga 3 and Buhimba and in Nyiragongo Territory: Health areas of Munigi and Kanyaruchinya from 14 to 17 April 2025 |url=https://ehtools.org/uploads/brochures/1615.pdf |access-date=25 December 2025 |website=Ehtools.org |publisher=[[Tearfund]] |pages=1–19 |language=fr |publication-place=Teddington, UK}}</ref> The assessment identified 43 active "collective centers" hosting 2,263 displaced households, approximately 11,950 individuals, primarily concentrated in Goma and Karisimbi communes as well as in Nyiragongo Territory, with particularly high concentrations in Mugunga, Mugunga 3, Buhimba, Baraka, [[Bukumu Chiefdom#Groupements|Munigi]], [[Bukumu Chiefdom#Groupements|Rusayo]], and Kanyaruchinya. Some of the largest sites, often churches or schools, were sheltering more than 1,000 people, while approximately one quarter of displaced households were hosted by local families.<ref name=":47" />

=== Cholera, dysentery outbreaks, and malnutrition ===
[[File:Kibativillagers.jpg|thumb|Kibati villagers fleeing gunfire in a camp for internally displaced persons during the [[2008 Nord-Kivu war]]|201x201px|left]]
The initial influx of refugees in July 1994 saw an immediate health emergency, as overcrowded camps lacked [[Water pollution|clean water]], [[sanitation]], and hygiene facilities. The first case of cholera was diagnosed on 20 July 1994, leading to a major outbreak within the camps that saw an estimated 58,000 to 80,000 cases in less than a month.<ref name=":29" /> Concurrently, an outbreak of bloody [[diarrhea]] caused by ''[[Shigella dysenteriae]]'' type 1 emerged in early August, persisting in the camps until November. These outbreaks contributed to unprecedented mortality rates during the first month of the emergency, with an estimated 50,000 deaths recorded between mid-July and mid-August.<ref name=":29" />

The influx also led to severe [[food security|food insecurity]] among IDPs, resulting in widespread malnutrition, particularly affecting children. Goma's already fragile health infrastructure struggled to meet these needs, as ongoing conflict limited resources and disrupted supply chains.<ref name=":30">{{Cite journal |date=11 February 1995 |title=Public health impact of Rwandan refugee crisis: what happened in Goma, Zaire, in July, 1994? Goma Epidemiology Group |journal=Lancet |volume=345 |issue=8946 |pages=339–344 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(95)90338-0 |issn=0140-6736 |pmid=7646638}}</ref><ref name=":31">{{Cite web |last1=Dowell |first1=Scott F. |last2=Toko |first2=Alphonse |last3=Sita |first3=Claire |last4=Piarroux |first4=Renaud |last5=Duerr |first5=Ann |last6=Woodruff |first6=Bradley A. |date=14 June 1995 |title=Health and Nutrition in Centers for Unaccompanied Refugee Children: Experience From the 1994 Rwandan Refugee Crisis |url=https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/388857 |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=Jamanetwork.com |publisher=[[JAMA Network Open]] |publication-place=Chicago, Illinois, United States}}</ref> Many displaced families lacked access to sufficient food, and local health services were ill-equipped to address the scale of malnutrition.<ref name=":30" /><ref name=":31" />

Between January 2000 and December 2007, cholera remained a persistent threat in North and South Kivu, with 73,605 reported cases and 1,612 deaths, resulting in a [[lethality]] rate of 2.2%.<ref name=":32">{{Cite journal |last1=Bompangue |first1=Didier |last2=Giraudoux |first2=Patrick |last3=Piarroux |first3=Martine |last4=Mutombo |first4=Guy |last5=Shamavu |first5=Rick |last6=Sudre |first6=Bertrand |last7=Mutombo |first7=Annie |last8=Mondonge |first8=Vital |last9=Piarroux |first9=Renaud |date=19 May 2009 |title=Cholera Epidemics, War and Disasters around Goma and Lake Kivu: An Eight-Year Survey |journal=PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases |publication-place=San Francisco, California, United States |volume=3 |issue=5 |page=3 |doi=10.1371/journal.pntd.0000436 |pmc=2677153 |pmid=19436726 |doi-access=free}}</ref> In North Kivu, the cholera strains identified included ''[[Vibrio cholerae]]'' O1 El Tor Ogawa and Inaba, with the latter being exclusive to South Kivu.<ref name=":32" /> Annual cholera outbreaks peaked at over 700 cases per week, particularly affecting health districts bordering lakes. Despite the severity of these outbreaks, between January and April 2002, only 140 cholera cases were reported across Goma, with no fatalities, a significant deviation from the city's typical average of 29 cases weekly for that period.<ref name=":32" /> 

=== Mental health, nutritional challenges, and recent health crises ===
[[File:USG for Humanitarian Affairs, Valerie Amos visits IDP camp of Kanyaruchinya (7746996610).jpg|thumb|Food rations unloaded from trucks at the Kanyaruchinya IDP camp, located on the outskirts of Goma|205x205px]]
In 2012, nearly 1 million children in the Democratic Republic of the Congo were estimated to suffer from acute malnutrition, with North Kivu being particularly affected.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 November 2012 |title=Press Conference on Humanitarian Aid Efforts in Democratic Republic of the Congo |url=https://press.un.org/en/2012/121105_ocha.doc.htm |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=Press United Nations Un.org |publication-place=New York, New York, United States}}</ref> Food shortages also hindered access to adequate nutrition for IDPs.<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 November 2012 |title=Besoins humanitaires croissants à Goma |trans-title=Growing humanitarian needs in Goma |url=https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/fr/actualites/2012/11/28/besoins-humanitaires-croissants-goma |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=[[The New Humanitarian]] |language=fr |publication-place=Geneva, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 November 2012 |title=Nord Kivu l'interminable cauchemar pour des milliers de déplacés congolais |trans-title=North Kivu the endless nightmare for thousands of displaced Congolese |url=https://www.caritas.org/2012/11/nord-kivu-linterminable-cauchemar-pour-des-milliers-de-deplaces-congolais/?lang=fr |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[Caritas Internationalis]] |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Vatican City}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 November 2012 |title=RDC: l'ONU annonce la reprise de l'aide humanitaire à Goma {{!}} ONU Info |trans-title=DRC: UN announces resumption of humanitarian aid to Goma |url=https://news.un.org/fr/story/2012/11/257512 |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=News.un.org |language=fr |publication-place=New York, New York, United States}}</ref> Continuous exposure to violence and trauma led to pervasive [[mental health]] issues, including [[anxiety]], [[Depression (mood)|depression]], and [[post-traumatic stress disorder]] (PTSD), with limited mental health support available in the region.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Hatcher |first1=Jessica |last2=Hatcher-Moore |first2=Jessica |date=5 November 2013 |title=Eastern Congo grapples with mental health catastrophe after years of war |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2013/nov/05/eastern-congo-mental-health-catastrophe-brutality |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |publication-place=Kings Place, London, England, United Kingdom |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=14 February 2013 |title=Urgent need of assistance for displaced Congolese suffering from mental disorders |url=https://www.caritas.org/2013/02/rutshurunorthkivu/ |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=[[Caritas Internationalis]] |language=en-US |publication-place=Vatican City}}</ref>

From 2016 to 2022, the recurring conflicts and subsequent displacements in Goma worsened the health crisis, with recurrent outbreaks of communicable diseases such as cholera, measles, and a resurgence of malaria.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=13 March 2020 |title=La République Démocratique du Congo face à une grande épidémie de choléra |trans-title=The Democratic Republic of Congo faces a major cholera epidemic |url=https://www.solidarites.org/fr/pays/r-d-congo/la-republique-democratique-du-congo-face-a-une-grande-epidemie-de-cholera/ |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[Solidarités international]] |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Clichy, Hauts-de-Seine, France}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kombi |first=Jonathan |date=31 August 2019 |title=RDC: António Guterres évoque à Goma la rougeole, la malaria, le choléra et Ebola parmi les défis |trans-title=DRC: António Guterres mentions measles, malaria, cholera and Ebola among the challenges in Goma |url=https://actualite.cd/2019/08/31/rdc-antonio-guterres-evoque-goma-la-rougeole-la-malaria-le-cholera-et-ebola-parmi-les |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[Actualite.cd]] |language=fr |publication-place=Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=République démocratique du Congo: l'urgence permanente |trans-title=Democratic Republic of Congo: the permanent emergency |url=https://www.msf.fr/decryptages/republique-democratique-du-congo-l-urgence-permanente |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[Médecins Sans Frontières]] |language=fr}}</ref> Overcrowded and unsanitary conditions within IDP camps facilitated the spread of these diseases, and resulted in high morbidity and mortality rates. The [[COVID-19 pandemic]] also intensified health challenges for IDPs, as healthcare systems became severely strained and limited access to treatment and vaccination. IDPs were particularly vulnerable to severe COVID-19 outcomes due to overcrowded conditions and insufficient health resources.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 September 2020 |title=Lutter contre le covid-19 : Caritas Développement-Goma distribue des savons à 1.578 ménages dans les sites des déplacés – Democratic Republic of the Congo |trans-title=Fight against covid-19: Caritas Développement-Goma distributes soap to 1,578 households in displaced persons sites |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/lutter-contre-le-covid-19-caritas-d-veloppement-goma-distribue-des |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[ReliefWeb]] |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020 |title=Rapport d'enquete cap sur le COVID-19 dans la ville de Goma du 5 au 10 Avril 2020 |trans-title=Investigation report on COVID-19 in the city of Goma from April 5 to 10, 2020 |url=https://spherestandards.org/wp-content/uploads/BIFERD-rapport-covid19.pdf |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=Spherestandards.org |pages=1–13 |language=fr}}</ref> As of June 14, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reported 782 confirmed cases of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, with Goma identified as a key area of concern.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2026 |title=Ebola Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: Situation Report 14 June 2026 |url=https://www.who.int/emergencies/situations/ebola-drc-2026 |access-date=13 November 2024 |website=[[World Health Organization]]}}</ref> During this outbreak, medical teams in Goma faced significant mistrust from relatives of victims.<ref>{{Cite video |date=14 June 2026 |title=Medical teams in Goma face mistrust from relatives of Ebola victims |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/6/14/medical-teams-in-goma-face-mistrust-from-relatives-of-ebola-victims |access-date=13 November 2024 |work=[[Al Jazeera]]}}</ref>

=== Sexual violence ===
{{Further|Sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo}}

The conflict has been accompanied by a sharp rise in [[Sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo|gender-based violence]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 August 2024 |title=En RDC, une jeune femme sur dix victime de viol durant les cinq derniers mois dans les camps de déplacés de Goma |trans-title=In the DRC, one in ten young women has been raped in the last five months in the displaced persons camps in Goma |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/afrique/article/2024/08/06/en-rdc-une-jeune-femme-sur-dix-victime-de-viol-durant-les-cinq-derniers-mois-dans-les-camps-de-deplaces-de-goma_6270470_3212.html |access-date=26 October 2024 |work=[[Le Monde]] |location=Paris, France |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Blanchard |first=Sandrine |date=1 October 2024 |title=Une femme sur dix est victime de viol dans l'est de la RDC |trans-title=One in ten women are victims of rape in eastern DRC |url=https://www.dw.com/fr/rdc-violences-sexuelles-d%C3%A9plac%C3%A9s-camps-goma-appel-msf/a-70378591 |access-date=26 October 2024 |website=[[DW News]] |language=fr |publication-place=Bonn, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 August 2024 |title=Violences sexuelles en RDC: 10% des femmes déplacées dans les camps de Goma déclarent avoir été violées |trans-title=Sexual violence in the DRC: 10% of displaced women in Goma camps report having been raped |url=https://actualite.cd/2024/08/06/violences-sexuelles-en-rdc-10-des-femmes-deplacees-dans-les-camps-de-goma-declarent |access-date=26 October 2024 |website=[[Actualite.cd]] |language=fr |publication-place=Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> Armed groups, local militias, and, at times, even some members of state forces have been implicated in sexual violence against civilians.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Kiakuvue |first1=Yannick Nkiambi |last2=Kanyere |first2=Furaha Siwatula |last3=Mukubu |first3=Doris Mwila |last4=Ruhindiza |first4=Bienvenu Mukuku |last5=Mukuku |first5=Olivier |date=27 June 2024 |title=Sexual violence among female survivors in Goma, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: epidemiology, clinical features, and circumstances of occurrence |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=14863 |bibcode=2024NatSR..1414863K |doi=10.1038/s41598-024-65412-7  |doi-access=free|issn=2045-2322 |pmc=11211468 |pmid=38937549}}</ref> Such violations are often weaponized as a deliberate tool of war to terrorize communities, assert control, and break down social cohesion.<ref name=":2" /> Survivors often face physical [[Injury|injuries]], [[sexually transmitted infection]]s, [[psychological trauma]], and [[social stigma]]. A 2007 study revealed that around 1.69–1.80 million women aged 15–29 in the DRC reported experiencing [[sexual assault]] at some point in their lives, with North Kivu recording 223,262 cases, the highest rate nationally.<ref name=":2" /> 2010 research indicated that 39.7% of women in North and South Kivu had experienced sexual violence.<ref name=":2" /> 

In 2023, [[Médecins Sans Frontières]] (MSF) reported a sharp increase in sexual violence cases in the DRC, mainly concentrated in and around Goma. MSF treated 25,166 survivors nationwide, averaging more than two patients per hour.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2024 |title=MSF reports unprecedented number of sexual violence cases in DR Congo |url=https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/msf-reports-unprecedented-number-sexual-violence-cases-dr-congo#:~:text=The%20report%20outlines%20that,in%20admissions.&text=than%20two%20patients%20every,in%20admissions.&text=projects%20set%20up%20by,in%20admissions.&text=In%20the%20three%20preceding,in%20admissions |access-date=26 October 2024 |website=[[Médecins Sans Frontières]] |language=en}}</ref> Between 17 and 30 April 2023, [[Médecins Sans Frontières]] treated 674 survivors of sexual violence in camps such as Bulengo, Lushagala, and Rusayo, including 360 cases recorded in Rusayo alone, a recently created and densely populated site west of Goma.<ref name=":23" /> The majority of victims were attacked while outside the camps searching for essential resources, and access to cash has been cut off as banks no longer operate under M23 control.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Rebels took eastern Congo's largest city. Now they must run it. |url=https://www.csmonitor.com/World/Africa/2025/0430/congo-m23-rwanda-goma-peace-deal |access-date=17 May 2025 |work=[[The Christian Science Monitor]] |publisher=Boston, Massachusetts, United States |issn=0882-7729}}</ref> In the first five months of 2024 alone, MSF treated 17,363 survivors in North Kivu, representing 69% of the total cases treated across five provinces in the previous year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2024 |title=MSF reports unprecedented number of sexual violence cases in DR Congo |url=https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/latest/msf-reports-unprecedented-number-sexual-violence-cases-dr-congo#:~:text=This%20trend%20accelerated%20in,provinces%20studied.&text=province%20alone,%2017,363%20victims,provinces%20studied.&text=and%20May.%20Not%20even,provinces%20studied.&text=percent%20of%20the%20total,provinces%20studied |access-date=26 October 2024 |website=[[Médecins Sans Frontières]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== Medical literature, demographics, and medical treatment ====
[[File:UN Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Region visit in Goma (8695464935).jpg|thumb|[[Mary Robinson]], [[Special Envoy of the Secretary-General|United Nation Special Envoy]] for the [[African Great Lakes|African Great Lake Region]], meets with victims of sexual violence at Heal Africa's hospital in Goma]]
Despite substantial media coverage, sexual violence within the DRC remains insufficiently addressed in [[medical literature]]. A study conducted in Goma from 2013 to 2017 revealed that sexual violence disproportionately affected females below 18 years, with an average age of 16.5 years.<ref name=":2" /> Half of the perpetrators were known to the survivors; 12% of survivors tested positive for pregnancy, and 43% received [[emergency contraception]].<ref name=":2" />

In a separate study covering January 2019 to December 2020, [[Karisimbi (commune)|Karisimbi]] municipality in Goma reported 551 cases of sexual violence, while the [[Goma (commune)|Goma]] municipality recorded 149 cases.<ref name=":2" /> The Majengo neighborhood in Karisimbi reported the highest frequency, with 129 cases.<ref name=":2" /> Among the survivors, women aged 20–29 represented 28.6%, with only 15.7% reporting incidents occurring within their homes, and 60.7% of incidents involved the use of weapons.<ref name=":2" /> 

[[Vaginal trauma|Vaginal assault]] occurred in all cases, and other forms of assault, like touching, occurred in 7.2% of cases. Strangers constituted 64.7% of the perpetrators, and 61.4% of assailants were identified as members of military or police forces.<ref name=":2" /> Among survivors, 8.1% had a [[physical disability]]. Of the 700 survivors, only 16.1% sought [[Doctor's visit|medical consultation]] for [[Genital trauma|genital injuries]], and 0.7% presented with [[Muteness|mutism]].<ref name=":2" /> Approximately 60.6% sought [[Health care|medical care]] within 72 hours, with 8.1% testing positive for [[HIV]].<ref name=":2" /> Of the survivors, 76.3% underwent [[pregnancy test]]s, 6.4% of which were positive. Additionally, 55.4% of survivors received [[Birth control|contraception]], and 91.1% were offered [[Post-exposure prophylaxis|post-exposure prophylactic]] treatment for HIV.<ref name=":2" />

== Culture ==
[[File:Bintu Keita at the Amani Festival in 2022.jpg|thumb|[[Bintou Keita]] at the Amani Festival]]
Goma is home of the annual [[Festival Amani]] which celebrates peace; in 2020, it attracted an audience of 36,000.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020 |title=Amani Festival: The DR Congo music festival celebrating life |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-51543822 |access-date=5 February 2022 |work=BBC News}}</ref>
Goma serves as the [[North Kivu]]'s [[cultural center]] and has a vibrant entertainment and performing arts scene that encompasses various media forms, including television productions, radio broadcasts, theatre, cinematic expressions, multimedia installations, and print publications.<ref name=":5" />

Like many cities in DRC, Goma is known for its music scene with popular genres such as [[soukous]], [[Congolese rumba]], [[ndombolo]], and [[Jazz]].<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2024 |title=Festival Amani (Goma RDC): Jazz Music |url=https://amanifestival.com/fr/artiste/jazz-music-2 |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Amanifestival.com |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> Notable figures in Goma's popular culture scene include [[Innoss'B]], [[Jonathan Kuminga]], [[Rebecca Kabugho]], [[Anzor Alem]], [[Ley Uwera]], Petna Ndaliko Katondolo, [[Alicios Theluji]], [[:fr:El Weezya Fantastikoh|El Weezya Fantastikoh]], [[Christophe Madihano]], [[:fr:Patient Ligodi|Patient Ligodi]], Voldie Mapenzi, Mista Faba, Belamy Paluku, and Willow Miller.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=31 January 2022 |title=REDCAT: Films by Petna Ndaliko Katondolo |url=https://www.redcat.org/events/films-petna-ndaliko-katondolo |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Redcat.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kribios-Kauta |first=Adjuvant |date=12 September 2019 |title=Qui est Voldie Mapenzi, la trompette des Grands Lacs à la voie stupéfiante ! |trans-title=Who is Voldie Mapenzi, the Great Lakes trumpet with an astonishing voice! |url=https://www.kribiosuniversal.com/post/qui-est-voldie-mapenzi-la-trompette-des-grands-lacs-a-la-voie-stupefiante- |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Kribiosuniversal.com |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 March 2015 |title=Mista Faba |url=https://www.musicinafrica.net/fr/directory/mista-faba |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Music In Africa |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 October 2015 |title=Belamy Paluku |url=https://www.musicinafrica.net/fr/directory/belamy-paluku |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Music In Africa |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Biographie de Willow Miller |url=https://musique.243stars.com/artists/willow-miller |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=musique.243stars.com |language=fr}}</ref>

=== Entertainment and performing arts ===
During the 1970s, theatrical activities in Goma flourished, with well-organized theater troupes such as AMIKI (''Amis du Kivu'') with Kembo and Mazingi, CLB with Tshiaba, Kainos, and Robert De Souza, and Ngoma with Mpozayo Jean-Paul, among others. The shows were held at the city's Ciné Palace hall. Additionally, the Goma Institute organized a school troupe under the leadership of the then-prefect Lumaya Ombwel, featuring talented student actors like Robert De Souza, also known as Kablan or Gilima, and Mwamba, alias Ringo.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last1=Marie-Vianney |first1=Mpozayo Beru Jean |last2=Michigan |first2=Sebunyenzi Sebakunzi |last3=Eric |first3=Kamori Bazirukize |last4=Katembo |first4=Sivendire |date=3 September 2012 |title=Tourisme culturel dans la ville de Goma, Province du Nord-Kivu |trans-title=Cultural tourism in the city of Goma, North Kivu Province |url=https://www.istougoma.ac.cd/pdf/publication/640f284426987.pdf |access-date=14 February 2024 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Tourisme de Goma (ISTou-Goma) |pages=27–31 |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> In March 2013, Goma played host to the inaugural [[Chukudu|tshukudu]] race, a [[wooden bicycle]] race organized by the [[United Nations Volunteers]] (UNV) and Association of Volunteers of Congo (''Association des Volontaires du Congo''; ASVOCO), which aimed to provide opportunities for the region's unemployed youth and promote peace, with the proceeds benefiting children in [[Kitchanga]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 March 2013 |title=Goma: 120 personnes participent à la course de vélos en bois, "Tshukudu" |trans-title=Goma: 120 people take part in the wooden bicycle race, "Tshukudu" |url=https://www.radiookapi.net/sport/2013/03/16/goma-120-personnes-participent-la-course-de-velos-en-bois-tshukudu |access-date=4 October 2024 |website=[[Radio Okapi]] |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Durré |first=Jean-Jacques |date=18 March 2013 |title=RDC: Des "Tshukudu" pour la paix |url=https://www.cathobel.be/2013/03/rdc-des-tshukudu-pour-la-paix/ |access-date=4 October 2024 |website=Cathobel.be |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Carleton |first=Natasha |date=5 April 2013 |title=Tshukudu – La petite reine du Congo a sa classique |trans-title=Tshukudu – The little queen of Congo has her classic |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/blog/contre-pied/2013/04/05/tshukudu-la-petite-reine-du-congo-a-sa-classique/ |access-date=4 October 2024 |website=[[Le Monde]] |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Paris, France}}</ref>

[[File:Mohombi Moupondo (1545).jpg|thumb|[[Mohombi]] at the Amani Festival in 2022]]
Goma is a hub of art and craftsmanship, with skilled artisans creating intricate wood [[carving]]s, [[pottery]], [[textile]]s, and [[Jewellery|jewelry]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Isse |first=Albert |date=2023-10-03 |title=Goma Culture : quand la danse et la peinture s'allient pour dénoncer le mal |trans-title=Goma Culture: when dance and painting combine to denounce evil |url=https://zikplus.tv/goma-culture-quand-la-danse-et-la-peinture-sallient-pour-denoncer-le-mal/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=Zikplus.tv |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kibangula |first=Treasure |date=October 30, 2015 |title=RDC : Goma la volcanique, comme on ne vous l'a jamais racontée - Jeune Afrique.com |trans-title=DRC: Volcanic Goma, as we have never told you about it |url=https://www.jeuneafrique.com/258567/societe/grand-format-rdc-goma-volcanique-on-ne-jamais-racontee/ |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=JeuneAfrique.com |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Paris, France}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Younger |first=Veronica the |date=2017-11-06 |title=A Goma, si t'as un chukudu, t'es le roi de la rue |trans-title=In Goma, if you have a chukudu, you are the king of the street |url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/monde/afrique/societe-africaine/a-goma-si-t-as-un-chukudu-t-es-le-roi-de-la-rue_3059807.html |access-date=2024-02-13 |website=Franceinfo |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Paris, France}}</ref> The city is home to Petna Ndaliko Katondolo's acclaimed multigenre film productions, which embrace a decolonial ''Ejo Lobi'' ([[Afrofuturism|Afro-futuristic]]) aesthetic that weaves together historical narratives to confront contemporary sociopolitical and cultural paradigms.<ref name=":6" />

The [[Foyer Culturel de Goma]] is the city's most significant [[cultural center]], which plays a pivotal role in nurturing emerging talents, including [[musician]]s, [[poet]]s, thespians, and [[Visual arts|visual artists]], as well as fostering the proliferation and commercialization of indigenous culture and artistic expression within the North Kivu Province.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mutebwa |first=Emilie |date=2 December 2023 |title=Goma: Projection du film " Garçon qui dopta le vent " au foyer culturel de Goma |trans-title=Goma: Screening of the film "Boy who tamed the wind" at the Goma cultural center |url=https://kivumorningpost.cd/2023/12/02/goma-projection-du-film-garcon-qui-dopta-le-vent-au-foyer-culturel-de-goma/ |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Kivu Morning Post |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=12 January 2021 |title=FOYER CULTUREL DE GOMA: Directeur ou d'une Directrice du Foyer Culturel de Goma |trans-title=FOYER CULTURAL DE GOMA: Director of the Foyer Culturel de Goma |url=https://www.radiookapi.net/offre-demploi/foyer-culturel-de-goma-directeur-ou-dune-directrice-du-foyer-culturel-de-goma |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=[[Radio Okapi]] |language=fr |publication-place=Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> The city also hosts the [[Festival Amani|Amani Festival]], a [[Transculturalism|transcultural]] [[festival]] drawing participants from the [[African Great Lakes]] region along with international artists and representatives of different ethnic groups from the region.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=AMANI FESTIVAL |url=https://amanifestival.com/download/archives/2014/AmaniFestival2014_PressKit.pdf?version=v2023.02 |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Amanifestival.com |pages=4–5 |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> Goma also houses Yole! Africa, a youth cultural center promoting peace through art, music, dance, and film.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDarris |first=Annie |date=12 March 2019 |title=Confronting Conflict with Creativity |url=https://tapnet.no/2019/03/12/confronting-conflict-with-creativity/ |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=TRANSCEND Art & Peace Network}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Youth & Artists |url=https://friendsofthecongo.org/youth/ |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=Friends of the Congo}}</ref> The renowned spectacle "Au Chemin des Urnes", hosted by the French Institute (IF) of Goma, celebrates the city's poetic, musical, and rhythmic tapestry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Isse |first=Albert |date=9 May 2023 |title=Goma-culture: présentation du spectacle ''Au Chemin des Urnes'' |trans-title=Goma-culture: presentation of the show "Au Chemin des Urnes" |url=https://zikplus.tv/goma-culture-presentation-du-spectacle-au-chemin-des-urnes/ |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Zikplus.tv |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Isse |first=Albert |date=1 May 2023 |title=Goma Culture: quand le slam s'invite dans le processus électoral |trans-title=Goma Culture: when slam enters the electoral process |url=https://zikplus.tv/goma-culture-quand-le-slam-sinvite-dans-le-processus-electoral/ |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Zikplus.tv |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

=== Cuisine and handicrafts ===
[[File:Goma, Nord-Kivu, RD Congo - Une congolaise transporte des fretins - localement appelés "sambaza" (21953939023).jpg|thumb|Goma's ''sambaza'' are small fish that are traditionally fried and consumed in the region]]
Cuisine in Goma reflects the region's agricultural abundance and diverse influences. Staple foods include [[cassava]], [[Cooking banana|plantains]], [[maize]], and [[rice]], often served alongside a variety of [[meat]]s, [[fish]], and [[vegetable]]s. Local specialties such as ''[[Ugali|bugali]]'' (a starchy dough), ''sambaza'' (small [[dried fish]]), and [[sombe]] (cassava leaves cooked in [[peanut]] sauce) are popular among both residents and visitors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=James |first=Walter |date=1 July 2009 |title=Bon Appetit! |url=https://www.advocacynet.org/bon-appetit/ |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=Advocacynet.org}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

Art-object sellers are organized under an association known as ASEVENOKI, which brings together more than 45 members. Rather than operating from formal [[Art gallery|galleries]], these artisans exhibit and sell their creations in open-air spaces.<ref name=":48">{{Cite web |last=Karumba |first=Janvier Bagula |date=2011 |title=De l'opportunité du développement du tourisme au nord Kivu: Cas de la ville de Goma |trans-title=The opportunity for tourism development in North Kivu: The case of the city of Goma |url=https://www.memoireonline.com/01/14/8505/m_De-l-opportunite-du-developpement-du-tourisme-au-nord-Kivu-Cas-de-la-ville-de-Goma23.html |access-date=27 December 2025 |publisher=Institut Supérieur de Tourisme de Goma (ISTou-Goma) |language=fr |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> Their displays feature a wide range of items, including wooden and ivory [[Figurine|figurines]], [[Bronze sculpture|bronze]] and [[copper]] [[Sculpture|sculptures]], [[Carpet|rugs]] crafted from [[Hide (skin)|animal hides]] and [[Fiber crop|plant fibers]], [[Traditional African masks|masks]], [[Lampshade|lampshades]], and antelope-skin vests.<ref name=":48" /> 

=== Sports ===
[[Association football]] is Goma's most popular sport. Prominent football clubs in the city include [[AS Dauphins Noirs]], which competes in [[Linafoot|Vodacom Ligue 1]], the premier division of the [[Congolese Association Football Federation]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Enyimo |first=Martin |date=13 September 2023 |title=Linafoot/Ligue 1: Dauphin noir désillusionne V.Club, Mazembe et Lupopo gagnent |trans-title=Linafoot/Ligue 1: In addition to football, Goma is home to the Stade Paralympique de Goma, a dedicated [[basketball]] stadium that hosts national [[wheelchair basketball]] championships.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2021 |title=Goma: le sport au cœur de la célébration de la journée internationale des personnes vivant avec handicap |trans-title=Goma: sport at the heart of the celebration of the international day of persons living with disabilities |url=https://www.radiookapi.net/2021/12/03/actualite/societe/goma-le-sport-au-coeur-de-la-celebration-de-la-journee-internationale |access-date=14 October 2024 |website=[[Radio Okapi]] |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Konga |first=Christian Kamalebo |date=10 May 2019 |title=Goma: un bijou remis aux handicapés, un stadium inauguré pour l'émergence de balle au panier |trans-title=Goma: a jewel given to the disabled, a stadium inaugurated for the emergence of basketball |url=https://larepublique.net/goma-un-bijou-remis-aux-handicapes-de-un-stadium-inaugure-pour-lemergence-de-balle-au-panier/ |access-date=14 October 2024 |website=Groupe de presse La République |language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mpoyo |first=Gaël |date=2021 |title=RDC: 3e édition des championnats de basket-fauteuil à Goma |trans-title=DRC: 3rd edition of the wheelchair basketball championships in Goma |url=https://fr.africanews.com/2021/11/30/rdc-3e-edition-des-championnats-de-basket-fauteuil-a-goma/ |access-date=14 October 2024 |website=[[Africanews]] |language=fr |publication-place=Lyon, France}}</ref>

[[Boxing]] plays a significant role in Goma's sports culture, with the city hosting a variety of boxing events, including inter-regional boxing tournaments at the Higher Institute of Commerce of Goma (''Institut supérieur de Commerce de Goma''; ISC-Goma).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |date=25 June 2015 |title=Coup d'envoi du tournoi interrégional de boxe à Goma |trans-title=Inter-regional boxing tournament kicks off in Goma |url=https://provincenordkivu.cd/coup-d-envoi-du-tournoi-interregional-de-boxe-a-goma/ |access-date=14 October 2024 |website=Province du Nord-Kivu |language=fr-FR |publication-place=Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo}}</ref> In 2015, Goma served as the host city for an inter-regional boxing tournament organized by the brewing company Brasimba of [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], which attracted both amateur and professional pugilists from Goma, [[Bukavu]], Beni, [[Butembo]], and [[Rwanda]].<ref name=":0" /> On 30 June 2024, Goma hosted a Boxing Gala organized by the North Kivu Boxing League to commemorate the nation's independence, featuring participants from North Kivu, [[South Kivu]], and [[Maniema]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Muhima |first=Georges Ben |date=18 June 2024 |title=Boxe: Un gala de Boxe pour célébrer l'indépendance du pays annoncé à Goma |trans-title=Boxing: A boxing gala to celebrate the country's independence announced in Goma |url=https://kivumorningpost.cd/2024/06/18/boxe-un-gala-de-boxe-pour-celebrer-lindependance-du-pays-annonce-a-goma/ |access-date=14 October 2024 |website=Kivu Morning Post |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

<noinclude>{{COVID-19 pandemic sidebar|expanded=issues}}</noinclude>
The [[COVID-19 pandemic|<noinclude>COVID-19 pandemic</noinclude>]] affected educational systems across the world.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Lili |last2=Taeihagh |first2=Araz |last3=Tan |first3=Si Ying |date=2023-02-03 |title=A scoping review of the impacts of COVID-19 physical distancing measures on vulnerable population groups |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=599 |doi=10.1038/s41467-023-36267-9  |doi-access=free|issn=2041-1723 |pmc=9897623 |pmid=36737447|bibcode=2023NatCo..14..599L }}</ref> The number of cases of COVID-19 started to rise in March 2020 and many educational institutions and [[University|universities]] underwent closure.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Salazar-Morales |first1=Diego |last2=Pineda |first2=Pedro |last3=Amaral |first3=Lucas |date=2024 |title=Governing schools in times of pandemic: A set-theoretical analysis of the role of policy capacities in school closure |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/gove.12860 |journal=Governance |language=en |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=1433–1463 |doi=10.1111/gove.12860 |issn=1468-0491|doi-access=free }}</ref> Most countries decided to temporarily close the educational institutions in order to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].
[[UNESCO]] estimates that at the height of the closures in April 2020, national educational shutdowns affected nearly 1.6 billion students in 200 countries: 94% of the student population and one-fifth of the global population. 

Closures are estimated to have lasted for an average of 41 weeks (10.3 months). They have had significant negative effects on student learning, which are predicted to have substantial long-term implications for both education and earnings, with disproportionate effects. The [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdowns]] more highly affected already disadvantaged students, and students in low and middle income nations.<ref name="Srivastava" /><ref name="Betthäuser">{{cite journal |last1=Betthäuser |first1=Bastian A. |last2=Bach-Mortensen |first2=Anders M. |last3=Engzell |first3=Per |date=March 2023 |title=A systematic review and meta-analysis of the evidence on learning during the COVID-19 pandemic |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-022-01506-4 |journal=Nature Human Behaviour |language=en |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=375–385 |doi=10.1038/s41562-022-01506-4 |issn=2397-3374 |pmid=36717609 |s2cid=256415516 |access-date=29 March 2023}}</ref><ref name="Donnelly">{{cite journal |last1=Donnelly |first1=Robin |last2=Patrinos |first2=Harry Anthony |date=1 October 2022 |title=Learning loss during Covid-19: An early systematic review |journal=Prospects |language=en |volume=51 |issue=4 |pages=601–609 |doi=10.1007/s11125-021-09582-6 |issn=1573-9090 |pmc=8579897 |pmid=34785823}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Betthäuser |first1=Bastian A. |last2=Bach-Mortensen |first2=Anders M. |last3=Engzell |first3=Per |date=2023-01-30 |title=A systematic review and meta-analysis of the evidence on learning during the COVID-19 pandemic |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-022-01506-4 |journal=Nature Human Behaviour |language=en |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=375–385 |doi=10.1038/s41562-022-01506-4 |issn=2397-3374 |pmid=36717609 |s2cid=256415516}}</ref>

During the pandemic, education budgets and official aid program budgets for education had decreased.<ref name="Srivastava">{{cite journal |last1=Srivastava |first1=Prachi |title=How to recover from the Great Education Disruption |journal=Knowable Magazine |publisher= Annual Reviews |date=15 March 2023 |doi=10.1146/knowable-031423-1|doi-access=free |url=https://knowablemagazine.org/article/society/2023/how-to-recover-great-education-disruption |access-date=29 March 2023 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="UNPB">{{cite book |title=UN Policy Brief: Education During COVID-19 and Beyond |date=August 2020 |publisher=United Nations |url=https://www.un.org/development/desa/dspd/wp-content/uploads/sites/22/2020/08/sg_policy_brief_covid-19_and_education_august_2020.pdf |quote="By mid-April 2020, 94 per cent of learners worldwide were affected by the pandemic, representing 1.58 billion children and youth, from pre-primary to higher education, in 200 countries."}}</ref><ref name="Lennox">{{cite journal |last1=Lennox |first1=Janet |last2=Reuge |first2=Nicolas |last3=Benavides |first3=Francisco |title=UNICEF's lessons learned from the education response to the COVID-19 crisis and reflections on the implications for education policy |journal=International Journal of Educational Development |date=1 September 2021 |volume=85 |article-number=102429 |doi=10.1016/j.ijedudev.2021.102429 |pmid=34518731 |pmc=8426293 |s2cid=236570133 |language=en |issn=0738-0593}}</ref><ref name="Donnelly" /><ref name="Betthäuser" /> Scarcer education options impacted people with few financial resources, while those with more found education.<ref name="Goudeau 2021">{{cite journal |last1=Goudeau |first1=Sébastien |last2=Sanrey |first2=Camille |last3=Stanczak |first3=Arnaud |last4=Manstead |first4=Antony |last5=Darnon |first5=Céline |title=Why lockdown and distance learning during the COVID-19 pandemic are likely to increase the social class achievement gap |journal=Nature Human Behaviour |date=27 September 2021 |volume=5 |issue=10 |pages=1273–1281 |doi=10.1038/s41562-021-01212-7|pmid=34580440 |s2cid=238203517 |doi-access=free }}</ref> New online programs shifted the labor of education from schools to families and individuals, and consequently, people everywhere who relied on schools rather than computers and [[homeschooling]] had more difficulty.<ref name="Goudeau 2021" /> [[Early childhood education]] and care as well as school closures impacted students, teachers, and families,<ref name="Bao 2020">{{cite journal | vauthors = Bao X, Qu H, Zhang R, Hogan TP | title = Modeling Reading Ability Gain in Kindergarten Children during COVID-19 School Closures | journal = International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health | volume = 17 | issue = 17 | pages = 17 | date = September 2020 | pmid = 32882960 | pmc = 7504163 | doi = 10.3390/ijerph17176371 | doi-access = free }}</ref> and far-reaching economic and societal consequences are expected.<ref
