In July 2019, Sanders was an original cosponsor of the Sensible, Timely Relief for America's Nuclear Districts' Economic Development (STRANDED) Act, a bipartisan bill introduced by [[Susan Collins]] and [[Tammy Duckworth]] that would give economic impact grants to local government entities for the purpose of offsetting economic impacts of stranded nuclear waste in addition to forming a task force that would identify funding which already exists that could be used to benefit its respective community and form a competitive innovative solutions prize competition to aid those communities in their search for alternatives to "nuclear facilities, generating sites, and waste sites."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timesrecord.com/articles/local/senate-bill-to-help-communities-like-wiscasset-stranded-with-nuclear-waste/|title=Senate bill to help communities like Wiscasset 'STRANDED' with nuclear waste|date=July 10, 2019|publisher=timesrecord.com|access-date=July 11, 2019|archive-date=July 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190711022915/https://www.timesrecord.com/articles/local/senate-bill-to-help-communities-like-wiscasset-stranded-with-nuclear-waste/}}</ref>

=== Pipelines ===
At a September 2016 rally near the White House, Sanders called on President Obama to ensure the [[Dakota Access Pipeline]] "gets a full environmental and cultural impact analysis" and stated his position that the pipeline would not continue in the event of such an analysis taking place, citing findings by Oil Change International that the Dakota Access Pipeline would have the same impact on the planet as adding 21 million more cars on the road along with constructing 30 more coal plants.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/295813-sanders-joins-protesters-against-nd-pipeline-project/|title=Sanders joins protesters against ND pipeline project|date=September 13, 2016|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In October 2016, Sanders led four senators in a letter to President Obama requesting the administration halt work on the Dakota Access Pipeline until the permitting process of the Army Corps "be transparent and include public notice and participation, formal and meaningful tribal consultation, and adequate environmental review" and stating their support for the "tribes along the pipeline route in their fight against the Dakota Access pipeline project."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/energy-environment/300775-sanders-dem-senators-press-obama-to-halt-nd-pipeline/|title=Sanders, Dem senators press Obama to halt ND pipeline|first=Devin|last=Henry|date=October 13, 2016|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In December 2016, following the [[United States Army Corps of Engineers]]'s block on the Dakota Access Pipeline, Sanders released a statement praising President Obama for listening to Native Americans as well as others opposed to the pipeline's construction and said the United States should neither "endanger the water supply of millions of people" nor "become more dependent on fossil fuel and accelerate the planetary crisis of climate change." He called for a transformation of the American energy system that would see a departure from the usage of fossil fuels.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.politico.com/story/2016/12/sanders-praises-dakota-access-pipeline-block-232174|title=Sanders praises Dakota Access Pipeline ruling|date=December 4, 2016|first=Rebecca|last=Morin|work=Politico}}</ref>

Following a spill at the Keystone pipeline in October 2019, Sanders said he would shut down the existing Keystone pipeline if elected.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/BernieSanders/status/1189997655864348672|title=@Bernie Sanders on Twitter|quote=This is what happens when we have a president who ignores scientists and puts short-term fossil fuel profits ahead of the environment and the future of the planet. As president, I will shut down the Keystone Pipeline that should never have been built in the first place.|last=Sanders|first=Bernie|date=October 31, 2019|publisher=Twitter|access-date=November 2, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/keystone-spils-over-1-million-litres-oil-north-dakota-1.5343509|title=Keystone pipeline shut after spilling 1.4 million litres of oil in North Dakota|date=October 31, 2019|publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref>

==Transparency and corruption==
===Campaign finance===
Sanders supports the [[DISCLOSE Act]], which would make campaign finances more transparent and ban U.S. corporations controlled by foreign interests from making political expenditures.<ref>{{cite web |title=Legislation – Campaign Finance: Bernie Sanders – U.S. Senator for Vermont |publisher=Sanders.senate.gov |url=http://www.sanders.senate.gov/legislation/issue/?id=a22c4c55-2c79-4d6b-895b-704230412415 |access-date=February 17, 2013}}</ref> He has been outspoken in calling for an overturn of ''[[Citizens United v. FEC|Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission]]'', in which the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] overturned [[Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act|McCain–Feingold]] restrictions on political spending by [[corporations]] and [[labor union|unions]] as a violation of the [[First Amendment to the United States Constitution|First Amendment]].<ref name="Huffington Post">{{cite news |last=Sanders |first=Bernie |date=March 22, 2015 |title=If We Don't Overturn Citizens United, The Congress Will Become Paid Employees of the Billionaire Class |work=[[HuffPost]] |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/rep-bernie-sanders/sanders-to-senate-if-we-dont-overturn-citizens-united-the-congress-will-become-paid-employees-of-the-billionaire-class_b_6918468.html |access-date=July 18, 2015}}</ref> Saying that he believes that the ''Citizens United'' decision is "one of the Supreme Court's worst decisions ever" and that it has allowed big money to "deflect attention from the real issues" facing voters,<ref>{{cite news |last=Collins |first=Eliza |date=May 10, 2015 |title=Bernie Sanders takes dead aim on Citizens United ruling |work=[[Politico]] |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2015/05/bernie-sanders-takes-dead-aim-on-citizens-united-ruling-117792.html}}</ref> he has proposed a [[constitutional amendment]] to undo the ruling.<ref>{{cite news |last=Easley |first=Jason |title=Bernie Sanders Files a New Constitutional Amendment to Overturn Citizens United |work=PoliticsUSA |url=http://www.politicususa.com/2015/01/21/bernie-sanders-files-constitutional-amendment-overturn-citizens-united.html}}</ref> He warns: "We now have a political situation where billionaires are literally able to buy elections and candidates."<ref>{{cite news |last=Zaru |first=Deena |date=May 6, 2015 |title=Election 2016: Who are the richest candidates? |publisher=CNN |url=http://www.cnn.com/2015/05/06/politics/election-2016-richest-presidential-candidates/}}</ref>

In January 2016, Sanders was one of 29 senators to sign a letter spearheaded by [[Ron Wyden]] and [[Sheldon Whitehouse]] to President Obama urging him to issue a final executive order that would require federal contractors to disclose political donations, arguing that form of disclosure was "a modest step that would expose an especially troubling type of secret money: campaign contributions that have the potential to influence government contracting practices."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/blogs/floor-action/senate/265137-dems-push-obama-to-tighten-campaign-spending-rules/|title=Dems push Obama to tighten campaign spending rules|date=January 7, 2016|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In October 2016, while stumping for Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton, Sanders advocated for Trump supporters to vote for Clinton due to her promise to propose a constitutional amendment in the first 100 days of her presidency to overturn ''Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission'' as well as her intent to nominate a Supreme Court justice to fill the vacancy by the late [[Antonin Scalia]] that would support overturning ''Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission'': "This issue of Citizens United is a profound issue impacting the entire country. I say to Mr. Trump's supporters: most of you understand that system is rigged in favor of wealthy and power."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/blogs/ballot-box/presidential-races/301426-sanders-makes-pitch-to-trump-supporters-over-campaign/|title=Sanders makes pitch to Trump supporters over campaign finance reform|date=October 17, 2016|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

===Instant-runoff voting===
In 2007, Sanders testified to the [[Vermont Senate]] Government Operations Committee that he "strongly supports [[instant-runoff voting]]" because it "allows people to vote for what they really want, without worrying about the possibility of them getting what they really don't want".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.fairvote.org/?page=1998|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150722213037/https://archive.fairvote.org/?page=1998|archive-date=July 22, 2015|title=Testimony to the Vermont Senate Government Operations Committee|last=Sanders|first=Bernie|date=March 15, 2007|website=FairVote.org|publisher=FairVote|access-date=July 22, 2015}}</ref> The committee and legislature ultimately passed legislation that would have enacted instant run-off voting for U.S. Representatives and U.S. Senators, but the governor vetoed it.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive3.fairvote.org/articles/douglas-vetoes-campaign-finance-instant-runoff-voting-bills/|title=Douglas vetoes campaign finance, instant-runoff voting bills|last=Gram|first=Dave|date=April 7, 2008|newspaper=Boston Globe|access-date=July 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331224932/http://archive3.fairvote.org/articles/douglas-vetoes-campaign-finance-instant-runoff-voting-bills/|archive-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>

=== Criticism of the media ===
In an early essay, Sanders claimed that the corporate owners of the television industry sought to benumb critical thinking among their viewers. Later he bemoaned the media's emphasis on reporting disasters, while ignoring what he characterizes as the plight of the working class.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2019/02/26/ive-reported-bernie-sanders-years-free-press-cant-give-him-what-he-wants/|title=I've reported on Bernie Sanders for years. A free press won't give him what he wants.|last=Heintz|first=Paul|date=February 26, 2019|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=March 24, 2019}}</ref> Consequently, he has been a leader in calling for media reform and opposes increased [[Concentration of media ownership|concentration of ownership of media outlets]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nichols |first1=John |last2=McEhsney |first2=Robert W. |date=July 7, 2003 |title=The Battle Over Media Ownership is Far From Over |publisher=[[Common Dreams NewsCenter]] |quote=Members of Congress are finding they cannot avoid talking about media issues because people really are upset with what the FCC did and with the broader issue of who controls the media," says U.S. Rep. Bernie Sanders, I-Vermont, a leading critic of the FCC rule changes [removing limits on the ability of individual companies to dominate more than 35 percent of television communications and to prevent "cross-ownership" schemes that allow corporations to buy up primary newspapers, radio and television stations and cable and Internet services in a city.] and a champion of media reform in the public interest. |url=http://www.commondreams.org/views03/0707-01.htm |access-date=August 4, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120628013951/http://www.commondreams.org/views03/0707-01.htm |archive-date=June 28, 2012}}</ref> as well as being a contributing author for ''[[OpEdNews]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bernie Sanders author page at ''OpEdNews'' |newspaper=[[OpEdNews]] |url=http://www.opednews.com/author/author7111.html |access-date=May 19, 2014}}</ref> He appeared in ''[[Orwell Rolls in His Grave]]'' and ''[[Outfoxed: Rupert Murdoch's War on Journalism]]'', two documentaries on the subject.<ref>{{cite news |agency=Associated Press |date=July 26, 2004 |title=Vt. congressman interviewed for film |work=[[USA Today]] |quote=Rep. Bernie Sanders has a burgeoning second job: movie star. Vermont's lone congressman is one of many legislators, journalists and media watchdogs interviewed for 'Orwell Rolls in His Grave,' by director Robert Pappas, and Robert Greenwald's latest film, 'Outfoxed: Rupert Murdoch's War on Journalism.' |url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/people/2004-07-26-senator-filmed_x.htm |access-date=August 4, 2009}}</ref>

=== Internet privacy ===
In April 2017, after President Trump signed a law undoing a [[Federal Communications Commission]] rule requiring internet service providers to obtain permission from customers prior to selling their data to advertisers, Sanders was one of eleven senators to sponsor legislation undoing the repeal and reinstating the regulations.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/technology/327652-senate-dems-want-to-reinstate-privacy-rules/|title=Senate Dems offer bill to restore internet privacy rules|date=April 6, 2017|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref> Sanders voiced support for penalizing companies that neglect to protect their users' personal data, specifically citing the [[2017 Equifax data breach]].<ref name="controls">{{cite web |url=https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2019/12/3/20965463/tech-2020-candidate-policies-online-data-equifax |title=2020 Democrats on who controls your data — and who's at fault when it's mishandled |author1=Molla, Rani |author2=Stewart, Emily |work=Vox |date=December 5, 2019 |access-date=February 21, 2020}}</ref>

Sanders has also proposed creating a public, secure [[credit reporting agency|credit registry]] to replace the current credit reporting system.<ref name="controls"/>

===Net neutrality===
Sanders opposes the [[Net neutrality in the United States#Under the Trump administration (2017–2020)|repeal of net neutrality in the United States]], as voted by FCC commissioners in a 3–2 vote on December 14, 2017 — his statement on the issue from his U.S. Senate website on the same day as the vote, partly reads: "The FCC's vote to end net neutrality is an egregious attack on our democracy. With this decision the internet and its free exchange of information as we have come to know it will cease to exist ... At a time when our democratic institutions are already in peril, we must do everything we can to stop this decision from taking effect."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/recent-business/-sanders-statement-on-fcc-decision-to-repeal-net-neutrality |title=Bernie Sanders, U.S. Senator for Vermont – Sanders Statement on FCC Decision to Repeal Net Neutrality |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=December 14, 2017 |website=sanders.senate.gov |publisher=Office of U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders |access-date=December 16, 2017 |quote=Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) issued the following statement Thursday after the Federal Communications Commission voted to repeal net neutrality protections: "Once again, the Trump administration has sided with big money and against the interests of the American people. '''The FCC's vote to end net neutrality is an egregious attack on our democracy. With this decision the internet and its free exchange of information as we have come to know it will cease to exist.''' The end of net neutrality protections means that the internet will be for sale to the highest bidder, instead of everyone having the same access regardless of whether they are rich or poor, a big corporation or small business, a multimedia conglomerate or a small online publication. '''At a time when our democratic institutions are already in peril, we must do everything we can to stop this decision from taking effect."''' |archive-date=November 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123110802/https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/recent-business/-sanders-statement-on-fcc-decision-to-repeal-net-neutrality }}</ref>

In May 2014, days before the FCC was scheduled to rewrite its net neutrality rules, Sanders was one of eleven senators to sign a letter to FCC Chairman [[Tom Wheeler]] charging Wheeler's proposal with destroying net neutrality instead of preserving it and urged the FCC to "consider reclassifying Internet providers to make them more like traditional phone companies, over which the agency has clear authority to regulate more broadly."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/technology/205743-senate-dems-protest-fcc-plan-for-internet-fast-lanes/|title=Senate Dems protest FCC plan for Internet 'fast lanes'|date=May 9, 2014|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In March 2018, Sanders was one of 10 senators to sign a letter spearheaded by [[Jeff Merkley]] which lambasted a proposal from FCC Chairman [[Ajit Pai]] that would curb the scope of benefits from the [[Universal Service Fund#Low income (Lifeline)|Lifeline program]], which provided access to high-speed internet to roughly 6.5 million people in poor communities, citing that it was Pai's "obligation to the American public, as the Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, to improve the Lifeline program and ensure that more Americans can afford access, and have means of access, to broadband and phone service".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/technology/380870-democrats-slam-fcc-head-over-plan-to-limit-internet-access-funding-for-low/|title=Dems slam FCC head for proposed limits to low-income internet program|date=March 29, 2018|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In May 2018, Sanders voted for a bill that would reinstate net neutrality rules and thereby overturn the FCC's repeal via a law authorizing Congress to reverse regulatory actions by a simple majority vote.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-internet/senate-approves-bill-in-bid-to-retain-u-s-net-neutrality-idUSKCN1IH2DS|title=Senate approves bill in bid to retain U.S. net neutrality|date=May 16, 2018|first=David|last=Shepardson|work=Reuters}}</ref>

==Foreign policy==
[[File:Bernie Sanders in Vallejo, California.jpg|thumb|300px|Sanders at a May 2016 rally in [[Vallejo, California]]]]

=== Afghanistan ===
Sanders voted for the 2001 [[Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Terrorists]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 342 |publisher=Office of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives |url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2001/roll342.xml |access-date=October 13, 2014}}</ref> that has been cited as the legal justification for controversial military actions since the [[September 11 attacks]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Johnsen |first=Gregory D. |date=January 16, 2014 |title=60 Words And A War Without End: The Untold Story Of The Most Dangerous Sentence In U.S. History |publisher=Buzzfeed |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/gregorydjohnsen/60-words-and-a-war-without-end-the-untold-story-of-the-most |access-date=October 13, 2014}}</ref> In February 2011, Sanders traveled to [[Afghanistan]] and [[Pakistan]] with fellow senators [[Bob Corker]], [[Chris Coons]], and [[Joe Manchin]], opining afterward that Afghanistan was "one of the most backward countries in the entire world", given its massive poverty, lack of literacy, and corruption. He stated his belief that the US could afford to reduce its funding for the American and Afghanistan armed forces, Afghanistan police, and Afghanistan's economic development.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/blogs/floor-action/senate/83675-sen-sanders-afghanistan-is-a-backward-country/|title=Sen. Sanders: Afghanistan is a backward country|first=Josiah|last=Ryan|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref> Sanders said in 2019 that [[Barbara Lee]], the sole "no" vote on the 2001 AUMF, was correct to do so.<ref>{{cite web |title='I Was Wrong': Bernie Sanders Admits Barbara Lee Only Member of Congress in 2001 Who Had it Right on Afghan War |url=https://www.commondreams.org/news/2019/12/20/i-was-wrong-bernie-sanders-admits-barbara-lee-only-member-congress-2001-who-had-it |website=Common Dreams |access-date=April 8, 2026}}</ref> By 2009, Sanders stated that the war was "unwinnable", voted against funding for it, and opposed sending more troops.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bernie Sanders on Afghanistan |url=https://feelthebern.org/bernie-sanders-on-afghanistan/ |website=Feel the Bern |access-date=April 8, 2026}}</ref>

In 2019, Sanders was one of eight lawmakers to sign a pledge by grass-roots organization Common Defense stating their intent "to fight to reclaim Congress's constitutional authority to conduct oversight of U.S. foreign policy and independently debate whether to authorize each new use of military force", along with acting toward bringing "the Forever War to a responsible and expedient conclusion", after seventeen years of ongoing US military conflict.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/defense/432670-sanders-ocasio-cortez-sponsoring-end-the-forever-war-pledge/|title=Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez back "end the forever war" pledge|date=March 5, 2019|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In June 2019, Sanders told ''The New York Times'' that "by the end of my first term, I think our troops would be home".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2019/us/politics/bernie-sanders-2020-campaign.html?mtrref=www.nytimes.com&gwh=9C1025B222DC01F2DFA69B122317C4C4&gwt=pay&assetType=REGIWALL|title=2020 Democrats on Troops in Afghanistan|date=June 19, 2019|work=The New York Times|access-date=September 16, 2019|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In September, a campaign spokesman indicated to ''The Washington Post'' that this did not rule out leaving residual forces.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/graphics/politics/policy-2020/foreign-policy/|title=Where 2020 Democrats stand on Foreign policy: Would you set a hard date for withdrawal from Afghanistan of all U.S. military forces?|date=September 10, 2019|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=September 15, 2019}}</ref>

In September 2021, after a drone strike accidentally killed 10 civilians, Sanders called the incident "a human tragedy" that reflected on the US and "unacceptable".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newsweek.com/unacceptable-bernie-sanders-calls-us-afghanistan-drone-strike-human-tragedy-1630611|title='Unacceptable': Bernie Sanders Calls U.S. Afghanistan Drone Strike a 'Human Tragedy'|date=September 19, 2021|first=Christina|last=Zhao|publisher=Newsweek}}</ref>

=== Balkans ===
Sanders supported the 1999 [[NATO bombing of Yugoslavia]], arguing that while aspects of the Clinton administration's military push to resolve ethnic tensions in [[Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija|Kosovo]] bordered on unconstitutional, such a push was necessary to prevent genocide in the region.<ref>{{cite web|date=August 18, 2015|title=Bernie Sanders on Kosovo (4/28/1999)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R8S19u91Dfs|via=YouTube|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=June 22, 2015|title=Bernie Sanders Town Hall on NATO's Air War on Serbia May 3, 1999|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dazZyVW7DaQ|via=YouTube|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref> Regarding the level of influence Congress needed to have in approving the bombing, he preferred the administration's recommendation that the bombing not be subject to the [[War Powers Resolution]] of 1973,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.politico.com/magazine/story/2019/06/23/bernie-sanders-foreign-policy-doctrine-227193/|title=What Would Bernie Bomb?|first=Bill|last=Scher|date=June 23, 2019|work=Politico|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref> and opposed an explicit [[declaration of war by the United States]] proposed by then-Representative [[Tom Campbell (California politician)|Tom Campbell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record/1999/4/28/house-section/article/h2427-1?s=1&r=26|title=Congressional Record, Declaring State of War Between United States and Government of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, House of Representatives debate|publisher=Congress.gov|date=April 28, 1999 |access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref>

During the [[Greek government-debt crisis]], Sanders opposed fiscal [[austerity#Greece|austerity]] measures, and called on the [[European Central Bank]], [[European Commission]], and [[International Monetary Fund]] to back "pro-growth" economic stimulus policies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/recent-business/the-week-in-review-071015|title=The Week In Review: July 10, 2015|publisher=Bernie Sanders United States Senator for Vermont (official government site)|date=July 10, 2015|access-date=June 24, 2019|archive-date=November 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109024800/https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/recent-business/the-week-in-review-071015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=February 9, 2015 |title=Greek Democracy|via=YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WKeyizCv6Xo |access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref> In November 2018, Sanders and former Greek finance minister [[Yanis Varoufakis]] reiterated their opposition to austerity before launching the [[Progressive International]] movement at an event in Rome.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/lesterfeder/bernie-sanders-yanis-varoufakis-european-spring-movement|title=Bernie Sanders is Partnering With a Greek Progressive to Build a New Leftist Movement|first=J. Lester|last=Feder|date=October 26, 2018|publisher=BuzzFeed News|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref>

=== Central America ===
In April 2019, Sanders was one of 34 senators to sign a letter to President Trump encouraging him "to listen to members of your own Administration and reverse a decision that will damage our national security and aggravate conditions inside Central America", asserting that Trump had "consistently expressed a flawed understanding of U.S. foreign assistance" since becoming president, and that he was "personally undermining efforts to promote U.S. national security and economic prosperity" through preventing the use of Fiscal Year 2018 national security funding. The senators argued that foreign assistance to Central American countries created less migration to the U.S., citing the funding's helping to improve conditions in those countries.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/international/americas/437463-more-than-30-dem-sens-ask-trump-to-reconsider-cutting-foreign/|title=More than 30 Senate Dems ask Trump to reconsider Central American aid cuts|first=Rachel|last=Frazin|date=April 4, 2019|newspaper=The Hill|access-date=April 4, 2019|archive-date=April 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404221454/https://thehill.com/policy/international/americas/437463-more-than-30-dem-sens-ask-trump-to-reconsider-cutting-foreign|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Cuba===
On April 14, 2015, after the White House announced that President Obama had intended to [[Cuban thaw|remove Cuba from the United States' list of nations sponsoring terrorism]], Sanders issued a statement, saying: "While we have our strong differences with Cuba, it is not a terrorist state. I applaud President Obama for moving aggressively to develop normal diplomatic relations. Fifty years of Cold War is enough. It is time for Cuba and the United States to turn the page and normalize relations."<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sanders-statement-on-cuba | title=Sanders statement on Cuba | publisher=Bernie Sanders United States Senator for Vermont | date=April 14, 2015 | access-date=July 21, 2015 | archive-date=November 9, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109034307/https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sanders-statement-on-cuba }}</ref>

===China===
On May 1, 2019, Sanders tweeted: "Since the [[United States–China Relations Act of 2000|China trade deal]] I voted against, America has lost over 3 million manufacturing jobs. It's wrong to pretend that China isn't one of our major economic competitors."<ref name="foreign-policy"/>

On August 27, 2019, Sanders told ''The Hill'': "China is a country that is moving unfortunately in a more authoritarian way in a number of directions. What we have to say about China, in fairness to China and its leadership, is – if I'm not mistaken – they have made more progress in addressing extreme poverty than any country in the history of civilization. So they've done a lot of things for their people."<ref>{{cite news |title=Sanders: China has done more to address extreme poverty "than any country in the history of civilization" |url=https://thehill.com/hilltv/rising/458976-sanders-china-had-done-more-to-address-extreme-poverty-than-any-country-in-the/ |work=The Hill |date=August 27, 2019}}</ref>

On December 6, 2019, Sanders spoke concerning the [[Xinjiang internment camps]], telling the ''[[DesMoines Register]]'': "What we should be doing with China is understanding they are a super-power, they are a strong economy. We want to be working with them. We certainly don't want a Cold War. But we should be speaking out against human rights abuses. When you put into concentration camps, you know, or at least lock up, I don't know, a million Muslims there, somebody's got to speak out about that."<ref>{{cite video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZiQosAg1O6o|title=Full interview: Bernie Sanders meets with the Register's editorial board (12.6.19)|publisher=[[DesMoines Register]]|via=[[YouTube]]|time=37:13|date=December 6, 2019|access-date=December 17, 2019}}</ref>

On January 7, 2020, Sanders mentioned China in the context of the [[2020 Baghdad International Airport airstrike]] in an interview with [[Anderson Cooper]], saying: "... you can say there are a lot of bad people all over the world running governments... The President of China now has put a million people, Muslims, into educational camps – some would call them concentration camps."<ref>{{cite video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GxyXrezEfL0|title=Bernie Sanders: Trump administration hasn't a clue about what it's doing|date=January 7, 2020|access-date=January 7, 2020|time=3:33|via=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref>

===Iran===
Sanders supports the agreement with [[Iran]] reached by President Obama and Secretary of State [[John Kerry]]. While calling it less than a perfect agreement, he believes that the US needs to negotiate with Iran, rather than enter in another war in the Middle East.<ref>[https://berniesanders.com/press-release/bringing-people-together/ "Bringing People Together", is Campaign's Core, Sanders Tells Another Record Rally] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303093356/https://berniesanders.com/press-release/bringing-people-together/ |date=March 3, 2016 }}.BernieSanders.com, August 9, 2015.</ref>

During the January 17, 2016, Democratic debate in [[Charleston, South Carolina]], Sanders criticized Iran by saying, "Their support for terrorism, the anti-American rhetoric that we're hearing from of their leadership is something that is not acceptable", and espoused the view that the US should apply the same policy it did toward normalizing relations with Cuba to Iran, through a "move in warm relations with a very powerful and important country in this world".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/US-Elections/US-candidate-Bernie-Sanders-calls-for-normalizing-ties-with-Iran-441896|title=Democratic Candidate Sanders Calls for Normalizing US Ties With Iran|date=January 18, 2016|work=The Jerusalem Post}}</ref>

In 2017, Congress took up a bill designed to impose [[Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act|CAATSA sanctions]] on [[Russia]], for its alleged interference in the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 election]], and on Iran. Sanders announced that he supported the sanctions on Russia, but he voted against the bill because of the Iran provisions. He stated:

<blockquote>I have voted for sanctions on Iran in the past, and I believe sanctions were an important tool for bringing Iran to the negotiating table. But I believe that these new sanctions could endanger the very important nuclear agreement that was signed between the United States, its partners, and Iran in 2015. That is not a risk worth taking. ...<ref name="caatsa">{{cite press release|last= Sanders|first= Bernie|date= June 15, 2017|title= Sanders Statement on Iran and Russia Sanctions|url= https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sanders-statement-on-iran-and-russia-sanctions|location= Washington, D. C.|publisher= [[United States Senate]]|access-date= July 19, 2017|archive-date= November 9, 2020|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201109164255/https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/sanders-statement-on-iran-and-russia-sanctions}}</ref></blockquote>

In October 2017, Sanders said that "the worst possible thing" the United States could do was undermine the Iran nuclear deal if it was "genuinely concerned with Iran's behavior in the region", and that the president's comments against the deal had isolated the US from foreign allies that had retained their commitment to the agreement.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/355369-sanders-rips-trumps-bluster-on-iran/|title=Sanders rips Trump's "bluster" on Iran|date=October 13, 2017|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

In May 2018, Sanders was one of 12 senators to sign a letter to President Trump, urging him to remain in the Iran nuclear deal, on the grounds that "Iran could either remain in the agreement and seek to isolate the United States from our closest partners, or resume its nuclear activities" if the US pulled out, and that both possibilities "would be detrimental to our national security interests".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/386604-senate-dems-urge-trump-to-remain-in-iran-deal-ahead-of-announcement/|title=Senate Dems urge Trump to remain in Iran deal ahead of announcement|date=May 7, 2018|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

Following [[Patrick M. Shanahan]] announcing 1,000 more US troops being deployed to the Middle East for defensive purposes in June 2019, Sanders was one of six senators to sign a letter spearheaded by [[Tim Kaine]] and [[Mike Lee]], expressing concern that "increasingly escalatory actions" by both the US and Iran would "lead to an unnecessary conflict". The senators noted that Congress had not authorized a war against Iran, and requested "a joint Defense, State, and Intelligence Community briefing by the end of June to address these policy and legal issues".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/defense/449188-senators-demand-trump-explain-decision-to-deploy-troops-amid-iran-tensions/|first=Jordain|last=Carney|title=Senators demand Trump explain decision to deploy troops amid Iran tensions|date=June 18, 2019|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

Sanders said during the Democratic primary debate hosted by NBC News: "I will do everything I can to prevent a war with Iran, which would be far worse than [the] disastrous war with Iraq."<ref name="foreign-policy"/>

Following the death of [[Qasem Soleimani]] in a US airstrike, Sanders tweeted: "Trump's dangerous escalation brings us closer to another disastrous war in the Middle East that could cost countless lives and trillions more dollars. Trump promised to end endless wars, but this action puts us on the path to another one."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sanders |first1=Bernie |title=Trump's dangerous escalation brings us closer to another disastrous war in the Middle East that could cost countless lives and trillions more dollars. Trump promised to end endless wars, but this action puts us on the path to another one. |url=https://twitter.com/BernieSanders/status/1212959357425651713 |website=Twitter |access-date=January 4, 2020}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=January 2020}}

===India===
Sanders, along with multiple other American politicians, expressed their concerns over the anti-Muslim [[North East Delhi riots]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.in/entry/delhi-violence-bjp-leader-threatens-bernie-sanders-with-us-election-interference_in_5e573f59c5b66137fb5d90d1|title=BJP General Secretary Threatens Bernie Sanders With US Election Interference|date=February 27, 2020|work=Huffington Post India}}</ref> In response, on February 27, 2020, the Indian Foreign Ministry spokesperson, [[Raveesh Kumar]], stated that these remarks were "factually inaccurate", "misleading", and "aimed at politicising the issue".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/delhi-violence-international-criticism-misleading-and-inaccurate-says-india/article30929288.ece|title=International criticism "misleading and inaccurate", says India |date=February 27, 2020|work=The Hindu|issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

===Iraq===
Sanders strongly opposed the [[2003 invasion of Iraq]] and voted against the 2002 [[Iraq Resolution|resolution]] authorizing the use of force against that country. In a 2002 speech, he said: "I am opposed to giving the President a blank check to launch a unilateral invasion and occupation of Iraq"; and: "I will vote against this resolution. One, I have not heard any estimates of how many young American men and women might die in such a war, or how many tens of thousands of women and children in Iraq might also be killed. As a caring Nation, we should do everything we can to prevent the horrible suffering that a war will cause. War must be the last recourse in international relations, not the first. Second, I am deeply concerned about the precedent that a unilateral invasion of Iraq could establish in terms of international law and the role of the United Nations."<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.businessinsider.com/bernie-sanders-revisits-vote-against-iraq-war-16th-anniversary-invasion-2019-3 |title = Bernie Sanders revisits his vote against the Iraq War |website = [[Business Insider]] |date = March 20, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Rep. Bernard "Bernie" Sanders Opposes the Iraq War | website=C-SPAN.org | date=October 9, 2002 | url=http://www.c-span.org/video/?c4512996/rep-bernard-bernie-sanders-opposes-iraq-war | access-date=June 25, 2019}}</ref>

===Islamic State of Iraq and Syria===
Sanders has called the [[Islamic State of Iraq and Syria]] (ISIS) "a barbaric organization" and "a growing threat", but does not believe that the U.S. should lead the fight against it. Sanders believes that "the United States should be supportive, along with other countries, but we cannot and we should not be involved in perpetual warfare in the Middle East – the [[Muslim countries]] themselves have got to lead the effort".<ref name="YouTube">{{cite web |date=June 2, 2015 |title=Bernie Sanders Speaks With Katie Couric – Full Interview |via=YouTube |at=24:00 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpgJYNaIeqo |access-date=July 12, 2015}}</ref>

On November 15, 2015, in response to [[November 2015 Paris attacks|ISIS' attacks in Paris]], Sanders cautioned against [[Islamophobia]], saying: "During these difficult times as Americans, we will not succumb to racism. We will not allow ourselves to be divided and succumb to Islamophobia. And while hundreds of thousands have lost everything, have nothing left but the shirts on their backs, we will not turn our backs on the refugees!"<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/2015/11/16/politics/bernie-sanders-cleveland-isis/index.html|title=Bernie Sanders on ISIS: U.S. needs to be "tough", not "stupid" |author=Tom LoBianco|date=November 17, 2015|publisher=CNN}}</ref>

Sanders criticized [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Kuwait]], [[Qatar]], and [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]], saying that those "countries of enormous wealth and resources – have contributed far too little in the fight against ISIS". Sanders said Saudi Arabia, instead of fighting ISIS, has focused more on supporting the Yemeni government against Iranian sponsored [[Houthis|Houthi militants in Yemen]] that [[Houthi takeover in Yemen|seized control]] of much of the country in 2015, and Kuwait, which has been a well-known source of financing for ISIS, and Qatar is spending $200 billion on the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]], yet very little to fight against ISIS.{{According to whom|date=March 2020}} "Wealthy and powerful Muslim nations in the region can no longer sit on the sidelines and expect the United States to do their work for them."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://berniesanders.com/democratic-socialism-in-the-united-states/ |title=Senator Bernie Sanders on Democratic Socialism in the United States |date=November 19, 2015 |work=Berniesanders.com |access-date=October 8, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170720220054/https://berniesanders.com/democratic-socialism-in-the-united-states/ |archive-date=July 20, 2017 }}</ref>

=== Syria and Assad ===
In January 2016, Sanders said on the Democratic primary debate: "Our first priority must be the destruction of ISIS. Our second must be getting rid of Assad."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ABC/status/688926438985232384|title=Bernie Sanders: "Our 1st priority must be the destruction of ISIS. Our 2nd must be getting rid of Assad" #DemDebatepic.twitter.com/UVbTCVUurS|date=January 17, 2016|publisher=ABC|via=Twitter|access-date=March 10, 2020}}</ref> Then, in September 2019, Sanders told the Washington Post, "The world and in particular the Syrian people would be far better off without Bashar al-Assad, who is responsible for the mass murder of hundreds of thousands of innocent men, women and children, the forced migration of millions and the collapse of the nation of Syria. It is not up to the United States to topple him, and diplomatic engagement does not imply approval of him or of his activities. If he remains in power, the United States needs to engage with his regime in some fashion."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/graphics/politics/policy-2020/foreign-policy/syria-assad-negotiations/|title=Where 2020 Democrats stand on foreign policy: Would you reopen diplomatic relations with the Syrian government if Bashar al-Assad remains in power?|date=September 12, 2019|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=September 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190912024736/https://www.washingtonpost.com/graphics/politics/policy-2020/foreign-policy/syria-assad-negotiations/|archive-date=September 12, 2019}}</ref>

In April 2018, in a statement, Sanders said President Trump had "no legal authority for broadening the war in Syria" and recommended Trump approach Congress if he believed "expanding the war in Syria will bring stability to the region and protect American interests".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/382665-bernie-sanders-trump-has-no-authority-to-broaden-war-in-syria/|title=Bernie Sanders: Trump has no authority to broaden war in Syria|date=April 11, 2018|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref>

===Israeli–Palestinian conflict===
Sanders supports a [[two-state solution]], saying that "the Palestinian people, in my view, deserve a state of their own, they deserve an economy of their own, they deserve economic support from the people of this country. And Israel needs to be able to live in security without terrorist attacks."<ref name="War and Peace">[http://www.sanders.senate.gov/legislation/issue/war-and-peace War and Peace] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906005919/http://www.sanders.senate.gov/legislation/issue/war-and-peace |date=September 6, 2015 }}, Bernie Sanders, Senate website</ref> Sanders has said Israel must have a right to live in peace and security.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/US-Israel/sanderscampaign.html |title=2016 U.S. Elections: Bernie Sanders |encyclopedia=Jewish Virtual Library |access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref>

In 2008, Sanders was a co-sponsor of a Senate Resolution, "recognizing the 60th anniversary of the founding of the modern State of Israel and reaffirming the bonds of close friendship and cooperation between the United States and Israel." The resolution reaffirmed [[Israel]]'s right to defend itself against terror. It also congratulated Israel on building a strong nation and wished for a successful Israeli future.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov/bill/110th-congress/senate-resolution/522?q=%7B%22search%22%3A%5B%22bernie+sanders%22%2C%22israel%22%2C%22israel%22%5D%7D |title=S.Res.522 - 110th Congress (2007-2008): A resolution recognizing the 60th anniversary of the founding of the modern State of Israel and reaffirming the bonds of close friendship and cooperation between the United States and Israel. |publisher=Congress.gov |date= April 22, 2008 |access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref>

According to Sanders' senate webpage, David Palumbo-Liu wrongly noted in ''[[Salon (website)|Salon]]'' that Sen. Sanders "voted" for a resolution supporting [[Operation Protective Edge]] which had actually passed without a vote.<ref>{{cite web|title = News July 24|url = http://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/newswatch/072414|website = Sen. Bernie Sanders|access-date = September 10, 2015|archive-date = December 3, 2020|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20201203041700/https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/newswatch/072414}}</ref> A statement published on his Senate website reads in part: "Sanders believes the Israeli attacks that killed hundreds of innocent people&nbsp;– including many women and children&nbsp;– in bombings of civilian neighborhoods and UN controlled schools, hospitals, and refugee camps were disproportionate, and the widespread killing of civilians is completely unacceptable. Israel's actions took an enormous human toll, and appeared to strengthen support for Hamas and may well be sowing the seeds for even more hatred, war and destruction in future years."<ref name="War and Peace"/>

''[[The Intercept]]''{{'}}s Zaid Jilani wrote that Sanders "stood out in contrast to the remarks from the other four major party candidates" in the 2016 presidential election, criticizing Israel's policy of settlement expansion after violent episodes and defended self-determination, civil rights, and economic well-being for Palestinians. After [[AIPAC]]'s refusal to accept Sanders's telepresence at their 2016 debate, former U.S. ambassador [[Marc Ginsberg]] explained the event saying that Bernie Sanders "has never really extolled his [[Jewishness]], much less any support for Israel".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theintercept.com/2016/03/22/bernie-sanders-spoke-up-for-suffering-palestinians-but-few-in-broadcast-media-covered-it/|title=Bernie Sanders Spoke Up for Suffering Palestinians, but Few in Broadcast Media Covered It|date=March 22, 2015|access-date=March 22, 2016|website=The Intercept|last=Jilani|first=Zaid}}</ref> Sanders was criticized for hiring [[IfNotNow (organization)|IfNotNow]] founder [[Simone Zimmerman]] as his Jewish Outreach Coordinator, and she was fired from the campaign after critical social media posts about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the conflict surfaced.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/US-Elections/Meet-the-outspoken-critic-of-Israel-who-is-Bernie-Sanders-new-Jewish-outreach-director-451056|title=Meet the outspoken critic of Israel who is Bernie Sanders' new Jewish outreach director|work=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|access-date=June 22, 2017 |issn=0792-822X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://forward.com/news/breaking-news/338724/sanders-campaign-suspends-controversial-jewish-outreach-coordinator/|title=Sanders Campaign Suspends Controversial Jewish Outreach Coordinator|work=The Forward|access-date=June 22, 2017}}</ref>

While being interviewed in April 2016 by the ''[[New York Daily News]]'', Sanders said that Israel killed over 10,000 innocent civilians in Gaza,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nydailynews.com/opinion/transcript-bernie-sanders-meets-news-editorial-board-article-1.2588306 | title=TRANSCRIPT: Bernie Sanders meets with the Daily News Editorial Board, April 1, 2016 | website=[[New York Daily News]] | date=April 4, 2016 | access-date=April 6, 2016}}</ref> an unnecessarily high death toll.<ref>[https://www.timesofisrael.com/bernie-sanders-accuses-netanyahu-of-overreacting-in-gaza-war/ Bernie Sanders accuses Netanyahu of overreacting in Gaza war] The Times of Israel, November 19, 2015</ref> The [[Anti-Defamation League]] subsequently called on Sanders to withdraw remarks he made about the casualties, which the ADL said exaggerated the death toll of the [[2014 Israel–Gaza conflict]], citing a number far in excess of Palestinian or Israel sources' estimates.<ref>[https://www.jpost.com/Diaspora/US-Jewish-group-slams-Bernie-Sanders-for-misstatements-on-2014-Gaza-war-450507 US Jewish group slams Bernie Sanders for misstatements on 2014 Gaza war] The Jerusalem Post, April 6, 2016</ref> Sanders later clarified that he was quickly corrected in that the death toll was closer to 2,000 civilians.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Politics-And-Diplomacy/Sanders-must-apologize-for-the-lie-that-he-spread-about-Israel-450706 |title=Sanders must apologize for the lie that he spread about Israel |work=The Jerusalem Post |date=March 6, 2016 |access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref>

In November 2017, Sanders was one of 10 Democratic senators to sign a letter urging [[Prime Minister of Israel]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] to halt the planned demolitions of Palestinian villages [[Khan al-Ahmar (village)|Khan al-Ahmar]] and [[Susya|Susiya]] on the grounds that such action would further diminish efforts to seek a two-state solution and "endanger Israel's future as a Jewish democracy."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/democratic-senators-urge-netanyahu-not-to-raze-palestinian-villages/|title=Democratic senators urge Netanyahu not to raze Palestinian villages|date=November 30, 2017|work=The Times of Israel}}</ref> In December 2017, Sanders opposed President Trump's decision to [[United States recognition of Jerusalem as capital of Israel|recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Who's Speaking Out Against Trump's Jerusalem Move |url=https://jstreet.org/experts-speak-trumps-jerusalem-move/ |work=J Street |date=December 12, 2017}}</ref>

In April 2018, shortly after the commencing of the [[2018 Gaza border protests]], Sanders stated, "From what my understanding is, you have tens and tens of thousands of people who are engaged in a nonviolent protest. I believe now 15 or 20 people, Palestinians, have been killed and many, many others have been wounded. So I think it's a difficult situation, but my assessment is that Israel overreacted on that." He furthered that Gaza remained "a humanitarian disaster" and called on the United States to play "a more positive role in ending the Gaza blockade and helping Palestinians and Israelis build a future that works for all."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/04/01/politics/bernie-sanders-gaza-protests-cnntv/index.html|title=Bernie Sanders: Israel 'overreacted' during Gaza protests|date=April 1, 2018|publisher=CNN}}</ref>

During an October 2018 speech, Sanders said it was "hard to imagine that Israel's Netanyahu government would have taken a number of steps— including passing the recent 'Nation State law,' which essentially codifies the second-class status of Israel's non-Jewish citizens, aggressively undermining the longstanding goal of a two-state solution, and ignoring the economic catastrophe in Gaza — if Netanyahu wasn't confident that Trump would support him."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2018-10-10/ty-article/.premium/bernie-sanders-cites-israels-nation-state-law-in-slamming-trump/0000017f-e5cd-d62c-a1ff-fdffad760000|title=Bernie Sanders Cites Israel's Nation-state Law in Slamming Trump for Inspiring Authoritarianism|date=October 10, 2018|work=Haaretz}}</ref>

In March 2019, after Representative [[Ilhan Omar]] received criticism from Democrats and Republicans over comments about Israel that were deemed as anti-Semitic, Sanders condemned antisemitism as "a hateful and dangerous ideology which must be vigorously opposed in the United States and around the world" while noting that they should not "equate anti-Semitism with legitimate criticism of the right-wing, Netanyahu government in Israel." Sanders called for the formation of "an even-handed Middle East policy which brings Israelis and Palestinians together for a lasting peace" and voiced his concern that Omar was being targeted "as a way of stifling that debate."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/432926-sanders-on-omar-cant-equate-anti-semitism-with-legitimate-criticism-of/|title=Sanders defends Omar: Can't equate anti-Semitism with 'legitimate criticism' of Israel|first=Tal|last=Axelrod|newspaper=The Hill|date=March 6, 2019}}</ref>

In a July 2019 interview, Sanders stated that he believed "that the people of Israel absolutely have the right to live in peace, independence and security" but that the Netanyahu government was extremely right-wing "with many racist tendencies" and that the role of the United States was "to try to finally bring peace to the Middle East and to treat the Palestinian people with the kind of respect and dignity they deserve." Sanders reflected on the trillions of dollars spent on the War on Terror and asserted that as U.S. president he would favor sitting down "in a room with the leadership of Saudi Arabia, with the leadership of Iran, with the leadership of the Palestinians, with the leadership of Israel, and hammer out some damn agreements, which will try to end the conflicts that exist there forever."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jpost.com/American-Politics/Sanders-would-absolutely-consider-using-foreign-aid-as-leverage-on-Israel-596960|title=Bernie Sanders Would Use Foreign Aid As Leverage on Israel|date=July 28, 2019|work=The Jerusalem Post}}</ref>

During the 2020 presidential campaign, Sanders stated he would impose human rights conditions on aid to Israel, a statement his then-rival [[Joe Biden]] called "bizarre".<ref name="Harb 2023">{{cite web | last=Harb | first=Ali | title=Bernie Sanders's failure to back Israel-Gaza ceasefire upsets US followers | website=Al Jazeera | date=October 30, 2023 | url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/10/30/bernie-sanderss-failure-to-back-gaza-ceasefire-disappoints-us-supporters | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref>

==== Gaza war ====

During the [[Gaza war]], after Biden-appointed Secretary of State [[Antony Blinken]] had done so, Sanders called for a "humanitarian pause" to the conflict to allow aid to reach Gazan civilians, thoroughly condemning the bombings of civilian targets by the IDF and Netanyahu's anti-democratic policies and calling Hamas an "authoritarian nightmare, repressing dissent and stealing from Gazans not just the basic materials of life they need, but the dream of a better future." He continued to insist on a [[two-state solution]].<ref name="The Guardian Gaza opinion 2023">{{cite web | last=Sanders | first=Bernie | title=Gaza needs a humanitarian pause. Then we need a vision of where we go from here | website=the Guardian | date=November 1, 2023 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2023/nov/01/gaza-humanitarian-pause-bernie-sanders | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Pilkington 2023">{{cite web | last=Pilkington | first=Ed | title=Bernie Sanders calls for end to Israeli strikes and killing of thousands | website=the Guardian | date=November 5, 2023 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/05/bernie-sanders-israeli-hamas-war | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> However, he was criticized by over 400 former staffers<ref name="Medium 2023">{{cite web | author=@formerberniestaff|title=Open Letter: Over 400 Former Bernie Sanders Staffers Urge Senator to Introduce 'Ceasefire Now' Senate Resolution | website=Medium | date=November 8, 2023 | url=https://medium.com/@formerberniestaff/open-letter-to-senator-bernie-sanders-9d1c10d99e99 | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Grim Thakker 2023">{{cite web | last1=Grim | first1=Ryan | last2=Thakker | first2=Prem | title=Nearly 300 Bernie Sanders Alumni Call On Senator to Back a Ceasefire in Gaza | website=The Intercept | date=October 24, 2023 | url=https://theintercept.com/2023/10/24/bernie-sanders-ceasefire-letter-israel/ | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> and over 300 presidential campaign delegates,<ref name="Lacy Thakker 2023">{{cite web | last1=Lacy | first1=Akela | last2=Thakker | first2=Prem | title=More Than 300 DNC Delegates for Bernie Sanders Push Senator to Call for Ceasefire in Gaza | website=The Intercept | date=November 15, 2023 | url=https://theintercept.com/2023/11/15/bernie-sanders-delegates-gaza-ceasefire-letter/ | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> as well as numerous Jewish and Palestinian American supporters,<ref name="Harb 2023"/> for not endorsing a full ceasefire to end the war.<ref name="Gambino 2023">{{cite web | last=Gambino | first=Lauren | title=Left revolts over Biden's staunch support of Israel amid Gaza crisis | website=the Guardian | date=October 28, 2023 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/oct/28/democrats-biden-reelection-israel-palestine | access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> Sanders later called for a ceasefire in August 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sen. Bernie Sanders calls for a Gaza ceasefire|date=August 21, 2024 |url=https://www.vpm.org/npr-news/npr-news/2024-08-20/sen-bernie-sanders-calls-for-a-gaza-ceasefire}}</ref>

On July 25, 2025, speaking about the [[Gaza humanitarian crisis (2023–present)|humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip]], Sanders said in a statement: "Having already killed or wounded 200,000 Palestinians, mostly women and children, the extremist Israeli government is using mass starvation to engineer the ethnic cleansing of Gaza." He accused Israel of carrying out an "extermination" campaign in Gaza.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harb |first1=Ali |title='Horrors upon horrors': How US Congress responded to mass hunger in Gaza |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/7/26/horrors-upon-horrors-how-us-congress-responded-to-mass-hunger-in-gaza |work=Al Jazeera English |date=July 26, 2025}}</ref> In July 2025, Sanders called for an end to all [[Israel–United States military relations|US military aid to Israel]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Democrats join global outcry over humanitarian crisis in Gaza |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/07/26/gaza-crisis-united-states-response-00478153 |work=Politico |date=July 26, 2025}}</ref>

In November 2024, April 2025, July 2025, and April 2026 Sanders forced votes in the U.S. senate to end military aid to Israel. All four attempts failed, though the third attempt received a majority of support from the [[Senate Democratic Caucus|Democratic caucus]], and the fourth received 85 percent of support from the caucus.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Salam |first1=Erum |title=US Senate rejects Bernie Sanders effort to block arms sales to Israel|work=The Guardian |date=November 21, 2024 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2024/nov/20/bernie-sanders-israel-gaza-resolution}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=US Senate rejects effort to block arms sales to Israel|work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us-senate-rejects-effort-block-arms-sales-israel-2025-04-03/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Senate votes down Israel arms sales ban, despite growing Democrat support|website=[[Politico]] |date=July 31, 2025 |url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2025/07/30/congress/sanders-israel-arms-sale-ban-vote-00484866}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bernie Sanders' effort to block US weapons sales to Israel fails in Senate|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/15/bernie-sanders-pushes-military-block-israel}}</ref>

In September 2025, Sanders became the first U.S. senator to affirm that Israel is [[Gaza genocide|committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gedeon |first1=Joseph |title=Bernie Sanders becomes first US senator to say Israel committing genocide in Gaza|work=The Guardian |date=September 17, 2025 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/sep/17/bernie-sanders-israel-gaza-genocide}}</ref>

During an October 2025 interview with [[Axios (website)|Axios]], when asked if he considers himself a [[Zionist]], Sanders stated, "No. Not within the terms of what Zionism means."<ref>{{cite web|title=Sen. Sanders on AOC, AIPAC and the AI revolution - The Axios Show, Ep. 4| website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?V=vhCParR8DUU&t=903s}}</ref>

====BDS and defense of Israeli right to exist====
Bernie Sanders supports a [[two-state solution]] to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, opposes attempts at a [[one-state solution]], opposes the [[Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions|Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions]] movement against Israel (BDS), and maintains that the [[United Nations]] has a bias against Israel.<ref name=JTABDS>{{cite news|url=https://www.jta.org/2017/05/04/news-opinion/politics/bernie-sanders-just-defended-israel-on-al-jazeera-heres-why-thats-a-big-deal|title=Bernie Sanders just defended Israel on Al Jazeera. Here's why that's a big deal. |date=May 4, 2017|last=Kampeas|first=Ron|publisher=Jewish Telegraphic Agency}}</ref><ref name=FrwdBDS>{{cite news |url= https://forward.com/fast-forward/370906/bernie-sanders-says-bds-wont-solve-mideast-impasse/ |title=Bernie Sanders Says BDS Won't Solve Mideast Impasse |agency= Forward |date=May 4, 2017 |last=Zeveloff|first=Naomi}}</ref> He has also maintained that [[anti-Semitism]] plays a role in the BDS movement.<ref name=2016BDS>{{cite news |url= https://www.jta.org/2016/03/22/news-opinion/politics/bernie-sanders-says-anti-semitism-is-a-factor-in-bds|title=Bernie Sanders says anti-Semitism is a factor in BDS |publisher=Jewish Telegraphic Agency|date=April 22, 2016}}</ref>

Following Sanders' signing of a US congressional letter denouncing a bias at the UN against Israel and calling upon UN Secretary-General António Guterres, urging him to remedy the problem, he defended his signature on an interview hosted by the Qatari news agency [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]], saying:<ref name=JTABDS/>

<blockquote> there are many problems with Israel ... On the other hand, to see Israel attacked over and over again for human rights violations — which may be true — when you have countries like Saudi Arabia or Syria, Saudi Arabia – I'm not quite sure if a woman can even drive a car today. So, I think the thrust of that letter is not to say that Israel does not have human rights issues — it does — but to say how come it's only Israel when you have other countries where women are treated as third-class citizens, where in Egypt, I don't know how many thousands of people now lingering in jail, so that's the point of that, not to defend Israel, but to say why only Israel." </blockquote>

Asked if he "respected" BDS as a protest tactic, Sanders has said "No, I don't", adding that it was counter-productive if the goal is trying to bring about peace talks.<ref name=JTABDS/> In 2016, Sanders averred that there was "absolutely" anti-Semitism in the BDS movement, elaborating:<ref name=2016BDS/>

<blockquote>Israel has done some very bad things, so has every other country on earth," Sanders said. "I think the people who want to attack Israel for their policies, I think that is fair game. But not to appreciate that there is some level of anti-Semitism around the world involved in that I think would be a mistake ... I spent many months on a [[kibbutz]] in Israel, so I know something about Israel. Israel has got to be defended, has a [[right to exist]], but you cannot ignore the needs of the Palestinian people.</blockquote>

Sanders supports a [[two-state solution]], and regarding the possibility of a one-state solution, he has stated:<ref name=JTABDS/>

<blockquote>I think if that happens, then that would be the end of the State of Israel and I support [[Israel's right to exist]] ... I think if there is the political will to make [peace and a two-state solution] happen and if there is good faith on both sides I do think it's possible, and I think there has not been good faith, certainly in this Israeli government and I have my doubts about parts of the Palestinian leadership as well.</blockquote>

In a December 2018 letter to Senate Majority Leader [[Mitch McConnell]] and Minority Leader [[Chuck Schumer]], Sanders and [[Dianne Feinstein]] advocated against a provision of a spending package barring companies from endorsing anti-Israel boycotts promoted by governmental groups, writing that while they did not support "the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, we remain resolved to our constitutional oath to defend the right of every American to express their views peacefully without fear of or actual punishment by the government."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/policy/international/middle-east-north-africa/422134-sens-sanders-and-feinstein-oppose-israel-anti/|title=Sens. Sanders and Feinstein oppose Israel anti-boycott provision|date=December 19, 2018|newspaper=The Hill}}</ref> In February 2019, Sanders voted against a controversial [[Israel Anti-Boycott Act|Anti-Boycott Act]] initiated by Republicans,<ref>{{cite news |title=Why These Democratic Presidential Hopefuls Voted No on an anti-BDS Bill |url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/why-these-democratic-presidential-hopefuls-voted-no-on-an-anti-bds-bill-1.6919089 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190211185702/https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/why-these-democratic-presidential-hopefuls-voted-no-on-an-anti-bds-bill-1.6919089 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 11, 2019 |work=[[Haaretz]] |date=February 11, 2019}}</ref> which would make it illegal for U.S. companies to engage in boycotts against Israel and [[Israeli settlement]]s in the occupied [[Israeli-occupied territories|Palestinian territories]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Don't Punish US Companies That Help End Abuses in the West Bank |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2018/12/18/dont-punish-us-companies-help-end-abuses-west-bank |publisher=Human Rights Watch |date=December 18, 2018}}</ref>

On December 14, 2023, Sanders introduced a privileged resolution invoking Section 502(b) of the [[Foreign Assistance Act]], calling on the State Department to investigate Israeli crimes against humanity in its conduct of the war in Gaza, effectively forcing a Senate vote on withholding military aid to Israel.<ref name="Sanders Gaza resolution 2023">{{cite web | title=NEWS: Sanders Introduces Resolution to Investigate Israel's Indiscriminate Bombing Campaign in Gaza » Senator Bernie Sanders | website=Senator Bernie Sanders | date=December 15, 2023 | url=https://www.sanders.senate.gov/press-releases/news-sanders-introduces-resolution-to-investigate-israels-indiscriminate-bombing-campaign-in-gaza/ | access-date=December 19, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Adragna 2023">{{cite web | last=Adragna|first=Anthony|title=Sanders' new Israel push | website=POLITICO | date=December 14, 2023 | url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2023/12/14/congress/sanders-new-israel-push-00131794 | access-date=December 19, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Chappell El-Tayyab 2023">{{cite web | last1=Chappell | first1=John Ramming | last2=El-Tayyab | first2=Hassan | title=Senator Sanders' New Resolution Could Force U.S. to Confront Any Complicity in Civilian Harm in Gaza | website=Just Security | date=December 18, 2023 | url=https://www.justsecurity.org/90716/senator-sanders-new-resolution-could-force-u-s-to-confront-any-complicity-in-civilian-harm-in-gaza/ | access-date=December 19, 2023}}</ref> Sanders said that "This resolution is not prescriptive — it does not alter aid to Israel in any way. It simply requests that the State Department report on how our aid is being used." The resolution would freeze [[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war|U.S. military aid to Israel]] unless the State Department issues a report within 30 days.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sanders to force vote on potentially freezing military aid to Israel |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/4411339-sanders-freezing-military-aid-israel-vote/ |work=The Hill |date=January 16, 2024}}</ref> The resolution failed in the Senate on January 16, 2024,<ref name="Al Jazeera 2024-01-17">{{cite web | title=US Senate rejects Bernie Sanders' push to tie Israeli aid to human rights | website=Al Jazeera | date=January 17, 2024 | url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/1/17/us-senate-overwhelmingly-rejects-measure-to-force-rights-report-on-israel | access-date=February 6, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Magid Berman 2024">{{cite web | last1=Magid | first1=Jacob | last2=Berman | first2=Lazar| title=US Senate rejects Bernie Sanders' bid to condition aid to Israel on human rights record | website=The Times of Israel | date=January 17, 2024 | url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/senate-rejects-bernie-sanders-bid-to-condition-aid-to-israel-on-human-rights-record/ | access-date=February 6, 2024}}</ref> with only eleven Senators voting for it.<ref>{{cite news |title=Senate Kills Measure to Scrutinize Israeli Human Rights Record as Condition for Aid |url=https://theintercept.com/2024/01/16/senate-israel-human-rights-condition-aid/ |work=The Intercept |date=January 16, 2024}}</ref> Sanders then announced on February 2 that he would introduce a cut of $10.1 billion in Israel-bound military aid to the $118 billion national security and immigration package the Senate was then debating.<ref name="Sanders tweet 2024-02-02">{{cite web |last=Sanders|first=Bernie| title=The U.S. must end its complicity in the nightmare unfolding in Gaza. That is why I will be offering an amendment to the supplemental bill to ensure zero funding for the continuation of Netanyahu's illegal, immoral war against the Palestinian people.|date=February 2, 2024
| website=X (formerly Twitter) | url=https://twitter.com/SenSanders/status/1753519126344032734 | access-date=February 5, 2024}}</ref> The aid package passed the Senate, and later the House, without his cut.<ref name="Harris 2024">{{cite web | last=Harris | first=Bryant | title=Senate passes Ukraine, Israel, Taiwan aid amid Trump-fueled opposition | website=Defense News | date=February 13, 2024 | url=https://www.defensenews.com/congress/2024/02/13/senate-passes-ukraine-israel-taiwan-aid-amid-trump-fueled-opposition/ | access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Insinna 2024">{{cite web | last=Insinna | first=Valerie | title=Congress passes $825 billion defense spending bill amid political battles, government shutdown threat | website=Breaking Defense | date=March 23, 2024 | url=https://breakingdefense.com/2024/03/congress-passes-825-million-defense-spending-bill-amid-political-battles-government-shutdown-threat/ | access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref>

===Henry Kissinger===
During a 2016 Democratic debate, Sanders took issue with Hillary Clinton's admiration of former Secretary of State [[Henry Kissinger]], describing him as "one of the most destructive" in US modern history, stating:

{{blockquote|I am proud to say that Henry Kissinger is not my friend. I will not take advice from Henry Kissinger. In fact, Kissinger's actions in [[Cambodia]], when the United States [[Cambodian Campaign|bombed]] that country, overthrew Prince [[Norodom Sihanouk|Sihanouk]], created the instability for [[Pol Pot]] and the [[Khmer Rouge]] to come in who then [[Cambodian genocide|butchered]] some 3 million innocent people – one of the worst genocides in the history of the world.<ref>[[Greg Grandin]] (February 12, 2016). [http://www.salon.com/2016/02/12/henry_kissingers_mad_and_illegal_bombing_what_you_need_to_know_about_his_real_history_and_why_the_sandersclinton_exchange_matters/ Henry Kissinger's "mad and illegal" bombing: What you need to know about his real history — and why the Sanders/Clinton exchange matters]. ''Salon''. Retrieved February 12, 2016.</ref>}}

===Nicaraguan Revolution===
During the [[Nicaraguan Revolution]], Sanders opposed funding the [[Contras|Contra Rebels]] and praised the leadership and popularity of the [[Sandinista National Liberation Front|Sandinista]] Party. Sanders stated that the support for the Sandinistas in their country was higher than the support of American voters for President [[Ronald Reagan]] and even those who did not vote for the Sandinistas did not want an invasion.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://feelthebern.org/bernie-sanders-on-latin-america/ | title=Bernie Sanders on Latin America | publisher=2016 feelthebern.org}}</ref>

===Venezuela===
In August 2011, Sanders's official Senate webpage re-printed in full an editorial from the West Lebanon, New Hampshire ''Valley News'' stating: "These days, the American dream is more apt to be realized in South America, in places such as Ecuador, Venezuela and Argentina, where incomes are actually more equal today than they are in the land of [[Horatio Alger]]. Who's the [[banana republic]] now?"<ref>West Valley Editorial Board. [https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/must-read/close-the-gaps-disparities-that-threaten-america Close The Gaps: Disparities That Threaten America] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200509064634/https://www.sanders.senate.gov/newsroom/must-read/close-the-gaps-disparities-that-threaten-america |date=May 9, 2020 }}, sanders.senate.gov. Retrieved January 27, 2020</ref>

Since the deterioration of Venezuelan living standards under the direction of the country's self-described socialist government, concerns and comparisons to Venezuela were raised over Sanders' desires to implement socialist policies in the United States.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vicens|first1=AJ|title=Former President of Mexico Compares Bernie Sanders to Hugo Chávez|url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2016/04/former-president-mexico-vicente-fox-bernie-sanders-hugo-chavez|access-date=June 1, 2016|work=[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]]|date=April 22, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Cardenas|first1=Jose|title=In Venezuela, Socialism Is Killing Venezuelans|url=http://www.nationalreview.com/article/435522/socialism-venezuela-hugo-chavez-nicolas-maduro-bernie-sanders-millennials|access-date=June 1, 2016|work=[[National Review]]|date=May 18, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Powell|first1=Thomas|title=Testing easy assumptions against facts reveals uncomfortable truths.|work=[[National Review]]|date=May 31, 2016}}</ref> In 2016, Sanders responded by attempting to distance himself from Venezuela's Bolivarian government, replying to such worries by stating, "When I talk about [[democratic socialism]], I'm not looking at Venezuela. I'm not looking at Cuba. I'm looking at countries like Denmark and Sweden".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sakuma|first1=Amanda|title=Cuban, Venezuelan immigrants wrestle with Bernie Sanders' brand of socialism|url=https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/cuban-venezuelan-immigrants-wrestle-bernie-sanders-brand-socialism|access-date=June 1, 2016|publisher=[[MSNBC]]|date=March 14, 2016}}</ref> Danish Prime Minister [[Lars Løkke Rasmussen]] has contested Sanders's portrayal of the nation, saying Denmark is not socialist but rather has a [[capitalist market economy]].<ref name=Yglesias2015>Matthew Yglesias. [https://www.vox.com/2015/10/31/9650030/denmark-prime-minister-bernie-sanders Denmark's prime minister says Bernie Sanders is wrong to call his country socialist], Vox.com, October 31, 2015. Retrieved January 27, 2020</ref>

Sanders also furthered himself from the Venezuelan government by calling the leader of Venezuela's [[Bolivarian Revolution]], former President [[Hugo Chávez]], a "dead [[communist]] dictator".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Gupta|first1=Girish|last2=Pons|first2=Corina|title=Venezuela's Maduro rooting for 'revolutionary friend' Sanders in U.S. campaign|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-usa-idUSKCN0YN32Q|access-date=June 1, 2016|work=[[Reuters]]|date=June 1, 2016}}</ref>

During the [[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]], Sanders cautioned about President Donald Trump's decision to back a competing claim for the government in Venezuela, citing US support of coups in [[1973 Chilean coup d'état|Chile]], [[1954 Guatemalan coup d'état|Guatemala]], and [[1964 Brazilian coup d'état|Brazil]]. At the same time, Sanders condemned the actions of the [[Nicolás Maduro]] government.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inquisitr.com/5265471/sanders-venezuela-us-trump/|title=Bernie Sanders: 'We Must Learn The Lessons Of The Past And Not Be In The Business Of Regime Change'|last=Mujezinovic|first=Damir|date=January 25, 2019|website=The Inquisitr|access-date=January 25, 2019}}</ref>

In a February 2019 CNN town hall, when asked by [[Wolf Blitzer]] why he would not describe Maduro as a "dictator", Sanders admitted that it was "fair to say" Venezuela's last presidential election "was undemocratic" while noting other "democratic operations taking place in that country" and stated his support for "internationally supervised free elections."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/25/politics/bernie-sanders-venezuela-maduro/index.html|title=Sanders warns against outside intervention in Venezuela, stops short of calling Maduro a 'dictator'|date=February 25, 2019|publisher=CNN}}</ref>

In an April 2019 interview, Sanders stated that Maduro was heading a "failed regime" while also expressing his opposition to military intervention, furthering that the world community needed to "be mindful of the humanitarian suffering and the hunger that's going on in Venezuela right now" and that what one would want is "free and fair elections, and we want to do everything we can to establish democracy there." Sanders noted that all recent evidence had pointed to Maduro's reelection being under fraudulent circumstances and cited the need for establishing a [[democracy in Venezuela]] without "deciding that some politician is the new President, who never won any election."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/bernie-sanders-opposes-us-military-intervention-venezuela-2019-4|title=Bernie Sanders slams Nicolas Maduro as a failure, but won't support a US military intervention in Venezuela|date=April 15, 2019|first=John|last=Haltiwanger|work=Business Insider}}</ref>

===Clinton Foundation===
When asked by [[CNN]]'s [[Jake Tapper]] in June 2016 if it was fair to criticize the [[Clinton Foundation]], an American charity, for taking money from foreign governments which do not represent American values, Sanders responded, "Yes it is. It is. If you ask me about the Clinton Foundation, do I have a problem when a sitting secretary of state and a foundation run by her husband collects many millions of dollars from foreign governments, governments which are dictatorships -- you don't have a lot of civil liberties or democratic rights in Saudi Arabia. You don't have a lot of respect there for opposition points of view for gay rights, for women's rights. Yes, do I have a problem with that? Yes, I do."<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/06/us/politics/bernie-sanders-hillary-clinton-california-primary.html Bernie Sanders Vows Fight to Convention as Hillary Clinton Wins a Primary]; ''[[The New York Times]]''; Yamiche Alcindorjune; June 5, 2016</ref><ref>[http://www.cnn.com/TRANSCRIPTS/1606/05/sotu.01.html State of the Union Transcript]; [[CNN]]; June 5, 2016</ref> In September 2016, Sanders told [[NBC]]'s [[Chuck Todd]] that if Clinton becomes president of the United States, she should cease all contact with the Foundation, but stopped short of agreeing it should be closed, noting, "I don't know enough. They do a lot of good things with A.I.D.S. and so forth.
